qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the See Someone, Save Someone Act, requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to develop or identify and implement a human trafficking identification and reporting training program for certain transportation employees and contractors. The bill requires employers to certify employee training completion annually starting January 1, 2027, train new hires within 90 days, create reporting procedures and prevention policies, grants civil and criminal immunity for good-faith reporting, and requires public service announcements in English and Spanish at specified transit facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: State and contract transportation employees working at transit stations, airports, port facilities, and highway rest stops, transit service providers and employers, and potential victims of human trafficking.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by $262,500 in FY 2026 and $137,500 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Transit Administration to develop an online training module ($125,000) and to cover estimated overtime costs for approximately 2,500 employees to complete the training during work hours. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing or identifying the human trafficking awareness training program, administering it across affected transportation divisions, collecting employer certifications, and requiring public service announcements at transit facilities.

As the MDOT modal administration operating public transit services and stations, MTA employs the majority of the staff subject to the training mandate and is anticipated by the fiscal note to develop the online training course at an estimated cost of $125,000.
SHA oversees state highways and rest stops; its employees and contract staff working at highway rest stops are subject to the training requirements and safety announcements mandated by the bill.
MAA operates state airport facilities (such as BWI), where employees must receive human trafficking identification training and where bilingual safety announcements must be broadcast or displayed.
MPA operates state port facilities whose staff and contractors are subject to the bill's training requirements and where public service announcements must be implemented.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program; the bill requires employers to establish reporting procedures that connect suspected trafficking incidents to these designated regional navigators.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 3 clarifies the definition of 'physical therapist assistant', increases the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9 members by adding a second licensed physical therapist assistant, and requires license renewal notices to be sent electronically by default rather than by first-class mail.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapist assistants, and members of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, board special fund expenditures increase by $1,500 annually for compensation for the additional board member, but decrease by an estimated $5,000 annually from switching default renewal notices to electronic delivery, resulting in net annual special fund savings of up to $3,500. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill alters board composition, modifies definitions, and updates electronic notification procedures affecting the board's operations and special fund expenditures.
The bill expands the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9 members, requiring the Governor to appoint an additional licensed physical therapist assistant member.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will handle the additional physical therapist assistant seat created by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Defines an unreasonable land use restriction on solar collector systems as one that increases installation costs by at least 5% or reduces projected energy generation by at least 10% compared to the initially proposed installation. The bill requires property owners to submit supporting documentation from a certified or experienced solar panel design specialist and clarifies the authority of community associations to regulate, restrict, or install solar systems in common areas or elements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, community associations (homeowners associations and condominiums), and solar energy designers and installers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially impact State or local government operations or finances, and has a minimal effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) advises on state energy policy and promotes the adoption of renewable energy technologies, including residential solar. MEA is also cited as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy analysis.

The Maryland Department of Planning oversees the Maryland Historical Trust, whose director is statutorily responsible under Section 2-119(d) for determining whether a historic property is listed in or eligible for the Maryland Register of Historic Properties, thereby exempting it from these solar collector restrictions.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative support to the state judiciary, which handles civil litigation and disputes between property owners and community associations regarding real property restrictions and solar easements; the agency was consulted as an information source in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 9 updates the duties and definitions pertaining to the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council. It establishes definitions for 'healthy food priority areas' and 'wasted food,' incorporates local food production and procurement goals into ongoing resiliency policy recommendations, eliminates outdated one-time reporting requirements, and mandates the inclusion of policy and legislative change recommendations in the Council's annual report.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council (within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing food insecurity or living in healthy food priority areas, local food businesses and agricultural producers, and local food council organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in the Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), and MDEM staffs the council and implements the bill's reporting and operational updates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory definitions, specific policy goals, and ongoing annual reporting requirements of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

The Maryland State Department of Education is specifically mentioned in the bill's statutory provisions as the recipient of the Council's recommendations regarding student nutrition and the federal Community Eligibility Provision.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permanently extends and expands requirements for health insurance carriers regarding member access to out-of-network specialists and nonphysician specialists. It requires carriers to provide referrals and additional assistance to arrange coverage for mental health and substance use disorder services at in-network cost-sharing levels for the duration of a treatment plan when network access standards are not met, and prohibits carriers from imposing utilization review requirements beyond those applied to in-network providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance policyholders and members seeking specialized care (particularly mental health and substance use disorder services), commercial health insurance carriers, and nonparticipating healthcare specialists and behavioral health providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) increase minimally in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees. MIA can handle any additional regulatory workload using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, and no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs affected by this bill. MIA will oversee compliance with the revised referral and utilization review procedures, review rate and form filings, and collect associated filing fees.

The bill regulates coverage and referral access for mental health and substance use disorder services and references behavioral health programs licensed by MDH under § 7.5-401 of the Health - General Article.
DBM oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; the fiscal note evaluated the program's operations and determined there is no fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale or distribution of products containing tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) that violate potency, packaging, or labeling requirements, or that are advertised as containing THC exceeding statutory thresholds. It authorizes the Field Enforcement Division of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) to issue citations for underage sales and other THC-related offenses, allows the ATCC Executive Director to seize and confiscate illicit THC products, establishes that displaying or offering THC for sale without a license is prima facie evidence of selling it, and sets misdemeanor fines up to $5,000 for unlicensed violators while subjecting licensees to administrative disciplinary action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) and Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cannabis businesses, unlicensed retailers and distributors of THC and hemp products, consumers, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may experience a minimal increase beginning in FY 2026 from penalties and citations heard in District Court. ATCC, MCA, and the District Court can implement the bill and handle any associated caseload with existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) by subjecting licensed cannabis entities that violate THC packaging, labeling, potency, or advertising restrictions to disciplinary action by the Administration pursuant to § 36-202. The bill also relies on potency and product standards promulgated and overseen by MCA.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense punishable by a fine up to $5,000, authorizes law enforcement to charge certain violations via citation, and establishes evidentiary rules regarding prima facie evidence of unlicensed THC sales in prosecutions handled by the District Court.
The bill specifically references cooperative arrangements between the Field Enforcement Division and the Office of the Comptroller regarding enforcement of cannabis and tax provisions.
State and local law enforcement officers collaborate with the Field Enforcement Division on peace officer duties, criminal enforcement, and the issuance of citations for prohibited THC sales.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office was consulted regarding potential impacts on criminal charging and defense caseloads resulting from the new misdemeanor THC citations and penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Association Act, authorizing the creation, operation, governance, conversion, and dissolution of limited worker cooperative associations (LWCAs) and collective worker cooperatives as limited liability companies under Maryland law.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Workers, small business owners, entrepreneurs seeking cooperative business structures, and commercial insurers providing workers' compensation.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $278,400 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming costs at the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). State revenues may see a minimal increase from business document filing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article and Corporations and Associations Article to specifically mandate that the Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforce statutory provisions regarding how insurers calculate workers' compensation insurance premiums for covered employee members of limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill amends multiple sections of the Tax - General Article governing admissions and amusement tax, motor fuel tax, income tax withholding, and sales and use tax to extend personal liability for unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties to individuals with direct fiscal control over limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill explicitly exempts membership interests and equity instruments of limited worker cooperative associations from the registration and broker-dealer requirements of the Maryland Securities Act (Title 11), which is administered and enforced by the Securities Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill establishes legal and judicial standards for limited worker cooperative associations, including provisions for judicial dissolution and service of process, and the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the bill's fiscal and policy analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the noise abatement monitoring system pilot programs in Montgomery County and Prince George's County by two years, setting a new termination date of June 30, 2028, and moving the program reporting deadline to December 1, 2027. It also applies public records inspection restrictions to recorded images from noise abatement systems, requiring record custodians to deny public inspection of the images except to cited individuals, their attorneys, or authorized agency employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County and Prince George's County governing bodies, alongside the District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists and residents in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, local law enforcement agencies, and county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally in FY 2027 and FY 2028 from contested citations collected in District Court, which can absorb the caseload within existing resources. Local revenues and expenditures for Montgomery and Prince George's counties will increase in FY 2027 and FY 2028 if the pilot programs are continued. Montgomery County previously estimated annual expenditures of $99,400, while fine revenues (capped at $75 per violation) are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the noise abatement monitoring pilot program through June 30, 2028. Contested citations are heard in the District Court, and the District Court is responsible for prescribing a uniform citation form and collecting fine revenues from contested citations.
The bill extends the pilot reporting deadline to December 1, 2027, requiring participating counties to submit comprehensive operational and fiscal evaluation reports directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Building Opportunities for Nurses Act of 2025 extends the State Board of Nursing and the Secretary of Health's authority over its infrastructure operations through July 1, 2030, allowing board special funds to cover infrastructure costs. It expands the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff to include for-profit employment in workforce shortage areas, modifies education and endorsement pathways for registered nurses, delays the implementation dates for certified nursing assistant tier credentials to 2026, and extends several healthcare preceptor income tax credit programs through 2030 while reducing required rotation training hours from 100 to 90.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, certified nursing assistants, healthcare preceptors, nursing students, and healthcare facilities located in designated workforce shortage areas.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by approximately $440,000 in FY 2025 as the Board of Nursing resumes paying for infrastructure operations from its special fund. General fund revenues decrease by up to $100,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2030 due to the extension of the physician preceptorship tax credit. General fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030 to fund the nurse preceptorship tax credit. Special fund revenues and expenditures for preceptorship funds increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2026 and up to $300,000 annually thereafter through FY 2030. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the sunset termination date for the State Board of Nursing (housed within MDH) to 2030, continues the Secretary of Health's authority over the Board's infrastructure operations, expands MDH's Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MLARP) for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff, and extends preceptorship tax credit programs administered by MDH.

The bill extends several income tax credits for preceptors (nurse practitioners, physicians, physician assistants, LPNs, and RNs) through tax year 2029, which the Comptroller must administer and which will impact State general fund revenues.

The bill maintains the requirement under Health Occupations § 8–6A–14 that the State Board of Nursing, in conjunction with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, approve nursing assistant training programs and develop regulations for those programs.

Under the Tax - General provisions amended and extended by the bill (§ 10–739 and § 10–739.1), the Department of Health must consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to identify geographic areas in Maryland with health care workforce shortages for preceptorship tax credit eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to conduct an annual study examining data on the location and county of residence of individuals before and after incarceration in a State correctional facility, and to submit an annual report to specified legislative committees beginning October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, individuals released from State correctional facilities, and local county communities receiving returning citizens.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not impacted as the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can conduct the study and prepare the annual reports using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) conduct an annual study tracking the location of individuals before and following incarceration in State correctional facilities and submit annual reports to specified legislative committees beginning October 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment to permit and regulate the planned placement of treated reclaimed water into surface water reservoirs used as drinking water sources, while extending the termination date of the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program to June 30, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments operating public water systems, drinking water utilities, and Maryland residents receiving public drinking water.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $97,300 in FY 2026, $85,800 in FY 2027, and $89,500 in FY 2028 for contractual staff to establish the program and develop regulations before terminating at the end of FY 2028. Special fund revenues increase by an estimated $75,000 in FY 2030 from a permit application fee. Local expenditures increase for participating local governments (such as the City of Westminster) to pay the application fee and fulfill water treatment and permitting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program within MDE, requiring the department to adopt regulations, review applications, issue and enforce permits, collect fees, manage a dedicated special fund, and report periodically to the General Assembly and the Governor.
MDE is required to submit implementation reports on the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program and the Reservoir Augmentation Program to the Governor on specified recurring statutory schedules.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill replaces the statutory commission rate schedules for trustees with a standard of compensation that is reasonable under the circumstances when the trust agreement does not specify compensation. It sets forth factors for courts to consider when assessing reasonableness, requires regular trustee compensation to be split equally between trust income and trust principal, and maintains the existing statutory commission rate structure for guardians of property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts) and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Trustees, trust beneficiaries, guardians of the property of minors or disabled persons, financial institutions, and estate and trust attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund income tax revenues may be impacted if trust income or principal shifts to personal or business income of trustees via increased compensation, but the impact cannot be reliably estimated and is likely to be limited. State expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the state court system, providing criteria and procedures for circuit courts to review, increase, decrease, or determine the reasonableness of compensation and allowances for guardians of property and trustees.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and probate matters in Maryland and was consulted as an information source regarding modifications to statutory commissions and compensation under the Estates and Trusts Article.

The Comptroller may be affected fiscally to the extent that shifting trust income or principal into trustees' personal or taxable business income alters state income tax collections, as identified in the fiscal note.
The Department of Labor houses the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, the statutory regulatory repository where qualifying institutional trustees and attorneys file schedules of rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes 'right to repair' requirements for powered wheelchairs, requiring manufacturers to provide documentation, parts, embedded software, firmware, and tools on fair and reasonable terms to independent repair providers and wheelchair owners for specified components. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Powered wheelchair owners and individuals with physical disabilities, independent wheelchair repair providers, authorized repair providers, and wheelchair manufacturers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially impacted. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle enforcement and implementation with existing resources, and the bill's application of existing civil and criminal penalty provisions is not expected to have a material financial effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes a violation of the powered wheelchair right-to-repair requirements an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill directly impacts the maintenance and repair of assistive technology (powered wheelchairs) used by individuals with physical disabilities, which falls squarely within the Department's policy focus areas of community living, accessibility, and assistive technology support.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a forensic review board at each facility housing individuals committed as not criminally responsible (NCR). The boards, composed of licensed healthcare providers, must conduct reviews at least annually to determine whether to recommend to the court that a committed person be granted conditional release or discharge, formulate plans to overcome release barriers, and allow committed individuals to be represented by authorized nonlegal agents at meetings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals committed to state facilities after being found not criminally responsible (NCR), facility treatment teams and healthcare providers, defense representatives and authorized agents, state courts, and State's Attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, as State forensic hospitals and the Community Forensic Aftercare Program already operate forensic review boards. The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Local effect: No material effect on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to establish forensic review boards at each facility housing individuals committed as not criminally responsible (NCR), adopt regulations to carry out the provisions, and implement treatment and rehabilitation recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents committed indigent individuals in criminal commitment and release proceedings. The bill requires notice to counsel of record, grants access to board records, and permits social workers or nonlegal representatives from the attorney's office to serve as authorized agents during board meetings.

The forensic review boards make formal recommendations regarding discharge or conditional release to the court, board records must be provided to the court upon request, and board representatives may testify at judicial release hearings.

Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings routinely conduct administrative hearings regarding the release and discharge eligibility of committed persons under Title 3 of the Criminal Procedure Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill revises the Maryland Corps Program and its service pathways (Young Adult Service Year Option and Maryland Service Year Option), updating participant eligibility, age requirements, and compensation structures. It mandates participant pay to be at least the applicable county or State minimum wage (whichever is greater), designates the $6,000 completion award strictly as a cash payment, grants flexibility to use pathway funds across both programs for participant stipends, repeals the inactive Executive Fellows Program, and officially renames the Governor's Volunteer Council as the Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
qa_results.stakeholders: Young adults aged 18 to 24 participating in the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway, Maryland residents aged 18 and older participating in the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway, and participating employer organizations and service hosts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures experience potential significant, offsetting decreases beginning as early as FY 2027 because surplus funds in the Maryland Service Year Pathway Fund can be used to fund Young Adult Pathway expenses rather than reverting to the General Fund, resulting in no net effect on the General Fund. There is also a potential minimal increase in special fund expenditures to cover participant stipends if local county minimum wages exceed the State minimum wage. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is the primary administering department for the legislation. The bill alters DSCI's program requirements, applicant eligibility, fund usage across service pathways, reporting deadlines, minimum wage stipends, and formally repeals the defunct Executive Fellows Program under its jurisdiction.

The bill updates statutory language to formally reflect the transfer of the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism out of the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives and into the Department of Service and Civic Innovation.

The bill repeals the statutory provision allowing Maryland Corps completion awards to be deposited into tax-exempt Maryland 529 accounts, converting all program completion awards exclusively into cash stipends due to account deposit limitations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames the statutory Governor's Volunteer Council to the Governor's Commission on Service and Volunteerism and repeals the selection committee established for the Executive Fellows Program.

The bill specifically references the Office of Legislative Audits and maintains audit authority and reporting oversight for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill consolidates three aging services programs—Senior Care, the Senior Assisted Living Subsidy (SALS), and the Congregate Housing Services Provider (CHSP) programs—into a unified system administered by the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA). It repeals the Interagency Committee on Aging Services, transferring and clarifying its duties under MDOA, and updates statutory terminology from "seniors" to "older adults." Additionally, it requires MDOA and Area Agencies on Aging to conduct transition planning and person-centered assessments for currently enrolled individuals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, their family caregivers, Area Agencies on Aging, assisted living facility providers, and congregate housing service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can likely be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. The fiscal 2026 state budget includes $20.1 million in general funds across the three consolidating programs ($13.2 million for Senior Care, $4.9 million for SALS, and $1.9 million for CHSP), which are assumed to fund the consolidated program beginning in fiscal 2027. State expenditures and local revenues/expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent MDOA enters into new agreements or contracts with local governments or other entities to coordinate services. Area Agencies on Aging can conduct required person-centered transition assessments using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reorganizes and consolidates the Department of Aging's major programs (Senior Care, Senior Assisted Living Subsidy, and Congregate Housing Services Provider programs) under a unified statutory framework, transfers the responsibilities of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services directly to the Department, and charges it with program transition planning and administering the single points of entry network.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals the statutory Interagency Committee on Aging Services and reassigns its responsibilities to the Department of Aging.

The Secretary of Health was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services, and the consolidated services include subsidies for assisted living programs regulated and licensed under the Health - General Article.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services, and the bill alters and consolidates senior housing and supportive living service frameworks.
The Secretary of Human Services was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services.
The Secretary of Disabilities was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services.
The Department of Aging plans to coordinate with DBM to consolidate three distinct budget lines (Senior Care, SALS, and CHSP totaling over $20 million) into a single unified budget program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the criminal misdemeanor prohibition and associated statutory penalties against knowingly transferring or attempting to transfer the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) to another individual.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals living with HIV and individuals involved in the criminal justice system in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local governmental finances or operations, including District Court caseloads and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 18-601.1 of the Health - General Article, which falls within the public health statutes governing infectious and contagious diseases under the purview of the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill decriminalizes conduct previously punishable as a misdemeanor carrying up to three years of imprisonment and fines, eliminating these specific charges and proceedings in District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor that carried a potential penalty of up to three years imprisonment, directly affecting the offenses for which indigent defendants may require representation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal removes a criminal offense that carried potential incarceration sentences of up to three years and community supervision, marginally impacting correctional intake and parole/probation caseloads.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing criminal laws, State Police troopers will no longer investigate or file charges under this specific repealed statute.

The Office of the Attorney General acts as legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health and handles criminal appeals on behalf of the State, both of which are touched by the repeal of this criminal health statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the fees for resident consolidated senior sport fishing licenses, resident and nonresident angler's licenses, and trout stamps. It also repeals the trout stamp exemption for holders of a resident consolidated senior sport fishing license, requiring seniors who fish for trout to purchase a trout stamp.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Recreational anglers (both resident and nonresident), senior anglers age 65 and older, trout anglers, and authorized license-issuing agents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $565,800 in FY 2025 and by approximately $2,977,800 annually in FY 2026 and subsequent years, primarily benefiting the Fisheries Management and Protection Fund and the Fisheries Research and Development Fund. General fund revenues increase indeterminately through FY 2028 from accrued interest. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 40 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It alters the fees for angler's licenses, resident consolidated senior sport fishing licenses, and trout stamps administered by DNR, generating an estimated $3.0 million in annual special fund revenues for DNR's Fisheries Management and Protection Fund and Fisheries Research and Development Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill moves up the deadline by which petitions to form a new political party, or any additional signatures, can be filed in presidential and gubernatorial election years, prohibiting filings after the first Monday in July rather than the first Monday in August before the general election. Additionally, it prohibits signatures submitted on a petition that failed to meet legal requirements from being resubmitted in a subsequent petition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Groups and voters seeking to form new political parties in Maryland, as well as state and local election administrators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill sponsored at the request of the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE). SBE is directly responsible for administering petition filing deadlines, verifying signatures, and managing the recognition process for new political parties in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of Public Works, upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health, to award grants under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program to counties, municipal corporations, and nonprofit organizations for the acquisition of land to construct or operate a federally qualified health center.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Counties, municipal corporations, nonprofit organizations operating or developing federally qualified health centers, and patients served by community health centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: Alters eligible uses for existing grant funds under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program; any administrative changes can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources of the Board of Public Works and the Maryland Department of Health. Local effect: Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local entities apply for and receive grant funding to acquire land for health centers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program, reviews applications, and recommends grant allocations—now including land acquisition—to the Board of Public Works.
The Board of Public Works is directly authorized under the bill to award grants for the acquisition of land for federally qualified health centers upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council by adding the Administrator of the Motor Vehicle Administration (or designee) and the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity in the Maryland Cannabis Administration (or designee), and updates technical references to the Maryland Cannabis Administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council, Motor Vehicle Administration, Office of Social Equity, traffic safety officials, and Maryland drivers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Administrator of the Motor Vehicle Administration (or their designee) as a voting member of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council to provide expertise on impaired driving.

The bill updates statutory language to reference the Maryland Cannabis Administration and directly adds the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity within the Administration as a member of the Advisory Council.

The Advisory Council is established within the Health - General Article and is staffed and provided technical assistance by the Maryland Department of Health, with the Secretary and Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health serving as statutory members.
The bill was introduced as a departmental request by the Maryland Department of Transportation to ensure transportation safety and impaired driving considerations are represented on the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory membership and composition of an executive advisory council (the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy is an existing statutory member of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council reenacted under the bill.
The Secretary of Agriculture is an existing statutory member of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council reenacted under the bill.
The State Superintendent of Schools is an existing statutory member of the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council reenacted under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) framework administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). It excludes hospitals and certain manufacturing facilities from the definition of covered buildings and establishes exemptions and special accounting credits for on-site renewable energy, biomethane use, steam sterilization, emergency backup power, and sensitive compartmented information facilities. The bill establishes an annual reporting fee of $100 per covered building, requires MDE to certify qualifying county-level BEPS programs (exempting buildings in those counties from the State program), and directs MDE to complete a comprehensive cost-benefit study and policy recommendations regarding BEPS options by December 31, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and commercial tenants of commercial and multifamily residential buildings (35,000 square feet or larger), hospitals, manufacturing facilities, defense and intelligence facilities, local governments (notably Montgomery County), and energy auditors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $690,000 in FY 2026, increasing to $746,900 by FY 2030 due to a $100 annual reporting fee (adjusted for inflation) assessed on an estimated 6,900 covered buildings. MDE administrative expenditures increase by $1,033,837 in FY 2026 (5 regular positions plus contractual tracking and study costs); because fee revenue covers $690,000, general fund expenditures increase by $343,837 in FY 2026 to fund the initial shortfall. State and local agencies owning covered buildings will incur minor annual costs to pay the reporting fee starting in FY 2026. Future alternative compliance pathway fee revenues collected by the State may decrease beginning in FY 2031 due to added exemptions and county certifications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, establishing and enforcing Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS), certifying county BEPS programs, collecting reporting fees, and completing the mandated cost-benefit study.

DGS oversees the operation, maintenance, and energy management of state-owned facilities. State-owned buildings meeting the size threshold are covered buildings subject to the BEPS requirements and the annual reporting fee.

MEA coordinates state energy efficiency and renewable energy policy, which intersects directly with building energy performance metrics, energy use intensity, and on-site clean energy standards addressed by the bill.

Multifamily residential buildings of 35,000 square feet or more are covered buildings under BEPS, directly intersecting with DHCD's oversight and financing of residential housing and energy efficiency initiatives.
USM owns and operates numerous campus facilities meeting the covered building threshold (35,000 sq ft or greater) that must comply with BEPS standards and pay the annual reporting fee.
As an independent state university owning substantial campus facilities, Morgan State University is subject to BEPS reporting requirements and fee payments for its eligible covered buildings.
MDOT operates and maintains significant state-owned administrative and operational facilities that are subject to the BEPS standards and annual reporting fees as covered state buildings.
OAG provides legal counsel and enforcement support to MDE for regulatory promulgation and compliance enforcement, including additional legal staffing noted in the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the June 30, 2025 sunset date on the formula used to calculate the maximum user fee assessment imposed on hospitals and related facilities by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC), permanently maintaining the cap at the greater of 0.1% of the prior fiscal year's budgeted gross hospital revenue or the highest cap amount from the preceding five fiscal years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals and related healthcare facilities regulated by the Commission, the Maryland Medicaid program, and healthcare payers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for HSCRC increase by an estimated $1.6 million in FY 2026, growing to $4.8 million in FY 2030 compared to current law. Higher hospital user fees lead to higher hospital rates, increasing Medicaid expenditures by up to $315,409 in FY 2026 ($126,164 general funds, $189,245 federal funds) and $963,267 in FY 2030, with federal fund revenues increasing correspondingly. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to HSCRC by repealing the sunset on the statutory formula used to calculate the maximum user fees it assesses on hospitals, preserving higher special fund revenues needed to support commission operations and the AHEAD Model.

HSCRC is an independent agency located within MDH, and this was introduced as an MDH departmental bill. Additionally, the higher hospital user fees will increase MDH Medicaid expenditures by hundreds of thousands of dollars annually due to associated hospital rate adjustments.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill revises Maryland's tax sale process by requiring local collectors statewide to withhold owner-occupied residential properties and homes occupied by heirs of deceased owners from tax sale if unpaid taxes and liens are under $1,000. It caps the annual redemption interest rate on owner-occupied residential properties at 10%, excludes post-sale taxes, interest, and penalties from redemption payments for owner-occupied properties statewide, requires counties to establish a registry for properties to be withheld from sale, mandates notice of foreclosure proceedings on owner-occupied properties to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, enhances tenant notice requirements prior to eviction, and expands the Homeowner Protection Program to include heirs and personal representatives of deceased homeowners.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners (especially low-income, senior, disabled homeowners, and heirs of deceased homeowners), tenants in foreclosed residential properties, local governments and tax collectors, and private tax lien purchasers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues are delayed and/or reduced by up to an estimated $92,000 annually due to limits on the redemption rate for owner-occupied properties; State expenditures are not materially affected. Local government revenues are also delayed or reduced, potentially by up to $1.1 million annually from the redemption rate cap and the $1,000 tax sale withholding threshold. Local government expenditures may increase for administrative, personnel, and IT programming costs to track owner-occupied properties and maintain the required withholding registry.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 59 was requested as a departmental bill by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The bill aims to protect vulnerable homeowners, prevent displacement, assist heirs in retaining inherited family homes, and facilitate the return of abandoned properties to productive redevelopment.

The bill directly impacts circuit court foreclosure proceedings by modifying procedures to foreclose the right of redemption, adding required notice to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, and altering procedural rules and notice timelines regarding writs of possession for tenant-occupied properties.

The bill has a minor fiscal impact on Annuity Bond Fund revenues (reducing or delaying state property tax receipts by up to $92,000 annually), which are managed by the Treasurer's Office to pay debt service on the State's general obligation bonds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Public Accountancy by five years to July 1, 2030, continuing its regulatory and licensing authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act, and requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report regarding the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed certified public accountants, public accountancy firms, and clients utilizing public accountancy services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Public Accountancy are maintained from fiscal 2026 through 2030. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee can manage the reporting requirement using existing resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This bill extends the board's termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2030, maintaining its special fund operations, and requires the Department to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Holocaust Education Assistance Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education to provide grants to local school systems for Holocaust-related teacher training and teaching materials.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, public school educators, and public school students.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 annually due to a mandated appropriation for the grant program, with no effect on State revenues. The Maryland State Department of Education can administer the program using existing resources. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2027 by up to $50,000 per school system (or roughly $2,083 annually if split equally among all 24 jurisdictions) for systems that apply for and receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Holocaust Education Assistance Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education, making the agency responsible for administering the grant program and awarding funds to local school systems.
The bill statutory mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $50,000 for the program in the state budget bill.
As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and managing mandated appropriations, DBM must incorporate the mandated $50,000 annual appropriation beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the threshold for State real property leases exempt from competitive procurement from 2,500 square feet to 5,000 square feet. It also reduces the required advertising window before lease proposals are due from 30 days to 20 days and updates advertising requirements to mandate posting on the Department of General Services website and eMaryland Marketplace.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies seeking leased property, commercial real estate landlords, and prospective lease bidders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on State finances or activities and has no local fiscal impact. The Department of General Services and the Department of Legislative Services also determined there is minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS requested this departmental bill and is the primary implementing agency responsible for state real estate leasing, procurement of building space, and managing the eMaryland Marketplace platform.
The Board of Public Works is responsible for reviewing and approving State leases and real property acquisitions, which are directly affected by the modified procurement and advertising processes.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the scheduling and administration requirements for special elections to fill vacancies in a county council or the office of county executive. It requires the election date to be at least 90 days after the adoption of the county council resolution and not within 120 days of a regularly scheduled election. It also provides that if a conflict exists between local charter laws and State election law or regulations, the State Administrator must conduct the election under State law. Additionally, for vote-by-mail special elections, it expands the ballot mailing deadline from 14 to at least 30 days before election day, permits ballot drop box returns, and eliminates the requirement for local boards of elections to mail specimen ballots.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections (State Administrator of Elections) and local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered voters in counties holding special elections, local boards of elections, county councils, county executives, and candidates for local office.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected. Local government finances may be indirectly affected depending on the timing of special elections, as the restrictions may alter whether a county must conduct a special election independent of a regularly scheduled election or concurrently, with independent special elections entailing substantial local expenditures (e.g., Prince George's County spent $2.1 million on a countywide mail-in special primary in 2024).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 75 was introduced at the request of the State Board of Elections (SBE) and directly affects the administration of special elections in Maryland. The bill alters special election timelines, authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to enforce state law and regulations over conflicting local charters, eliminates the specimen ballot mailing requirement for vote-by-mail special elections, adjusts ballot mailing deadlines, and authorizes ballot drop boxes for mail-in special elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill specifies the permissible methods for providing notice and sending documents under the Maryland Trust Decanting Act, requiring personal service, certified/first-class mail with return receipt requested, or courier delivery service, unless a recipient agrees in writing to alternative methods such as email, fax, or regular first-class mail.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and authorized fiduciaries
qa_results.stakeholders: Authorized fiduciaries (trustees), trust beneficiaries, estate planners, and individuals involved in trusts governed by Maryland law
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. Any impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes statutory standards for procedural notice and document transmittal under the Maryland Trust Decanting Act, which affects estate and trust litigation and disputes adjudicated within the Maryland court system.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court; although decanting primarily pertains to trusts, procedural changes under the Estates and Trusts Article directly intersect with their domain of probate and fiduciary administration.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protections, oversees charitable trusts that may be subject to decanting notices, and provided input as an information source during the bill's review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that each animal harmed in an animal cruelty violation constitutes a separate offense and is considered an individual victim for the sentencing guidelines stacking rule. It prevents animal crime convictions from merging with convictions for other crimes based on the same act, authorizes consecutive or concurrent sentencing, and clarifies exemptions for humane hunting and fishing conducted under State law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of animal cruelty crimes, state and local judicial and correctional systems, law enforcement officers, hunters, and anglers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues may increase minimally due to additional fine collections in District Court and circuit courts. State and local expenditures may increase minimally due to potential longer periods of incarceration resulting from separate convictions and consecutive sentencing under the sentencing guidelines stacking rule. Incarceration costs average $5,339 per month for State facilities and $140 to $350 per day for local facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by establishing that each harmed animal constitutes a separate offense for sentencing guidelines stacking, prohibiting merger of convictions, and permitting consecutive sentencing in District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows for multiple separate convictions and consecutive sentences for animal cruelty violations, potentially increasing sentence lengths and expenditures for State correctional facilities and supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts criminal defense caseloads and representation for indigent defendants who face expanded charges, non-merging convictions, and stacked sentencing for each animal harmed.
The bill clarifies that animal cruelty provisions do not apply to hunting and fishing activities conducted in compliance with Title 4 and Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article.
The bill maintains statutory exemptions for customary agricultural husbandry practices, veterinary practices, and farming operations overseen and supported by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the time period from 90 days to 4 years during which an individual with an expired heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) contractor license may apply for license restoration upon payment of the required renewal or reinstatement fee, rather than having to reapply as a new applicant.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors (Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration contractors and licensees in Maryland with expired licenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of HVACR Contractors can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and expenditures are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the licensing restoration timeframe for the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, which is an occupational licensing board housed within and administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership and leadership of the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs by replacing the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services with the Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee. It also authorizes local health departments and community-based organizations to appeal adverse program authorization decisions to the Secretary of Health or their designee instead of the Deputy Secretary.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Local health departments, community-based organizations operating or seeking to operate Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs, and members of the Standing Advisory Committee.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 94 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Health. It shifts the authority to hear appeals of program authorization denials and to chair the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs from the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services to the Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition and leadership of the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs by replacing the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services with the Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee as a member and chair.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy is responsible for nominating a law enforcement representative to serve on the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a population ratio quota for Class A and Class D off-sale alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County, prohibiting the issuance of new licenses if the ratio exceeds one license per 3,500 individuals in a tax assessment district (excluding the 6th assessment district). It also restricts the transfer of these licenses outside of their original assessment district, with exemptions for existing licenses and certain brewery on-site consumption permits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A and Class D off-sale alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants, local businesses, and residents of Anne Arundel County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Anne Arundel County revenues and expenditures are not affected; while new off-sale licenses are temporarily restricted in several assessment districts until population increases, existing licenses are grandfathered, resulting in no change to current county license fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding retail alcoholic beverages licenses and references State-issued Class 5 brewery licenses. While retail licensing is administered locally by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller regulates Maryland's alcohol industry and state-level alcohol manufacturer licenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of a 'public entity' in Maryland insurance law to include Resilience Authorities, thereby allowing them to pool together with other public entities to purchase casualty, property, or health insurance or to self-insure against those risks.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Resilience authorities, local governments that incorporate resilience authorities, and other public entities participating in insurance pools.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are unaffected. Local expenditures may decrease to the extent that resilience authorities participate in insurance pooling and achieve lower premium or insurance costs; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 19-602 of the Insurance Article to expand the definition of 'public entity' to include resilience authorities for the purpose of insurance pooling and self-insurance. As the primary regulatory agency overseeing Maryland's insurance laws and market practices, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees compliance with statutory insurance provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters and delays key implementation dates and administrative requirements for the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. It delays the start date of required employer and employee contributions by 18 months to January 1, 2027, and delays the start of benefit payments to a date between January 1, 2027, and January 3, 2028, as determined by the Secretary of Labor. It also establishes the term "anchor date" to govern average weekly wage calculations and benefit increases, modifies the definition of an application year, delays the inflation indexing of maximum weekly benefits to 2029, and postpones the optional self-employed enrollment program until regulations are adopted by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers (especially those with 15 or more employees), Maryland workers/covered employees, self-employed individuals, community service providers reimbursed by the State, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State FAMLI special fund revenues decrease by approximately $1,272.5 million in FY 2026 and $1,316.9 million in FY 2027 due to the 18-month delay in contributions. Special fund expenditures for benefit payments decrease by up to $1,753.5 million in FY 2027 and $946.7 million in FY 2028. For FY 2026, special fund administrative expenditures decrease by $66.8 million, general fund expenditures increase by $37.3 million for non-deferrable program administration, and provider reimbursement expenditures through the Maryland Department of Health decrease by $14.8 million in general funds and $14.9 million in federal funds (a net FY 2026 general fund increase of $22.5 million). The bill also eliminates a mandated appropriation for FY 2026. Local government expenditures decrease in FY 2026 and FY 2027 due to delayed employer contributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor administers the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. HB 102 is a departmental bill that directly modifies the program's statutory implementation dates, contribution schedules, benefit calculation rules, reporting requirements, and mandates the adoption of regulations for self-employed individuals.

Under state law and Section 8.3-601 of the Labor and Employment Article, the Maryland Department of Health is required to reimburse certain licensed community providers for employer FAMLI contributions. The delay in contributions directly reduces MDH general and federal fund reimbursement expenditures by nearly $30 million in FY 2026.

The Board of Public Works is statutorily designated under the FAMLI law to monitor state employment data and determine whether negative economic conditions exist to pause the annual Consumer Price Index adjustments to maximum weekly benefits.

As the state's budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and state agency appropriations. The bill effectuates contingent budget provisions in the FY 2026 state operating budget, resulting in adjustments to general and special fund expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the purpose and authorized uses of the Maryland Farms and Families Fund by allowing the Maryland Department of Agriculture to implement the program internally or provide funds to qualified nonprofit organizations or other responsible persons to match federal nutrition benefits (FMNP, SNAP, and WIC) at farmers markets and farm stands.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Food-insecure Maryland residents utilizing federal nutrition benefits (SNAP, WIC, and FMNP), Maryland farmers and farmers market operators, and nonprofit organizations managing food incentive programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances, as it only alters the allowable uses and administration of the existing Maryland Farms and Families Fund (which receives an ongoing mandated annual appropriation of $300,000). The Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement the bill using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) requested the bill and is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Maryland Farms and Families Program and Fund, including directly managing program funds and overseeing partnerships with farmers markets.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO has historically served as the grant applicant and fiscal pass-through entity to manage the program statewide with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission; this bill directly streamlines the process by eliminating the need to route funds through MARBIDCO.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates automatic renewal and continuous service offers for subscriptions and purchasing agreements by requiring businesses to clearly disclose renewal terms, obtain consumer consent before recurring credit card charges, provide advance notice before renewal or the end of a free trial, and offer simple, cost-effective cancellation mechanisms. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers enrolled in or entering into subscription services and businesses offering automatic renewal contracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's penalty provisions will not materially affect State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can administer and enforce the requirements using existing resources. No private right of action for damages is authorized.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines violations of the automatic renewal requirements as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill specifically mentions and exempts businesses or entities whose contract renewal practices are subject to rules, regulations, procedures, or guidelines established by the Maryland Insurance Administration.
The bill specifically mentions and exempts services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission from the new automatic renewal statutory requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires that commercial applications of restricted use pesticides be performed directly by certified applicators, eliminating the option for noncertified individuals to apply them under supervision. It establishes federal compliance and direct supervision standards for noncertified individuals applying restricted use pesticides privately in agriculture, specifies liability for certified applicators, and repeals obsolete statutory provisions regulating cyclodiene termiticides and tributyltin antifouling paint.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial pest control businesses, certified and registered pest control applicators, private agricultural pesticide applicators, and public agency applicators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Agriculture's Pesticide Fund increase by at least $140,000 annually starting in FY 2026 due to an estimated 2,000 registered employees upgrading to certified applicators and paying higher annual certification fees. State expenditures are unaffected as administrative tasks can be absorbed with existing resources, and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Department of Agriculture and directly alters the Pesticide Applicator's Law under Title 5 of the Agriculture Article, requiring the department to administer new certification requirements and examinations, as well as collect increased annual certification fee revenues for the State Pesticide Fund.

DNR employs public agency applicators who perform pest and vegetation management on state-owned lands and waterways, and must ensure its personnel comply with the updated certification and supervision standards for restricted and general use pesticides.

MDOT employs public agency applicators to perform pest control along highways and transit rights-of-way, and must ensure that personnel applying pesticides meet the revised applicator certification requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Utility Transparency and Accountability Act, requiring electric companies (excluding municipal electric utilities) to submit an annual report to the Public Service Commission by February 1 detailing all recorded votes cast by the company or its State affiliates at regional transmission organization meetings during the preceding calendar year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland electric companies (excluding municipal electric utilities), their State affiliates, regional transmission organizations such as PJM Interconnection, LLC, and Maryland electricity consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body designated to receive and oversee the annual reports submitted by electric companies detailing recorded votes cast at regional transmission organization meetings.

The Office of the People's Counsel advocates on behalf of Maryland's residential utility consumers before the PSC and federal regulatory bodies regarding utility operations, rates, and transmission issues, and is actively involved in monitoring RTO stakeholder voting and transparency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the membership of the Maryland Correctional Training Commission to include two additional members: the Director of the Division of Parole and Probation within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and one employee of the Division of Parole and Probation recommended by the employees' exclusive representative and appointed by the Governor.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Correctional Training Commission, personnel of the Division of Parole and Probation, and parole and probation agents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected, as any expense reimbursements for the two additional commission members can be handled with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
