agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Correctional Training Commission operates within DPSCS. The bill expands the commission's membership to specifically include the Director of the Division of Parole and Probation (a division within DPSCS) and an employee of the division.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory composition and membership requirements of the Maryland Correctional Training Commission.
The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint an employee of the Division of Parole and Probation to the Maryland Correctional Training Commission.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the newly established gubernatorial appointee from the Division of Parole and Probation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires wholesale buyers and wholesale sellers of residential property to provide specific written disclosures before entering into or assigning contracts of sale. If the required disclosures are not provided, property owners and assignees are authorized to rescind the contract without penalty before closing, and assignees are entitled to a refund of any deposit paid.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of residential property, wholesale real estate buyers and sellers, and assignees of residential purchase contracts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, monitors and enforces laws protecting residential property owners and consumers against unfair or deceptive business practices, including improper disclosures in wholesale real estate contract assignments.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation and licensing of real estate professionals and industry practices; it was consulted regarding the impact of contract assignment disclosures and consumer protections.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judiciary, which may adjudicate civil disputes relating to the rescission of residential sales contracts and the return of earnest money deposits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the entities eligible to originate and administer local rehabilitation programs under the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP) within the Department of Housing and Community Development to include qualified nonprofit sponsors.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit housing organizations and sponsors, local governments and political subdivisions, and limited-income Maryland residents seeking housing rehabilitation loans.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances. It is also not expected to materially affect local government operations or finances, although some local jurisdictions may experience minor shifts in MHRP suballocations if funding is directed to nonprofit sponsors rather than local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 127 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It expands eligibility for administering local rehabilitation programs under DHCD's Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP) to include nonprofit sponsors, authorizing DHCD to certify, allocate funds to, train, and provide technical assistance to these entities.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 131 modifies the prioritization and eligibility criteria for financial assistance awarded from the Bay Restoration Fund's Septics Account. It updates the funding priority order for repairing or replacing failing septic systems to prioritize systems in the Critical Area, systems in high-effectiveness nitrogen-reduction watersheds, and systems located within 500-year floodplains. Additionally, it expands eligibility for system repair and replacement funding to moderate-income homeowners in addition to low-income homeowners, and shifts the eligibility cutoff date for community sewerage system conversions and municipal wastewater connections from a fixed 2008 date to a rolling standard requiring installation or occupancy at least 15 years before the application year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of on-site sewage disposal systems (septic systems), low- and moderate-income homeowners, local governments, local health departments, and septic installation and maintenance contractors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected overall, as the bill only shifts project prioritization and eligibility without altering overall Bay Restoration Fund revenues or expenditures; the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the changes with existing resources. Local government grant totals remain unchanged, but funding distribution across jurisdictions may shift based on the new criteria, and local health departments may experience a minor operational workload increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) administers the Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account, establishes priority rankings, determines funding criteria for septic upgrades and community sewerage connections, and oversees grant distribution to local jurisdictions.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily tasked with maintaining the separate Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account and disbursing funds in accordance with the statutory formula.

The bill impacts the administration and prioritization of block grants distributed through local health departments, which operate under the state public health framework to evaluate and approve septic systems and health concerns.

The Department of Agriculture receives a statutory 40% transfer of Bay Restoration Fund septic fee revenues for the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost Share Cover Crop Program, referenced directly within the amended section.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the requirement that the State Department of Assessments and Taxation calculate and notify each local taxing authority of the constant yield tax rate annually, requiring the Department to calculate and provide the notice only upon the request of a taxing authority made on or before February 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Local taxing authorities (county councils, county commissioners, Baltimore City, and municipal governing bodies) and property taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative expenditures may decrease minimally for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation beginning in fiscal 2026 because the department will calculate constant yield tax rates only upon request rather than for all jurisdictions. There is no local fiscal impact, as the bill does not alter local property tax rates or notification requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is referenced in the unamended portion of § 2-205(b)(2) of the Tax - Property Article retained in the bill regarding changes in estimated property assessments resulting from board actions, though the bill does not substantively alter the board's operations.

The Maryland Tax Court is referenced in the unamended portion of § 2-205(b)(2) of the Tax - Property Article retained in the bill regarding notifications of changes in estimated property assessments resulting from court actions, though the bill does not substantively alter the court's operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, rather than the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, is responsible for reimbursing physicians, qualified health care providers, and hospitals for sexual assault forensic examinations and related treatments provided to victims of alleged rape, sexual offenses, or child sexual abuse.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of alleged rape, sexual offenses, or child sexual abuse, and the physicians, qualified health care providers, and hospitals providing them with forensic examinations and treatment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact. It codifies current practice, in which the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy already processes and pays these reimbursements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 136 is a departmental bill requested by GOCPP that formally designates the office, rather than the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, as the entity responsible for paying physicians, qualified health care providers, and hospitals for sexual assault examinations, follow-up care, and HIV postexposure prophylaxis treatments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a trustee of a trust under the Maryland Trust Act to resign without seeking court approval by providing at least 30 days' notice to qualified beneficiaries, the settlor (if living), any co-trustees, and any individual with the authority to appoint or replace a successor trustee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Trustees, trust settlors, qualified beneficiaries, co-trustees, and persons authorized to appoint successor trustees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under current law, a trustee typically must seek court approval to resign. The bill permits trustees to resign upon giving 30 days' notice to specified parties without court approval, which directly affects civil caseloads and proceedings in Maryland courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory requirement that child care centers maintain at least one staff member certified in basic first aid and CPR for every 20 children, instead authorizing the Maryland State Department of Education to establish the required ratio of certified staff to children by regulation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Child care centers and operators, child care workers and teachers, and children and families enrolled in child care programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill with existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. Small business child care centers may benefit from reduced staff training costs and easier staff recruitment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 150 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It authorizes MSDE and the State Board to establish the ratio of first aid and CPR-certified staff to children in child care centers through regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program to the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program and lowers the eligible participant age from 65 to 60 for older adults at risk of social isolation. It expands allowable communications beyond telephone calls to include texts, web-based, video, and in-person outreach accessible to individuals with disabilities, authorizes service integration with Telecommunications Access of Maryland, and allows contracts and agreements with local agencies, Area Agencies on Aging, and Senior Villages.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland older adults aged 60 and older who are at risk of social isolation (including deaf, hard-of-hearing, and disabled seniors), Area Agencies on Aging, local government agencies, and community Senior Villages.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The bill primarily alters the purposes for which existing funds may be used, with the fiscal 2026 budget including $419,967 in special funds from the Universal Service Trust Fund (USTF). Administrative duties can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, though special fund expenditures may increase if new service agreements are executed. Local Effect: Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent that local entities or Area Agencies on Aging contract with the Maryland Department of Aging to provide program services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames, restructures, and expands the Department of Aging's Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program into the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program, authorizing new forms of direct communication, expanding participant eligibility, and establishing new contracting and interagency partnership mechanisms.

The bill mandates integration of the program with the Telecommunications Access of Maryland (TAM) program, which is housed within the Department of Disabilities, requiring the promotion of accessible equipment and the use of TAM's educational outreach materials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt curriculum guides and courses of study aligned with content standards established by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It establishes a formal process for the State Superintendent of Schools to identify discrepancies, require corrective action plans, mandate the adoption of State curriculum standards and resources upon noncompliance, and withhold State education funds if a county board fails to comply.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (State Superintendent of Schools)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, public school educators, and local county boards of education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected, as MSDE can develop content standards and manage discrepancy notices using existing resources, though broader review duties may require staff redirection. Local school system expenditures may increase, likely minimally, to update curriculum guides to align with MSDE standards. Noncompliant school systems risk having State education funds withheld, though such occurrences are anticipated to be rare.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE and the State Superintendent of Schools are the primary entities responsible for implementing the bill, including developing state content standards, monitoring local school board curriculum guides for discrepancies, approving corrective action plans, and enforcing compliance by directing the withholding of state funds if necessary.

Under the enforcement provisions of the bill and current law referenced in §§ 2-303 and 5-205 of the Education Article, the State Comptroller is responsible for withholding state education aid disbursements to noncompliant local school boards upon direction from the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue reciprocal permits allowing licensed out-of-state motor home and recreational vehicle dealers to display or exhibit vehicles at shows in Worcester County, provided their home states grant reciprocal privileges to Maryland dealers and the dealer files a required bond, while prohibiting them from executing buyer's orders or accepting deposits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed out-of-state and Maryland dealers of motor homes and recreational trailers, vehicle show organizers, and attendees of recreational vehicle shows in Worcester County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local Effect: The bill does not affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is directly designated to implement and administer the bill, including establishing and issuing the out-of-state motor home and recreational trailer vehicle show permits, determining permit duration and bond amounts, approving corporate sureties, and enforcing compliance through suspension or revocation.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees vehicle administration, licensing, and regulatory compliance under the Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the date through which the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund may be used from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2027, allowing the Maryland Department of Health to spend any remaining funds on maternal and child health initiatives for two additional years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant women, mothers, infants, and young children in Maryland (particularly Medicaid recipients and those receiving maternal morbidity, asthma, home visiting, and doula care services), as well as participating healthcare providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: No new special fund revenues are collected. Allows up to an estimated $24.1 million in remaining special funds to continue to be expended across FY 2026 through the first half of FY 2028 in lieu of State general funds. Funds expended through Medicaid continue to leverage federal matching funds. In the absence of the bill, unspent balances would remain locked and general funds would be required to sustain programs. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health co-administers the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund, requested this departmental legislation, and directly expends the fund's monies through its Medical Care Programs Administration and Prevention and Health Promotion Administration.
The Health Services Cost Review Commission co-administers the Fund, establishes the hospital rate assessment that finances it, and must approve all expenditures made from the Fund.
Statute designates the State Treasurer to hold the Fund separately and invest its moneys on behalf of the State.
Statute requires the Comptroller to account for the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund.
The statute explicitly notes that the Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Davis Martinez Public Employee Safety and Health Act establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health (PESH) Unit within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry to oversee and enforce workplace safety and health standards for public bodies. The bill removes the previous exemption of public bodies from Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) civil penalties, requires standards to prevent workplace violence against public employees, and establishes regulations and legal exceptions for the use of body-worn cameras by correctional officers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Division of Labor and Industry)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public sector employees, state and local government agencies (public bodies), correctional officers, and participants in the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State expenditures increase by $604,785 ($535,390 in general funds and $69,385 in special funds) for 1 MD Labor administrative officer ($69,385), 1 Assistant Attorney General ($106,659), and $428,790 in contingent general funds for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to acquire body-worn cameras. State special fund revenues for the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program increase by an estimated $30,000 in FY 2026 and $40,000 annually thereafter from civil penalties assessed against public bodies. Local government expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 for compliance and potential MOSH penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency. The bill establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health (PESH) Unit within the Division of Labor and Industry, requires the Commissioner to adopt workplace violence regulations for public bodies, conduct inspections, issue citations, and dedicate civil penalty revenues to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly impacted by the bill's body-worn camera (BWC) provisions and the Correctional Training Commission's regulations. The bill also triggers contingent funding in the FY 2026 state budget providing $428,790 to DPSCS for the acquisition and implementation of BWCs for correctional and supervision personnel.

The bill mandates the Attorney General to expedite review of administrative search warrant applications, provide required notices when proceeding to enforce citations or collect penalties against public bodies, and represent MOSH in an expected increase of contested citation proceedings, requiring an additional Assistant Attorney General position.

As a state agency operating juvenile detention facilities and employing officers meeting the definition of correctional units/officers, DJS is required to develop and maintain written policies consistent with the regulations for body-worn cameras.

The operational costs and administrative staffing of the MOSH program within MD Labor are funded via appropriations from the State Workers' Compensation Commission, which supports the new administrative personnel required under the bill.

The District Court of Maryland is designated as the court where applications for administrative search warrants are submitted and where actions to enforce payment of civil penalties may proceed, along with court application of the bill's wiretap exceptions.

The bill requires the Attorney General and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to formally notify the Governor whenever legal enforcement action is initiated or when a public body fails to pay assessed workplace safety civil penalties within 30 days.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Organized Retail Theft Act of 2025 creates the felony offense of organized retail theft for committing a series of retail thefts over a 90-day period with an aggregate value exceeding $1,500, setting tiered penalties and restitution requirements. It allows multiple thefts across different counties under a single scheme or continuing course of conduct to be joined and prosecuted in any county where one theft occurred, merges convictions with general theft for sentencing, and requires courts to make findings on whether certain crimes constitute organized retail theft for criminal record reporting.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District and Circuit Courts), State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (including the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository)
qa_results.stakeholders: Retail merchants, individuals accused or convicted of retail theft, criminal defense attorneys/Office of the Public Defender, prosecutors, and state and local correctional facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State general fund revenues may decrease minimally as fine revenues shift from District Court to circuit courts, while state incarceration expenditures may increase minimally due to longer sentences or additional state facility commitments. Local fine revenues in circuit courts may increase minimally, with no material impact on local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense of organized retail theft, alters venue provisions allowing multi-county theft charges to be consolidated, shifts certain theft cases from the District Court to the circuit courts, and mandates that courts make specific findings of fact for reporting purposes upon request by a State's Attorney.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is impacted by potential increases in state incarceration costs resulting from new felony penalties and longer sentences. Additionally, DPSCS operates the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives the court findings of organized retail theft required under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency will be required to defend indigent clients facing the new felony charges and notes that aggregating multi-county cases into circuit court felony prosecutions shifts caseload demands from District Court attorneys to more experienced circuit court defense attorneys.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency investigating criminal offenses across county lines, MSP will investigate organized retail theft rings operating across multiple Maryland jurisdictions under the unified venue provisions of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 181 authorizes the Adjutant General of the Maryland Military Department, rather than the Governor, to appoint the department's chief of staff and aides, and establishes that these staff members serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Military Department (Adjutant General)
qa_results.stakeholders: Chief of staff, aides, and leadership within the Maryland Military Department, as well as the Office of the Governor.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations because it conforms statute to current practice. It has no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly grants the Adjutant General statutory authority to appoint the chief of staff and aides within the Military Department, and specifies that these individuals serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General.
The bill transfers the appointment authority and supervisory 'at-pleasure' status of the Military Department's chief of staff and aides away from the Governor to the Adjutant General.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor with executive appointments; removing these positions from gubernatorial appointment authority eliminates them from the office's portfolio.
The Military Department directs the Maryland National Guard, and the chief of staff and aides subject to the appointment authority changes are full-time personnel serving in State active-duty status.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 182 replaces the flat $40 maximum civil penalty for speed camera violations with an escalating tiered fine structure ranging from $40 to $425 based on the recorded speed over the posted limit. Additionally, the bill requires the State Highway Administration to convene a stakeholder workgroup to study best practices for speed monitoring systems in school zones and report its findings by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists and vehicle owners cited by speed monitoring systems, student pedestrians and school communities, local law enforcement agencies, local governments, and the District Court.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are expected to increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 due to higher fines and more contested court cases; TTF expenditures increase correspondingly for authorized purposes through FY 2029. In FY 2026, one-time State costs include $75,000 in TTF expenditures for a consultant to assist the SHA workgroup and $33,600 in general fund expenditures for District Court computer programming. Local government revenues and public safety expenditures are also projected to increase, potentially significantly (e.g., Baltimore City fine revenues could net an estimated $1.7 million annually).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Highway Administration (SHA) convene a workgroup to study best practices for speed monitoring systems in school zones and submit a report with recommendations by December 1, 2025. Additionally, SHA receives fine revenues from speed cameras on MD Route 210, which will experience fiscal impacts.

MDOT is the parent department of the State Highway Administration. The bill affects Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures, including $75,000 in FY 2026 for consultant staffing costs and adjustments to fine revenues from MD Route 210.

The District Court must prescribe a revised uniform citation form reflecting the tiered penalty schedule. The Judiciary incurs $33,596 in FY 2026 computer programming expenditures and anticipates an increase in contested citation trials due to higher fines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary study workgroup convened by SHA to evaluate best practices, incident rates, and camera placement policies in school zones.
The State Highway Administration must submit the final study report and recommendations of the school zone speed monitoring workgroup to the Governor by December 1, 2025.
Under current statute governing speed monitoring systems, any local revenue remaining after cost recovery exceeding 10% of a jurisdiction's total revenue must be remitted to the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill reestablishes a mandated annual state appropriation of $3,700,000 for the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Providers of therapeutic child care and early childhood education, as well as children under the age of six with developmental delays, physical disabilities, or delays in social, emotional, or behavioral functioning.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.2 million annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 to satisfy the mandated $3.7 million appropriation (as baseline outyear projections assumed $1.5 million in ongoing discretionary funding). There is no fiscal impact in FY 2026, and no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE administers the Therapeutic Child Care Grant Program and is responsible for awarding the grants each year according to the statutory funding formula.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning, and this bill establishes a statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $3.7 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include a $3.7 million appropriation to the Program in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to disqualify an individual from driving a commercial motor vehicle for one year if the individual holds a commercial driver's license or commercial instructional permit and drives or attempts to drive any motor vehicle with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial driver's license (CDL) and commercial instructional permit holders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. Reprogramming and procedural changes can be absorbed with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) disqualify commercial driver's license (CDL) or commercial learner's permit holders from operating commercial motor vehicles for one year if they drive any motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 or greater.
As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT requested this departmental legislation and oversees state transportation policies and CDL compliance with federal standards.
Administrative Law Judges at the OAH adjudicate administrative per se driver's license hearings and appeals resulting from chemical test failures and MVA disqualification actions.
The Maryland State Police enforces impaired driving statutes, conducts chemical testing, and submits test results and administrative paperwork to the MVA that trigger disqualification actions.
The state court system handles underlying drunk driving citations and transmits conviction records that interface with MVA driver licensing and commercial driver disqualification records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes towing companies and police departments that impound, remove, or take custody of abandoned or towed vehicles to provide required notifications to the registered vehicle owner electronically through the Motor Vehicle Administration, provided certified mail notice follows if the owner does not respond within seven days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Vehicle owners whose vehicles are towed or impounded, towing companies, police departments, and vehicle insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Motor Vehicle Administration will develop a web portal for electronic notifications and plans to charge a nominal fee to towers to completely offset development and maintenance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency charged with adopting regulations, sending electronic notices to vehicle owners using email addresses in its records, and developing/maintaining the web portal and insurer database.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a principal modal administration of the Department of Transportation, and the bill amends the Transportation Article regarding vehicle towing, abandoned vehicle processing, and electronic notice.

As a primary law enforcement agency taking abandoned vehicles into custody, the Maryland State Police is directly authorized under the bill to utilize the MVA's electronic notification mechanism to notify vehicle owners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to develop a comprehensive plan by July 1, 2026, to establish Restorative Practices Schools, provide technical assistance upon request, and submit a report on the plan to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Local school boards that choose to establish a Restorative Practices School are required to follow the comprehensive plan.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, school administrators, and local boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2026 for contractual services to support stakeholder engagement and development of the comprehensive plan. State revenues are not affected. Local school system revenues and expenditures are not directly affected, as establishing restorative practices schools is discretionary for local boards, though existing schools may experience operational adjustments to align with the plan.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing the comprehensive plan for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools, consulting stakeholders, establishing model training materials and standards, providing technical assistance to county boards, and submitting a report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Governor's Office receives the required report from the Maryland State Department of Education regarding the comprehensive plan for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools by December 1, 2026, as well as the annual student discipline data report.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the timeframe within which the State Board of Elections must send written pre-election confirmation notices to voters on the permanent absentee ballot list, establishing that notices must be sent between 120 and 90 days prior to an election. It also adjusts the requirement for attempting to reach a voter through an alternative communication method if the voter cannot be reached using their selected method.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters on the permanent absentee ballot list
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the State Board of Elections (SBE). It directly governs SBE's statutory obligations and timeline for contacting and confirming voter information for individuals on the permanent absentee ballot list prior to elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits sellers from advertising or offering digital goods for sale using terms that suggest unrestricted ownership unless the seller provides a clear and conspicuous disclosure or obtains an affirmative acknowledgment from the buyer that only a license is being acquired. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers of digital media and software, as well as digital retailers, publishers, and platforms offering digital goods for purchase or licensing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can enforce the bill's provisions using existing resources, and the application of existing penalties will not yield a significant financial effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Consumer Protection Act through its Consumer Protection Division. The bill establishes that advertising or offering digital goods without required ownership/license disclosures is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to civil enforcement by the division.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judicial Branch, which would adjudicate any civil enforcement actions, injunctions, or civil penalties pursued under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act for violations of this digital goods disclosure statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a duplicative statutory provision requiring county governments, local school systems, and local health departments to create or update a cybersecurity preparedness and response plan and complete an assessment, resolving redundancy with an identical requirement preserved elsewhere in state law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: County governments, local school systems, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is technical in nature and simply eliminates a redundant requirement that remains codified in another section of state law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 209 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to repeal a duplicative statutory provision regarding local government cybersecurity preparedness and response plans under Title 3.5 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill codifies the Maryland Assistive Technology Program within the Maryland Department of Disabilities to provide assistive technology devices and services to individuals with disabilities. It also establishes the Assistive Technology Services Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to receive revenues generated from program services—such as assistive technology assessments and digital accessibility trainings—and support the program's operations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities of all ages, their families, caregivers, support providers, educators, employers, and local government entities utilizing assistive technology services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $25,000 in FY 2026 from fee-for-service activities, growing to $38,300 by FY 2030; special fund expenditures increase correspondingly to support program operations. General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 due to interest earnings credited to the General Fund before shifting to the special fund in FY 2029. Existing federal funding of approximately $1.3 million continues. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to the extent local entities purchase program services or training.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Maryland Assistive Technology Program and the Assistive Technology Services Fund within the Department of Disabilities, making it the primary implementing agency responsible for operating the program and administering the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Assistive Technology Services Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Assistive Technology Services Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale, offer for sale, transfer, or distribution of non-arc-resistant jacketed corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST) that does not meet specified standards, establishes a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for violations, and establishes a penalty for using non-compliant tubing in certain fuel gas piping systems. It also directs the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal to conduct a study and report recommendations on mitigating fire hazards related to fuel gas piping systems.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufacturers, retailers, wholesalers, and distributors of CSST and fuel gas piping systems; plumbers and construction contractors; residential and commercial property owners; and local gas fitting inspectors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,983 in FY 2026 and $22,124 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a contractual engineer to conduct the required study and submit interim and final reports through October 2026. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Local governments can consult on the study using existing resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is one of the primary agencies tasked with implementing the bill. It is co-responsible with the Office of the State Fire Marshal for conducting a comprehensive study on fuel gas piping fire hazards, hiring a contractual engineer, and submitting interim and final reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are entities within the Department of State Police. The Office of the State Fire Marshal is explicitly mandated to co-lead the study, consult with the commission, and formulate safety recommendations and reports.

The bill mandates that the Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal submit both an interim report and a final report on their findings and recommendations directly to the Governor.

The bill creates civil penalties of up to $1,000 for unlawful sales, distribution, or installation of non-compliant tubing, which are adjudicated through the District Court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 225 modifies regulations for exceptional hauling permits for farm products. It permits vehicles carrying fluid milk products under an exceptional hauling permit to operate on the interstate highway system, updates weight limits and axle requirements while removing weight limit tolerances, revises preventive maintenance inspection documentation standards, and gives the State Highway Administration discretion over permit revocations for weight violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Farmers, dairy haulers, agricultural producers, and commercial motor carriers transporting farm products in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund revenues are expected to increase starting in FY 2026 due to additional permit applications, though the total increase is not expected to be significant and specific dollar estimates cannot be reliably determined. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill with existing resources. State and local highway preservation and maintenance expenditures may experience minimal long-term impacts resulting from changes to vehicle weight limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is the primary implementing agency under the bill, responsible for issuing, regulating, monitoring, suspending, and revoking exceptional hauling permits for farm and milk products, as well as conducting record audits and adopting regulations.

The bill is a departmental initiative sponsored by MDOT, which oversees the State Highway Administration and administers the Transportation Trust Fund into which exceptional hauling permit fees accrue.

The State Highway Administration must adopt implementing regulations in consultation with the Secretary of State Police, and Maryland State Police officers and authorized civilian employees are empowered to confiscate exceptional hauling permits for significant weight violations.
Maryland Transportation Authority Police officers are authorized under the bill to confiscate exceptional hauling permits when vehicles violate weight restrictions by more than 5,000 pounds.

The bill modifies hauling parameters and weight limits specifically for farm products (as defined in the Agriculture Article) and fluid milk products, directly affecting agricultural producers and commodity transport.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to operate all public schools within the county using an alternative scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days and allows for fewer than 180 school days, provided that minimum attendance hour requirements are met. It requires the board to offer hourly employees the opportunity to make up lost wages and submit annual reports to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County public school students, parents and families, teachers, and hourly school employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. There is no direct fiscal effect on Anne Arundel County, as the bill is authorizing in nature; if Anne Arundel County Public Schools implements an alternative schedule, it can do so using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts public school calendar and attendance standards governed by Maryland education laws and State Board of Education regulations (COMAR), and requires the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to submit annual reports on the alternative scheduling model to the State Board of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts unclaimed capital credits owed to past members of electric cooperatives from being classified as abandoned property under State law, allowing cooperatives to retain these nonescheat capital credits to assist cooperative members or make donations to approved charitable organizations, provided past members may still claim their refunds upon application.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric cooperatives, past and current electric cooperative members, and nonprofit charitable organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Unclaimed Property Fund) and general fund revenues may decrease by an indeterminate amount because nonescheat capital credits will no longer be remitted to the State as presumed abandoned property. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's unclaimed/abandoned property program. Because the bill exempts certain nonescheat capital credits held by electric cooperatives from being presumed abandoned, those funds will no longer be reported and transferred to the Comptroller, resulting in a potential reduction in revenues for the Unclaimed Property Fund and General Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the scope of the Maryland Veterans Trust and the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to provide grants, loans, and other monetary assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Veterans Trust (staffed by the Department of Veterans and Military Families)
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard and their families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State nonbudgeted expenditures from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 as additional grants and loans are distributed. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Veterans and Military Families staffs the Maryland Veterans Trust, administers the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund, and processes the grant and loan applications expanded under this bill to include National Guard members.

The bill directly benefits members of the Maryland National Guard and their families by making them eligible to receive loans, grants, and monetary assistance from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund during temporary financial difficulties.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General requested this departmental legislation to ensure support and financial relief resources are accessible for Maryland National Guard personnel and their families.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland Public Ethics Law by removing the minimum two-hour requirement for ethics training courses provided by the State Ethics Commission, clarifying that trainings may be conducted online or via live presentations, and expanding financial disclosure requirements to report any source of compensated employment rather than only salaried employment for individuals and their immediate family members.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: State officials, public officials, candidates for State office, regulated lobbyists, and local ethics authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none, as the State Ethics Commission can implement the bill using existing budgetary resources. Local fiscal impact is minimal, primarily involving potential updates to local ethics laws to conform with the financial disclosure revisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 230 is a departmental bill requested by the State Ethics Commission. It directly amends the requirements for ethics training programs administered by the Commission for public officials and regulated lobbyists, providing flexibility in format and duration, and modifies the employment reporting requirements on financial disclosure statements overseen by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 235 revises Maryland's cybersecurity governance framework by reallocating and clarifying duties between the Department of Information Technology's Office of Security Management and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management's Cyber Preparedness Unit. Specifically, it transfers responsibility for assisting local governments with cyber vulnerability assessments to the Office of Security Management, updates the duties of the Secretary of Information Technology regarding statewide cybersecurity strategy implementation, and establishes a separate January annual reporting requirement for cybersecurity expenditures and budget recommendations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology (including the Office of Security Management) and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (including the Cyber Preparedness Unit)
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, local governments, local school boards, local school systems, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the bill's requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 235 directly alters the statutory responsibilities of the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), its Secretary, and the Office of Security Management (OSM). It transfers specific cybersecurity assessment support responsibilities from MDEM to DoIT, clarifies threat mitigation authority on the State network, and modifies annual reporting requirements.

The bill directly modifies the statutory duties of the Cyber Preparedness Unit within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), transferring certain vulnerability assessment responsibilities to DoIT and updating requirements related to cybersecurity training and local plan development.

The bill requires DoIT's Office of Security Management to submit two annual reports directly to the Governor concerning cybersecurity activities, preparedness, multi-year state expenditures on cybersecurity, and budget recommendations.
The Maryland National Guard is specifically designated to coordinate with MDEM and DoIT in conducting regional cybersecurity preparedness exercises as necessary.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal harassment statute to prohibit visual surveillance of an area of another person's residence where the person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, provided it is done with the intent to harass, alarm, or annoy, without legal purpose, and after a warning to stop. It also expands the relief a court may order under a final peace order to include requiring the respondent to remove or reposition a visual surveillance device within 15 days and refrain from further visual surveillance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing nonconsensual visual surveillance of their residences, individuals accused of visual surveillance or harassment, and the state court system.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $29,600 in FY 2026 only for the Judiciary to make programming adjustments to update relief options for peace orders. State revenues and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the relief that can be granted in peace orders, requiring the Judiciary to implement programming and software updates to interim, temporary, and final peace order forms at an estimated cost of $29,600 in FY 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the misdemeanor offense of criminal harassment to include certain visual surveillance of a residence, which carries penalties of imprisonment and falls under the purview of public defender representation for indigent defendants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Secretary of State to suspend or waive late filing fees for charitable organizations under specified regulations or settlement agreements, clarifies that these late fees are not delinquent accounts requiring referral to the Central Collection Unit, and establishes procedures for canceling and reinstating charitable organization registrations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Charitable organizations operating or soliciting contributions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances, as the provisions regarding the suspension or waiver of late fees conform statutory law to the Secretary of State's existing practice. The bill has no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the Secretary of State's oversight of charitable organizations, authorizing the agency to waive or suspend late fees, adopt implementing regulations, and cancel or reinstate charitable registrations.

The bill specifies that late fees assessed against charitable organizations are not delinquent accounts requiring referral to the Central Collection Unit (CCU), a unit administered under the Department of Budget and Management.

The Office of the Attorney General coordinates with the Secretary of State on charitable enforcement and receives funding support from the Charitable Enforcement Fund, which is financed through charitable organization fees addressed in this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill specifies that 'spouse' includes a former spouse regarding confidential marital communications and establishes that a spouse who is the alleged victim is competent to disclose confidential communications between the spouses in a criminal case where one spouse is charged with a crime against the other. It also specifies that an alleged victim spouse may not be compelled to testify.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary and State courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Spouses and former spouses involved in criminal cases involving crimes committed against a spouse, crime victims, criminal defendants, prosecutors, and defense counsel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural and is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the marital communications privilege in criminal court proceedings by allowing an alleged victim spouse to disclose confidential spousal communications. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch where these evidentiary rules and proceedings are administered.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters criminal trial evidence rules regarding spousal privilege when one spouse is charged with a crime against the other, which impacts the defense strategies and litigation handled by public defenders representing indigent defendants.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals where statutory evidentiary privileges and trial court admissibility decisions under § 9-105 are litigated.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland adoption law when the prospective adoptee is an adult by eliminating requirements for parental consent, issuance of a show-cause order to biological parents, and mandatory spousal joinder in the adoption petition. It also restricts pre-ruling court investigations in adult adoption cases to instances where good cause is shown.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Adult adoptees, petitioners seeking to adopt an adult, spouses of petitioners, and biological parents of prospective adult adoptees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters judicial procedures in independent adoption cases involving adult adoptees, including removing mandatory spousal joinder, eliminating parental show-cause order and consent requirements, and limiting court-ordered investigations to circumstances where good cause is shown.

The Department of Human Services oversees state adoption policies and family services under the Family Law Article; this bill streamlines independent adult adoptions and removes certain notice and investigation requirements that may involve the department or child placement agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permits the disclosure of Adult Protective Services records and reporter identities to government investigators conducting official investigations. It also authorizes mandatory reporters to report suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults through the statewide reporting hotline, and expands the definition of 'health practitioner' under mandatory reporting laws to include certain emergency medical services personnel, excluding emergency medical dispatchers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, Adult Protective Services investigators, law enforcement and government investigative personnel, and emergency medical services providers designated as mandatory reporters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. State and local entities involved in investigations regarding vulnerable adults may experience operational efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS requested this departmental bill and oversees the Adult Protective Services (APS) program and local departments of social services that investigate allegations of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and certifies emergency medical services providers under § 13-516 of the Education Article, who are now brought under the definition of 'health practitioner' and designated as mandatory reporters for vulnerable adult maltreatment.
The Department of Aging advocates for older and vulnerable adults, coordinates with local APS offices during investigations, and was a primary informational source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
MDH regulates health occupations and public health agencies whose personnel are mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse under the Health Occupations Article.
State law enforcement officers investigate crimes involving vulnerable adult abuse and exploitation and are authorized to receive disclosed APS information necessary for official investigations.
The Judiciary and court system process court orders permitting disclosure of records and adjudicate related legal proceedings regarding vulnerable adults.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits counties and municipalities from enforcing local laws or ordinances that establish a threshold of emergency or police calls as grounds for designating a residential property as a nuisance, or that penalize residential property owners, operators, or tenants for summoning law enforcement or emergency services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local governments (counties and municipalities) and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants, property owners, owner-occupants, rental property operators, and local governments and emergency responders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 249 establishes legal defenses and affirmative claims that tenants, operators, and property owners can bring in court against local jurisdictions attempting to enforce prohibited nuisance laws, allowing courts to award damages, attorney's fees, and other relief.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the frequency of financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services conducted or contracted by the Department of Human Services Office of the Inspector General from at least once every three years to an interval of four years, while permitting three-year audits on a case-by-case basis based on risk and prior audit findings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Inspector General in the Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Local departments of social services, local boards and governing authorities, and personnel within the Department of Human Services Office of the Inspector General.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Any operational efficiencies are not anticipated to materially impact State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 251 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services. It directly alters the statutory timeframe and risk-based criteria that the DHS Office of the Inspector General uses to conduct or contract for financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory termination (sunset) dates for several health occupations licensing boards under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act: the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists to July 1, 2031; the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to July 1, 2031; the State Board of Pharmacy to July 1, 2030; and the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists (including its Behavior Analyst Advisory Committee) to July 1, 2028. It also increases the membership of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners from seven to nine members by adding one licensed massage therapist and one consumer member.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, audiologists, hearing aid dispensers, speech-language pathologists, music therapists, professional counselors, behavior analysts, consumers, and regulated health occupations boards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No impact in FY 2025. Special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained for the affected boards through their respective extension years (FY 2028, FY 2030, and FY 2031). Beginning in FY 2026, special fund expenditures for the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners increase by $3,500 annually for per diems for two additional board members. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reauthorizes and extends the termination dates for several health occupations licensing boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health (including the State Board of Pharmacy, State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, and State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists) and alters the board composition of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners.

The bill expands the membership of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners from seven to nine members, requiring the Governor to appoint the additional licensed massage therapist and consumer members with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees for state boards, which includes the two newly established seats on the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the structure, powers, and governance of the West North Avenue Development Authority (WNADA) to align with a State economic development authority. It designates WNADA as a body politic and corporate and an instrumentality of the State, establishes the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund to support operations, grants extensive development, financing, and property acquisition powers, exempts the authority from certain state procurement and tax laws, requires it to become self-sustaining starting in fiscal year 2028, and extends its termination date to September 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, property owners, community organizations, and commercial businesses located within the West North Avenue Corridor and surrounding buffer zones in Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $82,614 in FY 2026 due to a contingent appropriation for personnel. Discretionary general fund expenditures may increase by at least $21.2 million and special fund expenditures by at least $260,000 in FY 2027 based on FY 2026 budget levels; however, the authority must be self-sustaining by FY 2028. State and local tax revenues may decrease due to WNADA exemptions from transfer, recordation, and property taxes, though long-term redevelopment may expand the tax base. Baltimore City local expenditures could increase if discretionary municipal contributions continue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The President of Coppin State University, an institution within the University System of Maryland, is designated by statute to serve as the Chair of the Board of Directors of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or their designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Authority's Board of Directors, and the bill aligns the Authority's powers and operating model with State economic development authorities.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a member of the Authority's Board of Directors, and the Authority's statutory mandate directly involves residential development and housing rehabilitation.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated to serve on the Authority's Board of Directors, supporting commercial development and business attraction along the corridor.
The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a member of the Board of Directors of the Authority to coordinate transportation and infrastructure revitalization along the corridor.
The bill establishes the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and administer statutory provisions exempting fund interest from General Fund sweeps.
The Governor is authorized to appoint a member to the Authority's Board of Directors and is authorized to include discretionary appropriations to the Authority in the annual state budget bill.

The bill impacts state budgeting and personnel administration by explicitly exempting the Authority from Title 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article and authorizing staff salaries outside the State Personnel and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters statewide DNA database system procedures by requiring DNA sample collection from registered sex offenders and mandating that custodial facilities ensure an individual's DNA sample is collected before release. It establishes specific legal determinations required before testing samples from charged individuals, criminalizes the refusal to submit a required DNA sample with a fine up to $1,000, and updates timelines and conditions for automatic destruction and expungement of DNA records.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of qualifying crimes, registered sex offenders, law enforcement agencies, correctional and booking facilities, and State's Attorney offices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected and requirements will be handled with existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are unaffected, and most local jurisdictions can handle implementation within existing resources, though Montgomery County estimated an expenditure increase of approximately $200,000 annually for additional correctional staff.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. MSP's Forensic Sciences Division (Crime Laboratory) administers the Statewide DNA Database System, establishes DNA collection regulations and training, handles the testing and backlog of DNA samples, and executes expungements and destruction of records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates state correctional facilities and supervising authorities. The bill requires correctional facilities and custodial agencies to collect DNA samples at intake, verify collection before releasing individuals from custody, and collect samples upon sex offender registration.

The bill establishes that DNA testing and entry into the database depends on judicial or commissioner probable cause determinations, arrest warrants, or indictments in District and Circuit Courts, and impacts court expungement notices and sentencing procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants whose DNA may be collected, tested, or expunged under the altered statutory standards, and defends individuals facing new misdemeanor charges and fines for refusing to provide required DNA samples.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill reduces the penalties for offenses related to the use, possession, delivery, or sale of drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia. For subsequent drug paraphernalia offenses, maximum penalties are lowered from two years imprisonment and/or a $2,000 fine to one year imprisonment and/or a $1,000 fine. For controlled paraphernalia violations, penalties are reduced from up to four years imprisonment and/or a $25,000 fine to a maximum fine of $500 for a first offense and up to one year imprisonment and/or a $1,000 fine for subsequent offenses. It also removes the prohibition on possessing controlled paraphernalia to illegally administer a controlled dangerous substance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia offenses, law enforcement officers, state prosecutors, and public defenders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. While maximum fines are reduced, District and Circuit Court revenues are not significantly impacted due to a historically low number of convictions. Similarly, State and local incarceration expenditures are not materially affected. Caseload reductions for the Office of the Public Defender and operational time savings for local law enforcement from issuing citations instead of arrests are expected to be redirected to other cases and duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reduces penalties for drug and controlled paraphernalia offenses and makes a first-time violation of § 5-620 a fine-only offense. Because the Office of the Public Defender only provides representation in cases where incarceration is possible, the bill directly reduces or alters OPD caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Division of Correction and the Division of Parole and Probation, which receive individuals convicted of and sentenced for drug paraphernalia offenses. The reduction of maximum incarceration terms impacts potential sentence lengths and supervision requirements.
The Maryland Judiciary handles the charging, adjudication, and sentencing for misdemeanor violations under Criminal Law §§ 5-619 and 5-620 across the District and Circuit Courts.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing state criminal laws, MSP troopers investigate CDS paraphernalia offenses and will have to issue criminal citations rather than effectuate arrests for first-time § 5-620 violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prioritizes the payment of unpaid child support owed by a deceased individual when an estate has insufficient assets to pay all claims in full, placing child support claims directly after family allowances and ahead of taxes owed by the decedent and other lower-priority claims.
qa_results.responsible_party: Personal representatives of decedents' estates and the Registers of Wills
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and families owed unpaid child support, decedents' estates and personal representatives, and creditors of estates (including small businesses and state and local government entities)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government revenues may decrease to the extent that placing unpaid child support higher in the priority list results in lower-priority government claims—such as unpaid taxes or Public Assistance to Adults program reimbursements—going unpaid or receiving smaller disbursements. The decrease cannot be reliably estimated but is expected to be limited. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills oversees the administration of decedents' estates and probate proceedings, which includes ensuring that personal representatives pay valid claims against insolvent estates according to the statutory order of priority.

DHS administers child support enforcement services and the Public Assistance to Adults (PAA) program. The bill elevates unpaid child support claims above several categories, while pushing PAA reimbursement claims down in priority.

The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state taxes. The bill places unpaid child support claims above taxes due by the decedent, potentially reducing state tax recoveries from insolvent estates.
The Maryland Judiciary adjudicates estate disputes, claims against estates, and child support judgments, and may see procedural impacts in estate and child support proceedings.
