agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the state's health occupations boards, including the State Board of Nursing and the State Board of Pharmacy, which are directly required to implement the bill's changes regarding English proficiency standards, website disclosures, and nursing licensure by endorsement.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory termination date for the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, thereby making the authority and its neighborhood revitalization functions in Prince George's County permanent.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority (in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development and supported by the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and businesses in the target area municipalities of Prince George's County (the cities of Mount Rainier and Bladensburg, and the towns of Brentwood, Cottage City, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, nor Prince George's County operations or finances, as there is no statutory funding mandate for the authority.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, and the Authority operates in consultation with the department. Repealing the sunset makes these responsibilities permanent.

Under the Economic Development Article, the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, a role made permanent by the repeal of the termination date.
The Prince George's Gateway Development Authority is statutorily required to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 375 (Jay's Law) permits individuals to ride bicycles, play vehicles, or unicycles on sidewalks or sidewalk areas unless prohibited by a local ordinance. It also requires operators of these vehicles on sidewalks or in crosswalks to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and individuals using electric personal assistive mobility devices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Bicyclists, unicyclists, operators of play vehicles, pedestrians, and users of electric personal assistive mobility devices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may see a potential minimal decrease to the extent that fewer citations are issued. State and local law enforcement can handle enforcement with existing resources. Local governments can review and update local ordinances with existing resources, with no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article regarding the operation of bicycles, play vehicles, and unicycles on sidewalks and crosswalks, directly impacting the department's statewide transportation policy and pedestrian/bicycle safety regulations.
The MVA administers driver licensing and records, including assessing points against driving privileges when sidewalk driving or right-of-way violations occur under the Maryland Vehicle Law.
MDOT SHA designs, constructs, and maintains sidewalks, crosswalks, and pedestrian/bicycle facilities along state highways where these rules of the road and right-of-way requirements will apply.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law, MSP officers are responsible for enforcing bicycle and pedestrian right-of-way statutes and issuing citations.

The District Court processes traffic citations, establishes prepayment penalties, and adjudicates violations relating to the unlawful operation of vehicles on sidewalks and failure to yield right-of-way.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership and leadership structure of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council, establishing biennial elections for a chair and vice chair (one State employee and one non-State employee). It also expands the Council's duties to assess and address cybersecurity threats and privacy risks associated with artificial intelligence and quantum computing across critical infrastructure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cybersecurity Council
qa_results.stakeholders: State residents, cybersecurity businesses, higher education institutions, critical infrastructure providers (energy, water, banking, and healthcare), and state and federal cybersecurity agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Any reimbursements for additional Council members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgets. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership, leadership structure, and statutory duties of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council, an executive advisory and coordinating body.

Under current law, the Attorney General or designee chairs the Maryland Cybersecurity Council; the bill alters the chair structure to an elected position and maintains the Attorney General's council membership.

The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the council, and the agency is directly impacted by the council's expanded duties concerning artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and critical cyber infrastructure.
The bill explicitly adds the People's Counsel, or their designee, as a designated member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.

The bill explicitly designates multiple USM institution leaders (including the presidents of Bowie State, UMB, UMBC, and UMCP, the Dean of UMGC's cybersecurity school, and two appointments by the Chancellor) as council members. UMGC also historically staffs the council.
The bill explicitly designates the President of Morgan State University, or their designee, as a member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Chief Executive Officer of TEDCO, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of Emergency Management, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council and provided information for the fiscal note.
The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security, or their designee, is a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The State Administrator of Elections, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of State Police, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Adjutant General, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of Commerce, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and was consulted as an information source regarding the changes to executive council structures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to assess 12 points against the driver's license of an individual convicted of repeat drunk or drugged driving violations under § 21-902(h) or § 21-902(i) of the Transportation Article, subjecting their license to revocation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers convicted of repeat drunk or drugged driving offenses in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency directly responsible for assessing the 12 points on drivers' licenses following convictions under § 21-902(h) and (i) and issuing corresponding license revocations.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees vehicle laws, driver licensing administration, and highway safety policy.

The Judiciary processes subsequent offender drunk and drugged driving criminal convictions under the Transportation Article, which must then be transmitted to the Motor Vehicle Administration for points assessment.

Individuals subject to license revocation resulting from the accumulation of 12 points have the right to request an administrative hearing, which is typically adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill exempts personal property used in connection with large family child care homes from property valuation and taxation. It also expands eligibility for optional local real property tax credits to include large family child care homes, eliminates previous construction completion date requirements for eligibility, and increases or establishes the maximum local real property tax credit limit at $10,000 per year.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators and owners of registered large family child care homes, family child care homes, licensed child care centers, adult and elderly day care centers, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease minimally starting in FY 2026 due to the personal property tax exemption for large family child care homes (estimated at approximately $7,500 annually in Worcester County) and to the extent local jurisdictions authorize, expand eligibility for, or increase the value of real property tax credits up to the new $10,000 cap. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands property tax exemptions and local tax credit eligibility for family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers registered or licensed under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, which is administered and regulated by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE also tracks licensing data for these facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act authorizes county governing bodies to exempt rental housing real property from county property taxes if the property owner enters into a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreement. Under the agreement, the owner must agree to pay a negotiated amount and maintain at least 25% of the rental units as affordable dwelling units for at least 15 years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties
qa_results.stakeholders: Rental property owners, developers, low-income tenants earning 60% or less of area median income, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal year 2026 to the extent that eligible rental properties are granted property tax exemptions, though any reduction will be mitigated by negotiated PILOT payments. Specific dollar estimates are indeterminate and depend on the number and assessed value of participating properties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes statutory criteria for affordable rental housing payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements to incentivize and preserve affordable housing units, which directly aligns with DHCD's primary mission of expanding and supporting affordable rental housing throughout Maryland.

The bill references definitions codified in the Land Use Article regarding affordable dwelling units and area median income; while the department has no direct administrative mandate under the bill, it provides land use guidance and data to local jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program administered by MARBIDCO by increasing the maximum loan amount from $10,000 to $25,000 per seasonal full-time job projected to be created or retained, and by reducing the eligibility requirement for licensed seafood dealers from five years of licensure to three years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed seafood dealers, oyster processing facilities and shucking houses, and seasonal or full-time seafood industry workers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted expenditures and subsequent revenues for MARBIDCO increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that expanding eligibility and loan limits increases lending activity under the program, which currently has $750,000 in available funds remaining from a prior appropriation. The bill does not alter State general fund appropriations, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing agency for the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program. The bill directly alters MARBIDCO's loan terms by increasing the allowable loan amount per seasonal full-time job to $25,000 and expanding applicant eligibility by lowering the seafood dealer licensing tenure requirement.

DNR oversees the licensing of seafood dealers and tidal fish license holders who are eligible for the program, and acts as the receiving and verifying entity for oyster shells and spat-on-shell plantings tied to statutory loan forgiveness.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the higher education scholarship awarded to a student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education who completes a full term from $8,000 to $15,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Student members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education who complete a full term
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund the increased scholarship award. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the scholarship compensation for the student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education. The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school boards, though the bill has no state fiscal impact and solely affects local county expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the appointment process for licensed hearing aid dispenser members of the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists by requiring the Board, rather than an external professional society, to notify all licensed hearing aid dispensers in Maryland of vacancies and submit a list of nominees to the Secretary of Health and the Governor.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed hearing aid dispensers in Maryland, members of the Board, and the Hearing Society of Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Delaware.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is a health occupations board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and the Secretary of Health provides advice to the Governor regarding board appointments.
The Governor is statutorily responsible for appointing the hearing aid dispenser members to the board from the list submitted by the board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in administering appointments to state boards and commissions, including vetting candidates and processing board vacancies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the part-time deputy chief inspector employed by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from $9,000 to $18,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: The part-time deputy chief inspector for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $9,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to fund the salary increase. Local revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates chromite as the official State mineral of Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: State of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents, educators, historians, and geologists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Designating a State mineral does not materially affect State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is responsible for documenting official State symbols and maintaining the Maryland Manual On-Line, which catalogues official designations such as the State mineral. It was also the primary information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Local Boards of Elections Transparency Act, requiring each local board of elections to post open meeting agendas and related voting materials online at least 48 hours in advance (or as soon as practicable during emergencies), provide live video streaming of open meetings, and maintain unedited archived recordings for at least five years.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections and Maryland local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, members of the public seeking access to local election administration proceedings, and local boards of elections across Maryland counties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local government expenditures increase for counties whose local election boards do not currently possess the technology or infrastructure to live stream and archive meetings for five years. Reported local one-time equipment and installation costs range from approximately $5,300 to $25,000, along with recurring annual streaming, licensing, or storage fees ranging from $250 to $2,000 for certain counties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 412 directly tasks the State Board of Elections with adopting regulations by December 1, 2025, to ensure the uniform implementation of enhanced open meeting and live video streaming requirements across all local boards of elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 413 allows individuals 21 years of age and older to manufacture personal use amounts of cannabis products or concentrated cannabis at home without the use of volatile solvents. It establishes reduced penalties and removes mandatory minimums for cannabis-related volume dealer and drug kingpin offenses, while establishing that non-cannabis volume dealer offenses are felonies. In addition, the bill allows certain incarcerated individuals serving mandatory minimum sentences for cannabis or cocaine base offenses to apply for sentence reductions, and reclassifies several firearms-related offenses from misdemeanors to felonies with increased penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals aged 21 and older producing personal use cannabis, individuals incarcerated or facing charges for volume dealer or drug kingpin offenses involving cannabis or cocaine base, individuals charged with illegal firearm trafficking, manufacturing, or possession of stolen/unserialized firearms, public defenders, prosecutors, and state correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Public Defender increase by up to $95,726 in FY 2026 (and up to $130,500 by FY 2030) to hire one assistant public defender to handle increased workloads from sentence modification applications. Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services expenditures and overall state revenues are not materially affected, though minimal fine revenue shifts may occur between the District Court and circuit courts. Local State's Attorneys' offices and circuit courts may experience minor operational impacts from processing and hearing sentence modification motions, but no material local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of the Public Defender by authorizing incarcerated individuals to file applications for sentence modifications and reductions for certain cannabis and cocaine base offenses, leading to increased attorney caseloads and an estimated general fund expenditure increase of $95,700 to $130,500 annually.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters criminal penalties, eliminates mandatory minimums for cannabis volume dealers and drug kingpins, establishes sentence modification procedures for currently incarcerated individuals, and creates felony incarceration penalties for certain firearms offenses, impacting inmate populations and term lengths under DPSCS custody.

The bill requires Maryland courts to process applications and conduct hearings for sentence modifications, while also shifting caseloads between District Court and Circuit Court due to the reclassification of various firearm offenses to felonies and certain cannabis volume dealer offenses to misdemeanors.

The bill alters criminal classifications and penalties for firearms offenses under Title 5 of the Public Safety Article, which includes provisions governing handgun rosters, serial number marking, and regulated firearms trafficking overseen and enforced by the Maryland State Police.

The bill amends statutory thresholds and criminal provisions regarding the manufacturing of cannabis products and concentrated cannabis for personal use and adult sharing, which aligns with the broader regulatory framework overseen by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for Maryland's criminal justice policies and public safety strategies, the agency is affected by substantive changes to sentencing laws, mandatory minimums, and firearms offense penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 415 establishes the Family Literacy Pilot Program, administered by the Maryland State Library Agency in consultation with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Correctional Education Council. The program provides children's books to incarcerated individuals at four selected State correctional facility libraries or prerelease centers and enables them to record themselves reading aloud, distributing the book and recording to their children free of charge.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in participating Maryland correctional facilities and prerelease centers, along with their children and custodial parents or guardians.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $69,200 in FY 2026, $70,800 in FY 2027, $73,800 in FY 2028, and $38,500 in FY 2029 to support one contractual program administrator within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services as well as supplies, books, and recording equipment for the Maryland State Library Agency. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the primary administrator of the newly established Family Literacy Pilot Program, tasked with selecting books, developing program processes, and submitting a final report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is required to consult on the program's establishment, host the pilot program across four of its correctional facilities or prerelease centers, and incurs fiscal costs for contractual personnel to administer the program on-site.

The Correctional Education Council, which is required to consult on the selection of facilities and implementation processes for the pilot program, is housed under the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Correctional Education Council, an advisory and governing body under joint jurisdiction of MD Labor and DPSCS, is specifically mandated by the bill to consult on selecting facilities and designing the literacy pilot program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces the term 'auto-injectable epinephrine' with 'emergency use epinephrine' across the Education, Health - General, and Health Occupations articles of the Maryland Code, expanding authorization to cover FDA-approved non-injectable epinephrine delivery devices and products (such as nasal sprays). It also renames the Emergency Use Auto-Injectable Epinephrine Program to the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program and extends legal protections and protocols to non-injectable emergency epinephrine use in schools, youth camps, child care facilities, and participating food service facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals experiencing severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), public and nonpublic school staff and students, youth camp operators and attendees, child care providers, higher education and food service facilities, and healthcare professionals authorized to prescribe or dispense epinephrine.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can update existing program regulations, procedures, and materials using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program for youth camps and the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program for participating facilities. MDH is responsible for issuing certificates, collecting incident reports, and updating regulations and materials to incorporate newly approved FDA non-injectable epinephrine products.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public school and child care policies under the Education Article amended by the bill, including developing and disseminating the standard reporting form for emergency epinephrine incidents in public schools and maintaining guidelines for child care settings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to cover expenditures for activities shared between the 9-1-1 emergency system and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline, such as software interfaces and joint training, while prohibiting 9-1-1 Trust Fund monies from being used for expenses that solely support the 9-8-8 hotline.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland 9-1-1 Board within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Emergency telecommunications personnel, 9-1-1 public safety answering points, 9-8-8 crisis response centers, and individuals using Maryland's emergency and crisis hotline services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the 9-1-1 Trust Fund will increase minimally to cover shared activities and projects; however, administrative efficiencies are expected and may decrease expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no material fiscal or operational impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and manages the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. The bill directly alters the statutory purposes of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to authorize expenditures for shared operations, software interfaces, and joint training between 9-1-1 systems and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline.

MDH administers the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline and the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. The bill allows joint 9-1-1 and 9-8-8 initiatives to be funded through the 9-1-1 Trust Fund, which creates operational efficiencies and may reduce expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to adopt regulations to implement and enforce their respective statutory responsibilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Emergency management personnel, 9-1-1 specialists and operators, local public safety answering points (PSAPs), local governments, and Maryland residents relying on 9-1-1 and emergency services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Emergency Management and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board can handle the regulatory responsibilities using existing budgeted resources, and local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 423 directly grants statutory regulatory authority to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which is housed within MDEM, allowing them to adopt regulations to implement and enforce their statutory responsibilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands and alters the authority of the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB) to establish upper payment limits (UPLs) for prescription drug products that present affordability challenges. It updates criteria for setting UPLs (including considerations for drug shortages, rare diseases, and 340B providers), expands the membership of the Stakeholder Council, establishes new reporting requirements on the market impact of UPLs, and creates a contingent process to expand UPLs to commercial purchases and payor reimbursements across the State if specified conditions are met by September 30, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Prescription drug consumers in Maryland, pharmaceutical manufacturers, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), health insurance carriers, wholesale distributors, retail and independent pharmacies, 340B covered entities, rare disease patients, and state/local government health programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General increase by $106,700 in FY 2026, rising to $146,300 by FY 2030 for an additional Assistant Attorney General. PDAB special fund expenditures and fee revenues increase by at least $264,900 in FY 2027 (and approximately $273,300 by FY 2030) for personnel and contractual services, funded through an increased annual assessment fee on pharmaceutical manufacturers, PBMs, carriers, and wholesale distributors. Local governments may realize minimal cost savings on prescription drug spending once UPLs take effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly increases general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) by $106,700 in FY 2026 and over $128,000 annually thereafter to hire a full-time Assistant Attorney General to provide legal advice, draft regulations, and defend against potential litigation regarding upper payment limits. Additionally, the Attorney General shares approval authority with the Governor over PDAB's plan of action if not approved by the Legislative Policy Committee.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill explicitly requires the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to confer with Medicaid before setting an upper payment limit applicable to the program to evaluate federal rebate compliance and state budget impacts.

DBM has a designated representative on the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council and administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, whose prescription drug purchasing and formularies are impacted by upper payment limits set by the Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition and membership of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council, adding representatives for the rare disease community, oncologists, and patient advocacy organizations.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members of the Stakeholder Council (including a new patient advocacy representative) and holds statutory authority to approve the Board's plan of action alongside the Attorney General if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve it.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and councils, including the newly added gubernatorial appointment to the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council.
The bill repeals obsolete statutory language requiring the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to repay start-up funds to the Maryland Health Care Commission, as repayment has been completed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts licensed auctioneers from the definition of a boat dealer under the State Boat Act when they act on behalf of a seller, secured party, or owner, provided title does not pass to the auctioneer and the auction is not intended to evade the provisions of the Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed auctioneers, vessel owners, secured parties and lienholders, and Maryland boat dealers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances and has no local effect. While boat dealers pay an annual $25 license fee, the Department of Natural Resources notes there are currently only eight auctioneers licensed as boat dealers, resulting in a negligible fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) administers the State Boat Act, which governs the licensing and regulation of boat dealers and the collection of vessel excise taxes. This bill alters the definition of 'dealer' under the Act to exempt certain licensed auctioneers, directly impacting DNR's licensing jurisdiction and regulatory oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 426 requires the State Board of Elections, in collaboration with local boards of elections, to conduct a postelection risk-limiting audit of at least one statewide contest and any other selected contests following each statewide election prior to certification. It also authorizes local boards to conduct risk-limiting audits of local contests, allows risk-limiting audits after special general elections, makes postelection automated software audits permissive rather than mandatory, and repeals the requirement for a separate manual audit after each statewide general election.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, local boards of elections, election staff, and candidates running in statewide and local contests.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,000 in FY 2026, $72,000 in FY 2027, and $51,000 in FY 2028 and future years to cover software fees and consultant support. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 due to personnel and operational costs to carry out the audits, though some savings may offset costs during general election years from the repeal of previous manual audit requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Elections (SBE), in collaboration with local boards, with implementing and conducting risk-limiting postelection tabulation audits following statewide elections. SBE must adopt regulations establishing criteria, audit methods, and risk limits, and the fiscal note outlines direct general fund expenditures incurred by SBE for software and consulting services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Public Accountancy to place an individual on emeritus status if they meet specified experience, age, and disciplinary standing requirements and attest to being retired. Licensees on emeritus status are exempt from continuing education requirements and reinstatement fees, may use the title "CPA Emeritus," but are prohibited from actively practicing certified public accountancy or offering related services unless properly reinstated.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
qa_results.stakeholders: Retired or long-serving certified public accountants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Public Accountancy are likely not materially affected, as the bill is assumed to apply in a limited number of cases. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is a regulatory licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Department of Labor is directly responsible for administering the new emeritus licensing status, processing applications, and issuing certificates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the creation of a lien on owner-occupied residential property by contract or as a result of a breach of contract for the payment of medical debt, and requires courts to remove any lien created in violation. Additionally, requires complaints for a money judgment to indicate whether the judgment sought is for medical debt and include the address of the defendant's primary residence.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers and homeowners with medical debt, health care providers, medical debt collectors, and the Maryland court system.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article by requiring complaints for money judgments to specify if the claim is for medical debt and include the defendant's primary residence, altering judgment lien indexing rules, and mandating that courts remove prohibited liens.
The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces laws regarding consumer protection, unfair debt collection practices, and medical debt enforcement.
The Maryland Department of Health regulates health care providers and facilities generating medical debt and enforces health care financing and billing-related standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes that any provision in a consumer contract that sets a shorter time limitation to bring an action than otherwise required under Maryland law is against public policy, illegal, and void. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, enforceable by civil remedies and penalties. The bill exempts certain regulated utility services, businesses operating under specific state/local authorizations, and licensed security system service providers, and applies prospectively to contracts entered into on or after the effective date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers entering into consumer contracts, as well as businesses that issue or enter into consumer contracts for personal, family, or household goods and services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that a violation of its provisions constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to the enforcement and penalty provisions under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article, which is administered and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill directly impacts civil judicial proceedings by mandating that courts shall not give effect to shortened limitation provisions in consumer contracts and barring defenses based on such provisions.
The bill explicitly exempts services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission from its consumer contract limitations prohibitions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides that the medical exemption allowing a vehicle to have enhanced tinted windows is valid indefinitely, rather than for up to two years, if a licensed physician determines that the owner's medical condition requiring sun protection is permanent.
qa_results.responsible_party: Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Vehicle owners with permanent medical conditions requiring enhanced window tinting, licensed physicians, and law enforcement officers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Department of State Police, which establishes the manner and format for written medical exemption certifications and enforces vehicle safety equipment repair orders for tinted windows.
The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law regarding equipment standards, preserving the Motor Vehicle Administrator's regulatory authority regarding vehicle windows.
MDOT is the parent agency overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and the implementation of state transportation and vehicle equipment laws.
The Judiciary and court system process and adjudicate traffic citations and safety equipment repair orders issued for window tint violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal prohibition against conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent by adding residences and other places of private use or accommodation to the definition of a protected "private place." It also clarifies that surreptitious camera surveillance of an individual's private areas without consent is illegal regardless of the person's location.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals whose privacy is protected in residences and private accommodations, victims of surreptitious surveillance, criminal offenders, law enforcement, and state and local correctional systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues may experience a minimal increase from fines assessed in the District Court and circuit courts (up to $2,500 per violation). State and local expenditures may experience a minimal increase due to expanded incarceration penalties of up to one year, with local detention per diem costs ranging from approximately $140 to $350 per incarcerated individual. Specific aggregate dollar figures are not specified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal liability for visual surveillance with prurient intent and maintains a civil cause of action, directly impacting caseloads, trial proceedings, and fine collection within Maryland District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill subjects offenders to penalties including up to one year of imprisonment and probation, impacting the Division of Correction, the Baltimore Pretrial Complex, and the Division of Parole and Probation for supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because violation of the statute carries a potential penalty of incarceration for up to one year, the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants charged under the expanded offense.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Criminal Law Article, the State Police is responsible for investigating allegations of illegal visual surveillance and enforcing criminal penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum limit on compensatory damages that may be awarded to a pet owner from a person who tortiously causes injury to or the death of a pet from $10,000 to $25,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary (State Court System)
qa_results.stakeholders: Pet owners, pet tortfeasors/defendants, and civil court litigants in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 438 amends Section 11-110 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article by increasing the maximum compensatory damages cap in civil tort actions involving the injury or death of a pet from $10,000 to $25,000, directly affecting civil case adjudications handled across Maryland's judicial branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the statutory hearsay exception for out-of-court statements by child victims and witnesses under the age of 13 to allow the admission of statements made to qualified forensic interviewers affiliated with child advocacy centers in certain criminal and juvenile court proceedings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Child victims and witnesses under age 13, forensic interviewers, child advocacy centers, prosecutors, criminal defendants, and juvenile respondents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural and is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the evidentiary rules governing the admissibility of out-of-court statements made by child victims and witnesses in criminal and juvenile court proceedings, requiring judges to conduct pre-trial hearings, examine witnesses, and evaluate guarantees of trustworthiness.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the hearsay exceptions under which statements can be admitted against defendants and juvenile respondents represented by public defenders, establishing specific notice and deposition procedures that defense counsel must navigate.

The bill impacts Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and child abuse/neglect proceedings, which are handled in coordination with local departments of social services under DHS and partner Child Advocacy Centers.
The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals, where challenges to evidentiary rulings and the admissibility of out-of-court statements under the tender years statute are frequently litigated.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statement required on baby food product labels tested for toxic heavy metals by changing the phrasing from "toxic heavy metal" testing to "toxic element" testing, aligning Maryland's labeling requirements with other jurisdictions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Baby food manufacturers, distributors, and consumers of baby food products.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact, as the bill pertains exclusively to private-sector activities. Any small business impact is minimal, as it aligns Maryland's labeling standards with California's.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article (§ 21-330.4) governing baby food testing and labeling. The Maryland Department of Health is the administering agency responsible for requesting test results from manufacturers and receiving consumer reports regarding non-compliant baby food products.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits committing unauthorized computer access and related cyber offenses with the intent to interrupt or impair the functioning of a public safety answering point (PSAP), establishing a felony penalty punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years, a maximum fine of $25,000, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, the Judiciary, and State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Public safety answering points (9-1-1 call centers), emergency dispatchers and first responders, individuals charged with cyber offenses, and the general public relying on emergency communications.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which coordinates policy, standards, and funding for public safety answering points (PSAPs) across the state. This bill creates criminal penalties for intentional cyber interference with PSAP operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for housing individuals convicted and sentenced under state felony provisions, including the new felony penalty of up to 5 years imprisonment established by this bill.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates cybercrimes, computer-related offenses, and unlawful interference with critical emergency response and public safety communications infrastructure.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judiciary, which will hear and adjudicate criminal prosecutions and civil suits arising under the bill's provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants who may be charged with the felony offense created by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program within the Department of Natural Resources to curb the spread of invasive blue catfish in the Chesapeake Bay and tributaries. The program authorizes eligible participants to conduct for-hire and commercial fishing trips simultaneously, permits the expanded use of finfish trotlines south of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, directs the department to consider gear and harvest practice modifications such as electrofishing and longer trotlines, and requires a report on findings and recommendations by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fishermen, for-hire fishing charter operators, seafood processors, and Maryland tidal fisheries businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources because it establishes programs the department is already in the process of implementing. There is no local government fiscal impact. Small commercial fishing and seafood processing businesses may experience a meaningful positive impact from increased catfish harvest opportunities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency tasked with establishing, administering, expanding, and reporting on the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Department of Natural Resources to establish the pilot program in coordination with the Invasive Catfish Advisory Committee.
The bill mandates that the Department of Natural Resources report its findings and recommendations regarding the pilot program directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates statutory references to alter the name of Arundel Habitat for Humanity, Inc. to Habitat for Humanity of the Chesapeake, Incorporated, and expands an optional Anne Arundel County and municipal property tax credit to cover any real property owned by the organization rather than two specific addresses.
qa_results.responsible_party: The governing body of Anne Arundel County and governing bodies of municipal corporations in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Habitat for Humanity of the Chesapeake, Incorporated, Anne Arundel County, and municipal corporations within Anne Arundel County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County and municipal property tax revenues will decrease to the extent that qualifying properties receive the tax credit, depending on assessed property values and credit terms established locally. Expenditures are not affected. Anne Arundel County reported no county property tax credits were granted under this provision in FY 2023 or FY 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Modernization of Military Laws Act updates and standardizes military-related definitions across Maryland law by referencing the U.S. Code, expanding classifications of uniformed services to include bodies such as the Public Health Service and NOAA. The act eliminates the state residency requirement for certain veterans seeking burial in State veterans' cemeteries, expands cemetery eligibility to qualified reserve members and their families, updates housing and employment discrimination protections, and requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to develop transition policies and annual reporting on service members.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterans, active service members, reserve component members, commissioned officers of the Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general and federal fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 due to additional burials at State veterans' cemeteries. Costs for burying non-resident veterans are reimbursed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Burials of qualified reserve members and their dependents require collection of a fee matching the federal plot allowance ($948 as of August 2024), offsetting those expenditures. General fund expenditures for newly eligible PHS and NOAA officers and certain dependents increase by an indeterminate amount because no fee is charged. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Veterans and Military Families as the primary implementing agency, expanding eligibility and altering fee structures for burial in State veterans' cemeteries, removing residency requirements for certain veterans, expanding annual reporting requirements, and requiring the Secretary to develop coordinated policies for service members and veterans undergoing life transitions.

The bill amends the Election Law Article regarding voter registration, absentee voting definitions, use of common access cards, and qualifications for filing certificates of candidacy remotely for members of the uniformed services.

The bill expands the definition of 'military status' under Title 20 of the State Government Article to include reserve components of the uniformed services (such as the Reserve Corps of the Public Health Service), expanding the protected class under state employment and housing anti-discrimination laws enforced by the Commission.

The bill amends statutory language governing the Governor's authority as commander-in-chief of the state militia relative to active service in the uniformed services and requires expanded reporting directly to the Governor regarding active service members.
The bill reenacts provisions governing the acquisition of land for State veterans' cemeteries, which requires the formal approval of the Board of Public Works.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transit Administration to automatically renew the Disability Reduced Fare Program certification of enrollees who are permanently disabled and to adopt regulations establishing an implementation process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Permanently disabled transit riders enrolled in the Maryland Transit Administration's Disability Reduced Fare Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Transit Administration can fulfill the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Transit Administration is the primary implementing agency directly mandated to automatically renew the Disability Reduced Fare Program certification for enrollees who are permanently disabled and adopt regulations to establish the renewal process.

The Maryland Transit Administration is a modal unit within the Maryland Department of Transportation, making the department directly responsible for the broader administration and oversight of the transit systems and policies affected by this legislation.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates state programs, policies, and services to advance accessible transportation for Marylanders with disabilities, and served as an informational resource during the evaluation of this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands existing restrictions on using State funds for permanent outdoor lighting to include lighting on the grounds of State parks and trails, while exempting lighting used for sports facility fields. It requires non-MDOT luminaires installed or replaced with State funds to have a correlated light temperature of 3,000 Kelvins or less (subject to Board of Public Works waivers), directs the Maryland Green Building Council to update or develop outdoor lighting guidance considering American Medical Association recommendations by October 1, 2026, and requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to review highway lighting practices by September 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Green Building Council, Board of Public Works, and Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies acquiring outdoor lighting, Maryland Department of Transportation, visitors to State buildings, parks, and trails, motorists, and outdoor lighting contractors and suppliers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to be materially affected due to existing waiver procedures and the prospective application of the bill. The Maryland Department of Transportation can conduct its review of highway lighting practices using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is explicitly tasked with conducting a review of highway lighting practices by September 30, 2026, considering alterations inconsistent with Federal Highway Administration guidelines. The bill also specifies unique statutory exemptions tailored to MDOT operations and equipment.

DGS provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Green Building Council, which is required to update or develop outdoor lighting guidance by October 1, 2026. DGS also manages state facilities, oversees state procurement of lighting, and exercises delegated waiver authority from the Board of Public Works.

The bill authorizes the Board of Public Works (or its designees) to establish waiver criteria and review and grant waivers for the new correlated color temperature and restricted uplight luminaire requirements.
The bill broadens the restrictions on using State funds for outdoor luminaires to explicitly encompass State parks and trails, which are owned, operated, and maintained by DNR.

As the MDOT administration responsible for state highways and roadway infrastructure, SHA will be directly involved in the required review of highway lighting practices under Federal Highway Administration standards.

The bill creates a specific statutory exemption from the lighting restrictions for luminaires used to illuminate the field of play at sports facilities, directly relevant to MSA's sports venue operations.

USM operates extensive campus grounds and outdoor facilities subject to State building lighting restrictions and holds delegated authority from the Board of Public Works to review and grant lighting waivers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Council to grant exemptions from or credits against development impact fees for moderately priced dwelling units, accessory dwelling units, workforce housing, and certain developer conveyances of land or school construction accepted by the county or County Board of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and builders of affordable housing, accessory dwelling units, and workforce housing, as well as Anne Arundel County taxpayers and local school/public infrastructure programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County could experience an indeterminate decrease in development impact fee revenues if the county council passes an ordinance granting the additional exemptions or credits. County expenditures for capital improvement projects are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references agreements with the State Board of Education regarding the construction of contract schools as a qualifying criterion for development impact fee credits in Anne Arundel County, though the legislation has no state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Braille Flag Memorial Act of 2025, requiring the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families to designate a location for an American braille tactile flag at one or more State veterans' cemeteries to honor blind or visually impaired service members, veterans, and Maryland residents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Blind or visually impaired veterans, active-duty service members, and visitors to Maryland State veterans' cemeteries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Department of Veterans and Military Families can designate a location using existing resources, as installation of the flag is not explicitly mandated. If the department elects to purchase, install, and maintain tactile flags, general fund expenditures would increase by an indeterminate minimal amount (flags range from $250 to $850 each). Revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 455 directly requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to designate a location for an American braille tactile flag in one or more State veterans' cemeteries managed by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $350,000 in the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2027 for the TerpsEXCEED Program at the University of Maryland, College Park Campus, providing sustainable funding to support and expand educational and employment opportunities for students with intellectual disabilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland, College Park Campus
qa_results.stakeholders: College students with intellectual disabilities participating in the TerpsEXCEED program, peer mentors, and university program staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal year 2027, state general fund expenditures are assumed to increase by $350,000 annually if the discretionary funding is appropriated. Higher education revenues and expenditures for the University of Maryland, College Park Campus increase correspondingly by $350,000 annually. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly funds and supports the TerpsEXCEED program at the University of Maryland, College Park, which is a member institution of the University System of Maryland, providing an authorized $350,000 annual appropriation beginning in FY 2027.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal planning, which includes incorporating authorized discretionary appropriations into the Governor's annual budget bill.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include a $350,000 appropriation in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2027 for the TerpsEXCEED Program.

The bill authorizes funds to be used to connect students with state agencies supporting individuals with disabilities and facilitate cross-agency integrated resource teams for students with intellectual disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: The James 'Jimmy' Malone Act requires Maryland counties that offer self-insured employee health benefit plans to provide county-employed firefighters with coverage for preventive cancer screenings without copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles, adhering to International Association of Fire Fighters guidelines. Counties may fulfill this requirement through a no-cost annual exam or by applying for a state grant for innovative cancer screening technologies. Counties must collect and report screening and cost data to the Maryland Health Care Commission, which must evaluate expanding coverage to the commercial insurance market.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland County Governments
qa_results.stakeholders: County-employed professional firefighters and Maryland county governments that offer self-insured health plans.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2029 only for the Maryland Health Care Commission to complete a required study; state revenues are unaffected. Local government health insurance expenditures may increase for counties with self-insured plans employing firefighters to provide screenings without cost-sharing, though counties can fulfill the requirement by applying for existing grant funds and data reporting can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 459 directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission receive cancer screening data reports from counties in 2027 and 2028, conduct a study on expanding coverage to the commercial insurance market, and submit a final report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028, with an estimated $100,000 fiscal impact in FY 2029.

The bill allows counties to satisfy the cancer screening mandate by applying for grants under the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program (Health - General Article Title 13, Subtitle 40), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health. Additionally, the Maryland Health Care Commission operates as an independent commission within MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces the Motor Vehicle Administration's 3-hour alcohol and drug education program with a broader 3-hour Roadway Safety Driving Education Program for certain driver's license applicants. The updated curriculum includes instruction on signs, signals, and pavement markings; dangerous driving behaviors; work zone safety; impaired driving hazards and penalties; and the Maryland points system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Certain driver's license applicants (specifically out-of-country drivers qualifying without a learner's permit), students enrolled in driver education, and certified private driver education providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, and State revenues are not affected. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary agency responsible for establishing the 3-hour Roadway Safety Driving Education Program, determining course content, and adopting regulations to certify private entities to offer the program.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the state's transportation administration and motor vehicle safety policies.
The bill mandates that MVA establish the program in cooperation with the Behavioral Health Administration, an agency within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Health Equality for Service Members Act standardizes definitions relating to military and uniformed services across Maryland law by referencing federal definitions. It expands eligibility for certain state benefits, rights, and administrative procedures—such as expedited health occupations licensing, vital records fee waivers, housing voucher prioritization, and continued eligibility for Medicaid and developmental disability waiver services—to encompass all members of the uniformed services, specifically including the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, rather than only the armed forces.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (including health occupations licensing boards), Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, and Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty service members, veterans, and military families, particularly members of the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Officer Corps, as well as health occupation license applicants and licensees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the expansion applies to a relatively small population (primarily PHS and NOAA personnel) relative to the existing veteran population in Maryland. Any operational or workload changes can be absorbed within existing agency resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency for multiple sections of the bill, including vital records fee exemptions, Developmental Disabilities Administration waitlist protections, Medicaid waiver programs, behavioral health coordination and grants, and oversight of health occupations licensing boards.

The bill amends the core definitions in Title 9, Subtitle 9 of the State Government Article governing DVMF, expands the scope of veterans and uniformed service members covered, and requires DVMF collaboration regarding behavioral health coordination and uniformed services culture coursework.

The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 4-2906) to alter the definition and prioritization of housing vouchers and assistance payments for veterans and uniformed service members.

MSDE administers the Autism Waiver registry and services program, which is amended by the bill (§ 15-154) to protect the registry status and eligibility of children whose families relocate out of state due to uniformed services assignments.
The bill alters the Certificate of Need (CON) exemption criteria for comprehensive care facilities serving veterans under Health-General § 19-114, which falls under MHCC's regulatory oversight.

The bill explicitly references the Maryland National Guard in provisions requiring interagency collaboration with MDH to provide behavioral health service coordination for eligible veterans and service members.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the Maryland National Guard and Maryland Defense Force (both of which are statutory partners in the behavioral health service coordination provisions), the Adjutant General's operational scope aligns with the bill's expanded service member provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates statutory references in the Local Government Article regarding Anne Arundel County hotel tax distributions, annual reporting, and county audits by changing the name of the Annapolis and Anne Arundel County Conference and Visitors Bureau to Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc., the City of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County government, and local tourism organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal effect and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations, as it solely updates obsolete organizational name references.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland vehicle laws by prohibiting individuals from obscuring or modifying a vehicle registration plate in a manner that may prevent identification, making enforcement of this violation a secondary offense. It also amends the definition of a registration plate cover, prohibits advertising or promoting the sale of unlawful covers by falsely claiming they are legal in the State, and classifies such false advertising as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division) and State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers in Maryland, retailers and advertisers of vehicle registration plate covers, consumers, and law enforcement officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not materially affected, and the bill can likely be implemented and enforced using existing budgeted State resources. Local government finances and operations are also not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the false advertising or promotion of unlawful registration plate covers as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle laws and highway safety, the Maryland State Police is directly responsible for enforcing the bill's provisions on obscured registration plates, including the requirement that it be enforced only as a secondary offense.

The MVA regulates vehicle registration plates and assesses driver's license points for moving violations under § 16-402, which applies to violations of the prohibition on obscuring or modifying registration plates.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and the administration of the Maryland Vehicle Law altered by this bill.
The District Court and Judiciary process traffic citations, track prepayable fines, and adjudicate cases related to motor vehicle registration plate violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 400 block of East Oliver Street in the 45th alcoholic beverages district under specified conditions, including executing a memorandum of understanding with the Greenmount West Community Association. It also establishes a defined geographic boundary in the 45th district where holders of Class A and Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses are limited to sales between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license applicants and holders of Class A, Class B-D-7, and Class C licenses in the 45th alcoholic beverages district of Baltimore City, patrons, and the Greenmount West Community Association.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry. While the bill specifically alters local licensing and hours of operation administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it falls within the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program to allow part-time associate's degree students to receive scholarship awards for up to six years, while maintaining a three-year maximum duration for full-time associate's degree candidates. It also clarifies that students pursuing noncredit vocational certificates, certificate sequences leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs may receive the award for up to three years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland community college students (specifically part-time associate's degree students, vocational and certificate students, and apprenticeship participants) and Maryland community colleges.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an estimated $7,000 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to make system enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System to track differing award lengths. The bill does not change overall statutory funding for the scholarship program, though extending award durations could result in more students on waiting lists or fewer total recipients if funding limits are reached. Local community colleges and Baltimore City Community College can implement the changes with existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees the State's higher education financial assistance programs, including allocating Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program funding and tracking award durations through software enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System.
The Commission coordinates higher education policy and financial aid administration, including the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program affected by this bill.
