qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders, applicants, restaurants, bars, caterers, and small businesses in Dorchester County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Dorchester County revenues will increase by at least $10,250 annually beginning in FY 2026 due to increased license fees across at least 66 existing businesses, plus additional indeterminate revenues from new application and transfer fees. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates aspects of the state's alcohol industry; however, this bill strictly alters local license, application, and transfer fees administered by the Board of License Commissioners for Dorchester County, having no direct state fiscal or operational impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an arts beer and wine license in Dorchester County, allowing eligible nonprofit or for-profit retail art businesses located within an arts and entertainment district to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption when snacks are served.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Dorchester County
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit and for-profit art businesses (such as art centers, galleries, and museums) located in arts and entertainment districts in Dorchester County, their customers, and nearby schools and places of worship.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Dorchester County revenues will increase beginning in fiscal year 2026 from the $250 annual license fee for each arts beer and wine license issued. Any additional local enforcement activity can be managed using existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill stipulates that the arts beer and wine license may only be issued to qualifying businesses located within an arts and entertainment district approved by the Department of Commerce.

The Comptroller regulates the alcoholic beverage industry and oversees alcohol taxation in the state, although the license itself is administered and issued at the local county level by the Dorchester County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the beer and wine tasting license in Dorchester County as the beer, wine, and liquor tasting (BWLT) license, allowing eligible Class A license holders to conduct liquor tastings. It establishes per-individual consumption limits of 0.5 ounces per offering and 1.5 ounces per day, while clarifying that licensees may only offer tastings of alcoholic beverages they are authorized to sell under their Class A license.
qa_results.responsible_party: Dorchester County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County Class A alcoholic beverages license holders and their retail customers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Dorchester County revenues are not affected, and any additional enforcement activity can be handled using existing resources. The bill has a minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees alcoholic beverages laws and taxes, although direct administration of this tasting license is handled locally by the Dorchester County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes holders of Class C beer, wine, and liquor licenses, Class C fraternal/sororal organization licenses, and Class C veterans' organization licenses in Anne Arundel County to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption during events held on their licensed premises to members and their guests. It also requires outside groups that host events at these licensed premises to obtain a Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor license from the county licensing board.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Class C license holders (including clubs, fraternal/sororal organizations, and veterans' organizations), their members and guests, and outside groups hosting events at licensed premises.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: Anne Arundel County revenues will increase depending on the number of Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor licenses ($50 fee per license) issued to outside groups hosting events at these premises. Anne Arundel County expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and oversees state alcohol excise taxation. While HB 571 specifically affects local retail Class C licensing administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates broadly to the regulation of alcoholic beverage sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 573 expands the approved courses of study for an applicant seeking an expanded function dental assistant (EFDA) certificate to include programs offered by the DALE Foundation and Trapezio Orthodontic Assistant Training Solutions. It requires initial certification courses to include at least 35 hours of both online and in-person instruction, directs the State Board of Dental Examiners to adopt regulations regarding instruction hours and continuing education, and establishes specific conditions and fees for reinstating expired EFDA certificates.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Expanded function dental assistants (EFDAs), applicants for EFDA certification, dental assisting training providers, licensed dentists, and dental practices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources of the State Board of Dental Examiners. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Board of Dental Examiners, a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health, requiring it to adopt regulations regarding education and reinstatement requirements for expanded function dental assistants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners to issue up to three Class B beer, wine, and liquor restaurant licenses for separate premises to an individual or for the use of a person, provided that only one of the licenses authorizes off-premises consumption, and defines criteria under which direct or indirect interest in multiple licenses is prohibited.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurant owners, alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants, and businesses operating in St. Mary's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill does not materially affect St. Mary's County operations or finances, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. Although this legislation specifically governs the issuance and interest limitations of local Class B restaurant alcoholic beverages licenses administered by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it falls within the broader subject matter of the state's alcoholic beverages regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill decreases the frequency with which the Maryland Attorney General must submit reports to the General Assembly regarding efforts to recover economic damages from the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge and the closure of the Port of Baltimore, changing the requirement from monthly to every six months.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland General Assembly, the Office of the Attorney General, and the Maryland public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as altering the frequency of the reporting requirement does not affect revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting requirement imposed on the Office of the Attorney General under the PORT Act, decreasing the required reporting frequency to the General Assembly regarding the recovery of economic damages from the Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure from monthly to every six months.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller's Office, in consultation with specified stakeholders, to study the enforcement process used by its Field Enforcement Bureau for miscellaneous State business licenses and submit findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland business owners, operators, and employees subject to miscellaneous State business licensing, as well as retail, restaurant, and commerce trade organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is negligible, as the Comptroller's Office can conduct the study and prepare the required report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Comptroller's Office, through its Field Enforcement Bureau, to conduct a study and submit recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, regarding the enforcement process and citation authority for miscellaneous State business licenses.

The bill requires consultation with the Maryland Circuit Court Clerks' Association regarding the issuance and enforcement of miscellaneous State business licenses, which are administered through the circuit court clerks under the Judicial Branch supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates statutory terminology across the Annotated Code of Maryland by replacing obsolete references to the Maryland State Firemen's Association with the Maryland State Firefighters Association to reflect the organization's name change, as well as replacing gendered terms such as 'fireman' and 'squadman' with 'firefighter' and 'squad member'.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State Firefighters Association, volunteer and career firefighters, rescue squad members, emergency medical services personnel, and related state and local entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The statutory changes are purely technical in nature and do not affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates terminology in Tax - General § 10-208, which governs the volunteer firefighter subtraction modification report submitted annually to the Office of the Comptroller.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates statutory references in Tax - General § 10-208 regarding annual reports submitted to the department, as well as terminology concerning correctional officers in disease exposure reporting statutes.
The bill updates Transportation Article § 16-102, which directs the Administration to consult with the Maryland Firefighters Association when adopting certain driver licensing regulations.
The bill updates child labor statutory provisions in Labor and Employment § 3-213 enforced by MD Labor, replacing the term 'fireman' with 'firefighter.'

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Education Article § 13-511 regarding the composition of the State Emergency Medical Services Advisory Council, updating the reference to the Maryland State Firefighters Association.
The bill amends Health - General § 18-213 regarding contagious disease notification and exposure procedures for first responders and public health reporting.
The bill amends Education Article § 18-602 under the state financial assistance title, updating terminology for scholarships for children of volunteer firefighters.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the State Retirement Agency to convene and staff a workgroup of stakeholders to study the requirements and processes for transfers of member service credit between State and local retirement and pension systems. The workgroup must review statutory inconsistencies, examine transfer issues, and report its findings and recommended legislative changes to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government employees who transfer between public retirement and pension systems, participating county and municipal retirement systems, and public employee unions such as AFSCME.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. The State Retirement Agency can convene and staff the workgroup using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the State Retirement Agency to convene, participate in, and staff a workgroup studying the transfer of member service between State and local retirement and pension systems, and to submit a final report of recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary multi-stakeholder workgroup tasked with studying statutory requirements, reviewing Title 37 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, and issuing recommendations regarding retirement service transfers.
The workgroup is mandated to submit its final report of findings, recommendations, and proposed legislative initiatives to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to notify the State Department of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days of closing and the execution of a regulatory agreement that a commercial property developed under Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code has been awarded a federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and owners of affordable housing properties developed under the federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program, as well as state assessment officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Housing and Community Development can handle the notification requirement using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 585 directly requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to notify the State Department of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days of closing and execution of the regulatory agreement governing a federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit for commercial real property.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires local boards of elections to pay election judges for completed training courses only after they actually serve on an election day or early voting day. It also allows public school students who serve as election judges to choose between receiving election judge compensation or earning hours toward their high school service-learning graduation requirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local boards of elections and the Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Election judges, public school students serving as election judges, and local election officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not expected to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections supervises and administers elections across the state and oversees local boards of elections, which must implement the new timing requirements for paying election judge training compensation.

The bill directly touches upon high school graduation requirements overseen by the Department of Education by authorizing public school students serving as election judges to earn hours toward the service-learning graduation requirement (or receive compensation).

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each branch of a county public library system and the Enoch Pratt Free Library to place an automated external defibrillator (AED) in an accessible, prominent location, maintain its functionality, and comply with the Maryland Public Access AED Program beginning January 1, 2026. The bill also establishes civil liability protections for libraries and individuals administering AED aid in good faith and directs the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems to submit an implementation report by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Public library patrons and staff, county library systems, the Enoch Pratt Free Library, and individuals experiencing cardiac emergencies in public libraries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies (MIEMSS and the Maryland State Library Agency) can implement requirements and reporting with existing budgeted resources. Local government expenditures increase starting in fiscal 2026 for county library systems to purchase AEDs (ranging from $500 to $2,000 per unit) and provide staff training ($37 to $115 per person) for facilities that do not currently have equipment or trained personnel. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS administers the Maryland Public Access AED Program with which public libraries must comply. The agency is also tasked with receiving library registrations, adopting implementing regulations, and submitting a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, detailing library AED registrations and adverse cardiac events.

The Maryland State Library Agency provides coordination, strategic leadership, and funding oversight for Maryland's 24 public library systems and the State library network, which are directly subject to the AED mandate under the bill.
The bill explicitly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with jointly adopting regulations alongside MIEMSS to establish guidelines for AED maintenance, inspections, and library registration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County and municipal corporations within the county to provide a local personal property tax credit to supermarkets that complete new construction or substantial renovations in designated food desert retail incentive areas.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing body of Anne Arundel County and municipal corporations within Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Supermarket and grocery store owners and operators, residents in designated food desert areas, and local governments within Anne Arundel County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Personal property tax revenues for Anne Arundel County and municipalities decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent the credit is granted; exact revenue loss is indeterminate and depends on local adoption, the number of qualifying supermarkets, and the value of personal property. Expenditures are not significantly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the collective bargaining timeline and process for uniformed fire employees of the BWI Marshall Airport Fire and Rescue Department by establishing a system of binding arbitration if negotiations reach an impasse, while stipulating that an arbitrator's decision regarding wages remains subject to State budget limitations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) / Maryland Aviation Administration and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
qa_results.stakeholders: Uniformed fire employees of the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department and their exclusive bargaining representative.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and potentially general fund expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 due to shared arbitration costs (estimated at several thousand dollars per impasse, with hourly rates typically between $375 and $1,125) and potential need for additional human resources/labor relations staff. TTF personnel and related expenditures may also be affected, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2027 depending on arbitration outcomes. Revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department is a unit within the Maryland Aviation Administration, meaning MAA's uniformed fire personnel and operating procedures are directly governed by the bill's collective bargaining and binding arbitration mandates.

MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration and manages the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will directly fund the arbitration costs and potential personnel expenditure increases resulting from binding arbitration decisions.

DBM serves as the State's central personnel and budget agency, works in association with MDOT during labor negotiations, and may incur additional administrative workload or costs for labor relations personnel.
PERB regulates collective bargaining for Maryland public sector employees and noted an operational impact as issues under its jurisdiction may overlap with the jurisdiction of appointed arbitrators.

The Governor or the Governor's designee is the statutory bargaining authority representing the State in collective bargaining agreements and must reflect negotiated or arbitrated terms within the state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Educational Equality for Service Members Act establishes uniform definitions for military-related terms across the Maryland Code (Education, General Provisions, and State Government Articles), aligning them primarily with federal definitions in the U.S. Code. It broadens various education-related benefits and privileges—previously limited largely to the armed forces—to encompass all uniformed services (including the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration commissioned corps), their active duty members, veterans, and their eligible dependents. These benefits include public school enrollment exceptions, expedited teacher licensing, emergency medical services credentialing credits, in-state tuition exemptions, and state scholarship eligibility.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty and reserve members of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, Public Health Service, and NOAA), veterans, their spouses, and dependent children.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an estimated $9,200 per additional scholarship award annually beginning in FY 2026, though the total number of additional awards cannot be reliably estimated. Higher education institutions may experience a potential minimal loss of nonresident tuition revenue due to expanded in-state tuition exemptions. Public school enrollments and local finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory eligibility criteria and service deferment rules for several state financial aid programs administered by MHEC, including the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program, Senatorial scholarships, and Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts scholarships, creating a direct fiscal and operational impact.

The bill requires MSDE and local school systems to alter rules regarding public school enrollment hardships, reciprocity agreements, the Purple Star Schools Program, and expedited educator licensure to include all uniformed service members and their families.

The bill amends Title 9, Subtitle 9 of the State Government Article governing the department, updating definitions of 'active duty', 'active service member', 'armed forces', 'military family', 'reserve component', 'service member', and 'uniformed services' to align with federal statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Education Article § 13-516 to require the EMS Board within MIEMSS to credit uniformed services training, education, and active service experience toward EMS licensure and certification requirements.

USM institutions are required to extend nonresident tuition exemptions and priority enrollment privileges to the expanded category of active service members of all uniformed services and their eligible dependents.
As an independent public university, Morgan State must implement the bill's expanded nonresident tuition exemptions for active service members and dependents of all uniformed services.
As a public honors college, St. Mary's College must comply with statutory expansions of nonresident tuition exemptions for uniformed services personnel and their families.
The bill amends Education Article § 18-1910 to allow time spent in active duty in the uniformed services to extend the period for exercising benefits under the Maryland Prepaid College Trust.

The bill amends Education Article § 21-309 regarding qualified employees with disabilities, expanding the Maryland Department of Labor's determinations of individuals discharged or released from active duty for service-connected disabilities to include all uniformed services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority to provide loan guarantees under the Small Business Guaranty Fund in specified forms, such as an irrevocable letter of credit, an official treasurer's check, escrow or depository account funds, or other legal instruments guaranteeing restitution or reimbursement for loan losses, provided terms do not discourage lenders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) / Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Small businesses seeking financing, private lending institutions and commercial lenders, and the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for MSBDFA are likely not materially affected due to historically limited program activity, with only minor administrative costs associated with the new guaranty instruments. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA) and its financing programs, including the Long-Term Guaranty Program under the Small Business Guaranty Fund, are housed within and administered by the Department of Commerce.

The State Treasurer's Office manages state funds, banking, and depository accounts, and was consulted on the operational and fiscal impact regarding financial instruments and depository accounts used for state loan guaranties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Maryland Border States Advanced Practice Nursing Act, requiring the State Board of Nursing to engage in discussions with nursing licensing boards in Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia to pursue reciprocity agreements for advanced practice nursing licensure and specialty certification, and to submit annual progress reports to the General Assembly from 2025 through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), telehealth patients, and nursing licensing boards in Maryland and neighboring jurisdictions (Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington, D.C.).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources; however, if additional contractual staff is needed to support discussions, Board of Nursing special fund expenditures may increase by approximately $90,000 in the first year. Special fund revenues could minimally decrease in the future if reciprocity agreements reduce the number of out-of-state APRNs paying Maryland initial and renewal licensing fees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Nursing (MBON) operates within the Maryland Department of Health as the regulatory licensing board for nurses. The bill directly mandates that the Board hold reciprocity discussions with border states and submit annual reports on progress.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Comptroller to provide required annual notices regarding the federal and State earned income tax credit to Maryland employers electronically or by mail, rather than mandating delivery by mail.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees eligible for the federal and State earned income tax credit
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office may decrease due to mailing cost savings beginning in FY 2026. In FY 2026, savings are likely offset by one-time programming costs; in subsequent years, expenditures may decrease by more than $100,000 annually (compared to current annual mailing costs of about $140,000). State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 603 directly alters the statutory requirement for the Comptroller of Maryland by allowing the agency to provide annual Earned Income Tax Credit notices to employers electronically or by mail, resulting in significant annual cost savings for the Comptroller's Office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies the county income tax rate used to calculate the local earned income tax credit for counties that impose marginal or flat income tax rates.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible low-to-moderate-income Maryland taxpayers claiming the local earned income tax credit and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies existing administrative practice and has no direct state or local fiscal impact. The Comptroller's Office can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources, and state and local revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Comptroller's Office and amends the calculation of the local earned income tax credit administered on state income tax returns by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal prohibition against willfully destroying, damaging, defacing, or removing cemetery property to include landscaping and any other part of cemetery grounds, with exceptions for repair or replacement. It also extends the statute of limitations for prosecuting the destruction of funerary objects and cemetery elements from one year after the offense was committed to within three years after local authorities knew or reasonably should have known of the violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State's Attorneys, local law enforcement authorities, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
qa_results.stakeholders: Cemetery owners and operators, descendants and heirs of deceased persons interred in cemeteries, and individuals facing prosecution for cemetery vandalism or property destruction.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. While violators are subject to existing misdemeanor penalties of up to five years imprisonment and/or fines up to $10,000, historical data shows zero individuals were sentenced under these provisions in circuit courts in FY 2024, resulting in negligible fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statute of limitations and expands criminal prohibitions related to damaging cemetery elements, directly impacting cases filed, scheduled, and adjudicated in the Maryland court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal offenses carrying up to five years of imprisonment and lengthens the prosecution window, potentially impacting caseloads and representation of indigent defendants charged with these violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill addresses offenses carrying penalties of incarceration up to five years and probation, which fall under the jurisdiction of the Division of Correction and the Division of Parole and Probation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that the Comptroller of Maryland may record and monitor incoming telephone calls to the Comptroller's call centers rather than specifically to an automated call distribution system, updating outdated statutory language to accommodate modern call center technology.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers contacting the Comptroller's Office by telephone and employees of the Comptroller's call centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Comptroller's Office.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 617 is a departmental bill requested by the Comptroller of Maryland. It updates and clarifies the statutory authorization for the Comptroller's call centers to monitor and record incoming customer service calls for training, quality control, and safety purposes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to establish an internet-based system allowing individuals to purchase subscription plans for multijurisdictional and jackpot lottery games using electronic devices like computers and mobile phones. The bill also allows licensed lottery agents to sell vouchers used to purchase or renew subscriptions and receive commission on those sales, and requires the agency to report on subscription sales by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland lottery players, licensed lottery sales agents and retailers, and the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2026; as an illustrative example, an increase of 500 subscriptions would yield approximately $95,000 annually after paying $27,000 in retailer commissions. The State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency can implement software upgrades and reporting requirements using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to implement an internet-based subscription purchase system for jackpot and multijurisdictional lottery games, regulate voucher sales and agent commissions, and submit a required report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the sales and use tax exemption on cannabis to include sales between licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is clarifying in nature and conforms the sales and use tax exemption to include business-to-business transactions involving registered cannabis nurseries, which does not affect State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill was introduced as a departmental request by the Comptroller's Office and amends the sales and use tax code, which the Comptroller administers and enforces, to exempt transactions between licensed cannabis businesses and registered cannabis nurseries.

The Maryland Cannabis Administration is the regulatory body responsible for licensing cannabis businesses and registering cannabis nurseries under Title 36 of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which governs the entities qualifying for this sales and use tax exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory definition of 'slot machine' to exclude skills-based amusement devices that award tickets, tokens, merchandise, or other objects of minimal per-play value that can be accumulated and redeemed for noncash merchandise or prizes with a wholesale value up to $599.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators of skills-based amusement devices, family entertainment centers, arcades, and players/patrons of such devices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. Any enforcement activities can be handled by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission using existing resources. The effect on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing skills-based amusement devices excluded from the definition of a slot machine, referencing standards approved by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission through regulation and impacting its regulatory oversight of gaming devices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Income Tax Reconciliation Program to enable justice-involved individuals who were unable to file State income tax returns while incarcerated to set up installment payment plans of up to 10 years and receive waivers of accrued interest and penalties for tax years 2025 through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Justice-involved individuals who are currently serving or were released within the previous two years from a term of imprisonment between six months and ten years and have unpaid State income tax obligations incurred during their incarceration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2026 due to forgone interest and penalty collections on overdue income taxes. The Comptroller's Office can administer the program with existing budgeted resources, and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Income Tax Reconciliation Program, establishing installment payment plans, waiving interest and penalties, adopting regulations, and reporting annually on program impact to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily requires the department to collaborate with the Comptroller to develop and execute an awareness campaign informing justice-involved individuals and the public about the Income Tax Reconciliation Program.

The bill amends the Criminal Procedure Article to mandate that the court inform defendants sentenced to a term of imprisonment between 6 months and 10 years about the Income Tax Reconciliation Program, directly impacting judicial administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program to include veterinary practitioners and veterinary technicians who graduated from an accredited veterinary college or university and provided veterinary services in Maryland for at least five years as an employee or volunteered for at least 100 hours per year for three years at qualifying animal shelters.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Student Financial Assistance within the Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterinary practitioners, veterinary technicians, animal shelters, local governments, and organizations providing animal control or spay and neuter services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $8,000 in FY 2026 for one-time software enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) and minimal publicity updates. Expanding eligibility does not mandate additional grant funding, but each additional award granted costs approximately $5,800 per individual if funds are available; otherwise, qualified applicants are placed on a waiting list. State revenues are unaffected. Local finances are not affected, though local shelters may benefit from increased volunteer or employment participation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and its Office of Student Financial Assistance administer the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP). The bill expands eligibility under the program to include veterinary practitioners and technicians, requiring MHEC to update eligibility guidelines, modify promotional materials, and make IT enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).

MHEC directly administers the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program and will implement the expansion to include eligible veterinarians and veterinary technicians, incurring one-time system upgrade costs.

The bill establishes eligibility for veterinarians and technicians volunteering at shelters that received funding under the Maryland Spay and Neuter Grants Program, which is administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the reporting deadline for the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services to October 31, 2026, and extends the termination date of the task force to June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Returning citizens (individuals released from incarceration in Maryland) and members of the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Any additional expense reimbursements for task force members and staffing costs for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for staffing the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services, absorbing any associated staffing and member reimbursement costs, and would be the department housing the proposed new division.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the reporting deadline and operational duration of a temporary legislatively mandated task force tasked with studying reentry services and submitting recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license and an associated temporary to-go event permit in Wicomico County. Municipalities holding the license may establish designated special event areas for up to seven consecutive days, and adjacent Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders with the temporary permit may sell alcoholic beverages in approved to-go cups for consumption within the event area.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Wicomico County municipalities, Class B alcoholic beverages license holders (restaurants and hotels) located in or adjacent to designated special event areas, and event attendees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Wicomico County revenues will increase beginning in FY 2026 depending on the number of Class C per diem municipal licenses ($45 per day) and temporary to-go event permits ($20 per day) issued; overall revenue cannot be reliably estimated. The county can handle monitoring and enforcement using existing resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the composition, terms, and meeting requirements of the Juvenile Services Education Board. Specifically, it allows the Secretary of Higher Education and the State Superintendent of Schools to appoint designees, staggers the terms of appointed members, establishes a limit of two consecutive terms for appointed members, and adjusts the meeting schedule to at least 10 times per year (and generally not more than once per month) while authorizing special meetings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services and the Juvenile Services Education Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Appointed and ex officio members of the Juvenile Services Education Board, Department of Juvenile Services educators and staff, and juvenile students placed in detention and residential facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and has no state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the governance and meeting requirements of the Juvenile Services Education Board, which is staffed by DJS, includes the Secretary of Juvenile Services, and oversees educational programs within DJS-operated facilities.
The bill directly amends the composition of the Juvenile Services Education Board to authorize the State Superintendent of Schools to select a designee to serve on the board.
The bill authorizes the Secretary of Higher Education, who heads the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to appoint a designee to serve on the Juvenile Services Education Board.
The bill authorizes the Secretary of Higher Education to appoint a designee to serve in their place on the Juvenile Services Education Board.

The bill staggers terms, establishes term limits, and schedules term expirations for gubernatorial appointees to the Juvenile Services Education Board, impacting the appointment and vetting cycle managed by the Office of Appointments.
The bill affects gubernatorial appointments to the Juvenile Services Education Board by staggering terms and imposing consecutive term limits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory structure, meeting frequency, quorum/special meeting rules, and membership terms of an executive board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies the disciplinary actions the Maryland State Board of Nursing may take regarding applicants and licensees in direct-entry midwifery, explicitly authorizing the Board to grant a license subject to a reprimand, probation, or suspension if disciplinary grounds are violated.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for a license to practice direct-entry midwifery and licensed direct-entry midwives in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal or operational impact on the State Board of Nursing and no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees health occupations licensing boards, including the State Board of Nursing, which directly regulates and disciplines licensed direct-entry midwives and applicants under the provisions amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), managed care organizations, and certain health insurance carriers to provide coverage for calcium score testing in accordance with the most recent guidelines issued by the American College of Cardiology.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid enrollees and individuals covered by fully insured commercial health plans who have risk factors for cardiovascular disease, as well as health insurance carriers and managed care organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees. State Medicaid expenditures (50% general funds, 50% federal funds) may increase minimally due to increased utilization, though the service is already covered. There is no material fiscal impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to the extent health insurance premiums rise for fully insured employee plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the Health - General Article to require the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health, and managed care organizations to cover calcium score testing.

The bill establishes a new mandated health benefit under Insurance Article § 15-861 for insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs, which the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees through rate and policy form filings and regulatory enforcement.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must adhere to state insurance benefit mandates (though existing coverage already satisfies the bill's requirements).
MHBE operates the state health insurance marketplace, where qualified health plans sold to individuals and small employers are required to provide state-mandated health benefits.
MHCC evaluates and reports on proposed mandated health insurance benefits in Maryland and commissioned the actuarial and clinical analysis cited in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland State Department of Education to conduct an annual assessment of the State's school health and wellness personnel workforce, submit a report to the General Assembly beginning December 1, 2027, and publish the report online. It also adds a school nurse member nominated by the Maryland Association of School Health Nurses to the Maryland Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, local school systems, local health departments, school-based health centers, and school health and wellness personnel including counselors, nurses, psychologists, social workers, and therapists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $61,700 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time health policy analyst to coordinate data collection and analysis with MSDE, with ongoing expenditures of $57,700 in FY 2028, $60,300 in FY 2029, and $62,900 in FY 2030. There is no state fiscal effect in FY 2026, and state revenues are unaffected. Local school systems and health departments can gather and report data using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is jointly responsible with MSDE for conducting the annual assessment of the school health and wellness personnel workforce, submitting the annual report to the General Assembly, and publishing findings online. MDH also incurs direct fiscal expenditures to fund a health policy analyst position to implement the bill.

MSDE is jointly tasked with MDH to conduct the annual workforce assessment across local school systems, analyze staffing and vacancy data, prepare and submit the annual report to the General Assembly, and publish the report on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition of the Maryland Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers by adding a new voting member who is a school nurse.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the newly added school nurse member to the Maryland Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and appointment process for the additional school nurse member on the Maryland Council on Advancement of School-Based Health Centers.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill creates a felony offense prohibiting a person from knowingly and willfully dismembering, destroying, removing, burying, disposing of, or obliterating any part of human remains, or aiding and abetting in such acts, with the intent to conceal a crime. Convictions carry a penalty of up to five years of imprisonment, which may run consecutively or concurrently with sentences for other offenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals accused or convicted of destroying or concealing human remains to hide a crime, law enforcement agencies, state prosecutors, and the correctional system.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund incarceration expenditures may minimally increase due to the new felony penalty of up to five years imprisonment. The bill is not anticipated to materially impact local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense punishable by up to five years in prison, which may result in increased state incarceration costs and correctional facility commitments under DPSCS jurisdiction.
The bill establishes a new criminal charge and felony penalty, which affects court caseloads, case filings, and judicial proceedings managed and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony crime, and attorneys from the Office of the Public Defender will represent indigent defendants charged with this offense.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police investigators will be responsible for investigating criminal violations involving the destruction or concealment of human remains.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the authorized uses of the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund to include funding for the Office of the Attorney General to assist in investigating untested sexual assault evidence collection kits collected before October 1, 2020, supporting the statewide sexual assault victim notification hotline operated by the State sexual assault coalition, and supporting peer-to-peer telehealth programs. It permits grant awards of up to 36 months, prohibits using the fund for the Sexual Assault Evidence Collection Kit Tracking Program, and extends the deadline for reporting kit information to the tracking program from December 31, 2025, to March 31, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Sexual assault survivors and victims, law enforcement agencies, the Office of the Attorney General, the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault, healthcare providers, and forensic laboratories.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (GOCPP) increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent additional funds are disbursed, although an exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. Grant revenues and corresponding expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General also increase beginning in FY 2026 to hire investigators. The FY 2026 State budget includes $3.5 million for the fund, which had a balance of nearly $4.0 million at the end of FY 2024. Local law enforcement agencies and State's Attorneys benefit from investigative assistance, multi-year grants (up to 36 months), and an extended reporting deadline to March 31, 2026, with no material fiscal impact anticipated on local finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary administering agency of the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund and the Sexual Assault Evidence Collection Kit Tracking Program. The bill expands the Executive Director's duties regarding fund distribution, reporting, and multi-year grant awards up to 36 months.

The bill explicitly expands the authorized uses of the Rape Kit Testing Grant Fund to provide funding directly to the OAG to assist law enforcement agencies with investigations of crimes involving untested rape kits collected before October 1, 2020, resulting in increased grant revenues and expenditures.

As the primary state law enforcement agency operating forensic laboratories, MSP is directly affected by the extended reporting deadline for sexual assault evidence collection kits and remains eligible to receive grant funding from the Fund for kit testing.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $450,000 for the Maryland Deaf Culture Digital Library (DCDL) in the State budget bill starting in fiscal year 2026, and requires the DCDL to submit its annual operating budget to the Maryland State Library Agency by June 1 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals, library patrons, and State and county public library staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $49,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to fulfill the $450,000 mandated appropriation, accounting for $401,000 already budgeted for the Maryland Deaf Culture Digital Library. Funding is discretionary in FY 2026 and becomes a statutory mandate beginning in FY 2027. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency oversees the Deaf Culture Digital Library (DCDL), which is established under its purview and is required by the bill to submit its annual operating budget to the agency on or before June 1 each year.

DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and managing state expenditures, and will be required to implement the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 for the Deaf Culture Digital Library.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ODHH coordinates directly with the Deaf Culture Digital Library on sensitivity training, advisory board appointments, and partnership development to serve deaf and hard of hearing Marylanders.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a $450,000 appropriation for the Deaf Culture Digital Library in the annual state budget bill starting in fiscal year 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters child support enforcement by exempting obligors whose income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines from driver's license suspensions for arrears, unless judicially determined to be voluntarily impoverished. It also extends the noncompliance threshold for noncommercial license suspensions from 60 to 120 days and requires courts to provide copies of child support orders and guideline calculations to the Child Support Administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Child Support Administration (Department of Human Services) and the Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Child support obligors (particularly low-income obligors earning up to 250% of the federal poverty guidelines), child support obligees and children receiving support, and circuit court staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase for the Department of Human Services (DHS), including $125,000 in one-time IT programming costs in FY 2026 (34% general funds, 66% federal funds) and potential additional personnel costs for caseworkers (illustratively $49,000 per caseworker in FY 2026 and $73,000 annually thereafter). General fund expenditures for the Judiciary may increase minimally to transmit order and guideline data for over 50,000 additional cases annually, causing a significant operational impact on circuit courts. General fund fine revenues will decrease minimally from fewer citations for driving on a suspended license.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Child Support Administration (CSA) is a division of DHS. The bill directly alters the procedures and criteria under which CSA investigates obligors, determines poverty thresholds, and notifies the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend driver's licenses for nonpayment of child support, resulting in potential significant operational and IT programming fiscal impacts.

MVA is responsible for executing driver's license suspensions, reinstatements, expungements, and issuing work-restricted licenses based on child support arrearage notifications transmitted from the Child Support Administration.

The bill requires courts, after establishing a child support order, to send copies of child support orders and guideline calculations to the Child Support Administration, resulting in a significant operational impact and increased clerical workload across the court system.

MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, and the Secretary of Transportation is specifically tasked by the bill with cooperating with the Secretary of Human Services to adopt regulations implementing the act.

OAH is designated in the statute as the administrative forum for obligors appealing child support investigation findings regarding license suspension actions, and participates in adopting implementing regulations.
OAG provides legal representation and advice to DHS, CSA, and MVA regarding child support enforcement actions, administrative procedures, and statutory compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: The bill establishes Class BDR-DC (deluxe complex restaurant) and Class BRC (resort complex) beer and wine and beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Garrett County, along with associated license and issuing fees and catering options. It also updates hearing and application notice requirements for several temporary and festival alcoholic beverages licenses and authorizes nonprofit organizations, rather than clubs, to obtain Class C multiple day and multiple event licenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurants, resort complexes, nonprofit organizations, festival/event organizers, and patrons in Garrett County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Garrett County revenues increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that new deluxe complex restaurant, resort complex, and other licenses are issued; the exact revenue increase cannot be reliably estimated because the number of new licenses is unknown. Garrett County can handle administrative and enforcement duties using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and administering alcoholic beverage taxes. While House Bill 790 / Chapter 790 exclusively concerns local retail licenses, festival permits, and hearings administered by the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's overall alcoholic beverages regulatory framework and involves state-licensed wholesalers and manufacturers.

qa_results.bill_summary: The bill establishes uniform statutory definitions regarding military service across several Maryland Code articles, referencing federal standards under the U.S. Code. It broadens the application of various personnel, reemployment, and tax relief provisions (such as income tax abatements, military subtraction modifications, and property tax relief) to cover all uniformed services—including the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration—rather than only the armed forces.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, Office of the Comptroller, and the Maryland Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Active duty and reserve service members, veterans, and military families—particularly members of the U.S. Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration—as well as state and local government employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. While the bill expands access to state and local personnel benefits, tax abatements, and property tax relief, the newly eligible population (primarily PHS and NOAA commissioned officers) is small relative to the overall veteran population, allowing any fiscal impact to be absorbed within existing agency and local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article, which establishes the core definitions governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families (including definitions for 'active duty', 'active service member', 'armed forces', 'military family', 'reserve component', 'service member', 'uniformed services', and 'veteran') used across the Maryland Code.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and merit systems impacted by the bill, including reemployment and reinstatement rights for returning service members, veteran selection credits in state hiring, and paid leave for uniformed services training.

The Comptroller administers state tax laws and will be responsible for implementing the bill's tax provisions, which alter income tax subtraction modifications for military pay and retirement income, establish income tax abatements for service members dying in active service or public health emergencies, and update sales and use tax exemptions for veterans' organizations.

Members of the Maryland National Guard are directly impacted by the standardized definitions of reserve components and service members, which govern their state personnel reemployment protections, leave rights, and eligibility for state tax subtractions.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the state's military forces and National Guard members, the Adjutant General has an administrative interest in statutory updates affecting the rights, service credits, and protections of military personnel.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain charter, code, and commission counties in Maryland that impose development impact fees, surcharges, or excise taxes to report annually to the Maryland Department of Planning on the collection and expenditure of those revenues, make the report publicly available, and report local authorizing laws and subsequent amendments to the department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: County governments imposing development impact fees, surcharges, or excise taxes; property developers and homebuilders; and county residents and taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local governments can comply with the annual reporting requirements using existing resources, resulting in no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 698 specifically designates the Department of Planning (MDP) as the state entity to which Maryland counties must annually report data on the collection, expenditure, and location of local development impact fees, surcharges, and excise taxes, as well as copies of the local laws authorizing them.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'honorable discharge' for any State program of benefits, rights, or privileges to include discharges that are less than honorable if the Department of Veterans and Military Families determines the individual is eligible for State benefits under the criteria established in federal regulations (38 C.F.R. § 3.12).
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland military veterans with less than honorable discharges who meet federal discharge review criteria, making them eligible for State veteran benefits, rights, and programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations will not be materially affected. The Department of Veterans and Military Families can administer eligibility reviews and provide State veterans' benefits using existing budgeted resources. While some State programs may absorb minor costs if federal reimbursements are unavailable for certain non-federally recognized discharges, these costs are expected to be absorbed within existing general funds and no specific dollar amounts are estimated. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 699 directly tasks the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) and its Secretary with reviewing veterans' discharge documentation and determining eligibility for State veterans' benefits, rights, and privileges based on criteria in federal regulations (38 C.F.R. § 3.12).

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local county board of education to develop and publish on its website a list of all special education service delivery models provided to parentally-placed private school students within its jurisdiction, and to provide a written copy of the list upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: County boards of education (local school systems)
qa_results.stakeholders: Parentally-placed private school students with disabilities, their parents or guardians, private and religious schools, and local school systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local school systems can handle the publication requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's 24 local school systems and manages statewide policies, regulations, and federal compliance related to special education under IDEA, which directly pertains to the special education service delivery models local boards must publish.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include eligible Maryland residents attending the Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident graduate students attending the Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine, as well as students and participating institutions under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures or revenues. Program funding is as provided in the State budget ($1.2 million in FY 2026), meaning expanding eligibility redistributes existing scholarship funds across an additional institution rather than requiring new expenditures. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) administers the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, determines financial need criteria, establishes award guidelines, and allocates scholarship funds among eligible institutions.

As the administrator of state financial aid programs, the Commission is directly responsible for adopting regulations, establishing guidelines, and reallocating funds for the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include the newly eligible institution.

Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (such as the University of Maryland professional schools and the University of Baltimore School of Law) participate in this scholarship program, and the inclusion of an additional institution will affect their proportionate funding allocations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as Eric's ID Law, this bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to allow applicants for a driver's license, identification card, or moped operator's permit to indicate if they have a nonapparent disability, such as an intellectual or developmental disability. The MVA must place a notation on the credential without charging a fee or requiring proof of disability, conduct public outreach, restrict unauthorized disclosure of the information, and remove the notation upon request. Additionally, the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission must implement training for law enforcement regarding interactions with individuals who have this notation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with nonapparent disabilities (including developmental and intellectual disabilities) applying for or holding Maryland licenses, ID cards, or moped permits, advocacy groups, and law enforcement officers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2026 for one-time vendor costs to update credential templates, plus ongoing credential production costs of $1.39 per change (amounting to $69,500 per 50,000 credential holders). The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the required training with existing resources. State revenues and local government operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency responsible for updating applications, issuing credentials with the nonapparent disability notation, managing records and deletions, conducting public outreach, and ensuring data privacy protections.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund will incur the expenditures associated with credential redesign, vendor system updates, and card issuance.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to consult with the Department of State Police to implement law enforcement training regarding interactions with individuals who have a nonapparent disability notation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is tasked by the bill with implementing training for law enforcement concerning interactions with individuals displaying a nonapparent disability notation.

The department coordinates services and policy for Marylanders with disabilities and serves as a key stakeholder and resource regarding advocacy and outreach for developmental and intellectual disability communities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to issue one Class GSF (golf simulator facility) alcoholic beverages license to a person who holds one or more Class B licenses, with the GSF license counting toward the maximum limit of nine Class B licenses that may be issued to the same individual.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Harford County Class B alcoholic beverages licensees, golf simulator facility businesses, and their patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State finances and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations, with a minimal effect on small businesses. Class GSF licenses have an annual fee of $1,500.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and collects alcoholic beverage excise taxes. While this bill strictly applies to local licensing administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it falls within the broad subject area of alcohol regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill removes outdated references to the Comptroller of Maryland concerning recordkeeping and reporting requirements for performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverages licenses in Harford County, repealing the Comptroller's power to suspend licenses without a hearing. It also grants the Harford County Board of License Commissioners discretionary authority, rather than a mandatory requirement, to summon a license holder to a hearing and impose fines or license suspensions for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverage license holders in Harford County, the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or Harford County operations or finances. While the local licensing board has discretion to impose fines between $250 and $2,000 for violations, any fiscal impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly removes obsolete statutory references to the Comptroller of Maryland regarding record-keeping, reporting, and audit requirements for performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverage licenses in Harford County, and repeals the Comptroller's former authority to suspend such licenses without a hearing.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the population quota threshold from 4,000 to 4,750 individuals per license used by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to determine the maximum number of Class A, Class A-1, and Class A-2 off-sale alcoholic beverages licenses issued.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage retail establishments, prospective license applicants, and residents of Harford County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly referenced in the statutory text as the entity that specifies the county population figures used to calculate the alcoholic beverages license quota for Harford County.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program by including the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) under the definition of a public housing agency (PHA), permitting PHAs to administer the program under local administrative plans, and allowing DHCD to project-base up to 100% of voucher units.
