It also removes the requirement that priority categories of families be prioritized equally, adjusts inspection frequency requirements from annual to at least biennial, and increases the share of program funding distributed to local PHAs for administrative staffing costs from 6% to 15% (or the federal de minimis rate, whichever is greater).
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income households and families eligible for rental assistance (including children, young adults transitioning out of foster care, veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly), local public housing agencies, and participating rental property owners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because overall program funding remains unchanged. Local government revenues for public housing agencies increase due to higher administrative cost distributions (increasing from 6% to the greater of 15% or the federal de minimis rate of direct costs) to defray staffing expenses, while local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 716 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It alters the administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program housed within DHCD, including defining DHCD as a public housing agency, allowing project-basing of voucher units, adjusting inspection requirements, and modifying the distribution of administrative funds to local public housing agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies various provisions governing the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and public lands management. It establishes the Land and Property Management Program to process property transactions and employee housing, authorizes DNR to create affiliated nonprofit foundations to solicit contributions and support public land initiatives, and mandates annual budget requests for at least one permanent staff position per 400 acres of newly acquired fee-simple land. Additionally, it permits the transfer of Program Open Space (POS) land acquisition balances over $80 million to cover operating, maintenance, and Natural Resources Police costs, while granting local jurisdictions greater flexibility and revised matching requirements for local POS development projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland public lands, local governments managing parks and recreation, Department of Natural Resources personnel, and commercial contractors and vendors providing conservation and park development services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $212,543 in FY 2026 to fund two positions in the newly codified Land and Property Management Program (funds are included in the FY 2026 budget contingent on this legislation). Beginning in FY 2027, expenditures escalate as additional staff are requested and hired based on land acquisition formulas, reaching an estimated $1,875,970 in FY 2030 for a cumulative 18 positions. Additional special fund expenditures may occur if excess POS acquisition fund balances over $80 million are transferred to operational uses. State revenues are not directly affected. Local governments benefit from increased flexibility to direct up to 100% of local POS allocations toward development projects, reduced local matching requirements on projects receiving federal or other state funds, and the ability to apply up to $125,000 in acquisition funding toward 5-year recreation plan updates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which establishes a Land and Property Management Program within DNR, authorizes DNR to create affiliated foundations, modifies real property interest acquisition processes, mandates budget requests for land management positions, and alters the use of Program Open Space funds.

The Board of Public Works has direct statutory authority under the bill to approve DNR's real property acquisitions, authorize real property interest disposals/exchanges, approve an easement valuation system, and supervise appropriations for land acquisitions.

DNR is statutorily required to submit funding requests to DBM in its annual budget requests to create new permanent, classified positions based on acres of fee simple real property interests acquired.

The Maryland Department of Planning, in conjunction with DNR, is responsible for certifying whether local jurisdictions have met their land acquisition goals under approved local land preservation and recreation plans to allow use of Program Open Space funds for development projects.
The Attorney General is required to review policies developed by DNR for operating affiliated foundations for form and legal sufficiency and, if appropriate, approve them.

The State Ethics Commission is required to review and approve affiliated foundation policies concerning conflicts of interest, receive notification of DNR officials/employees serving on foundations, evaluate potential concerns, and receive annual reports on foundation governance.
DNR must consult with the Department of General Services to develop a system for appraisal reviews for real property interest acquisitions as part of its regulatory implementation.

The bill authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Program Open Space State land acquisition balance to DNR under specified conditions and mandates that DNR submit an annual report on affiliated foundations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor and assess potential and actual federal changes to the Affordable Care Act, the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act, Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, Medicare, and the Maryland All-Payer Model, and to make recommendations for state and local actions to maintain access to affordable health coverage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services, Maryland Department of Health, and Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents enrolled in or seeking health insurance coverage (including Medicaid, Medicare, MCHP, and ACA marketplace plans), health insurance carriers, healthcare providers, employers, and state health regulatory agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Department of Legislative Services, Maryland Department of Health, and Maryland Insurance Administration can jointly staff the commission and prepare required reports using existing budgeted resources. Commission members are entitled to standard travel expense reimbursement, but receive no compensation. State revenues are not affected. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the Commission, and the Maryland Department of Health is explicitly required to jointly provide staff and operational support for the Commission.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) serves on the Commission, and the Maryland Insurance Administration is mandated to jointly staff the Commission alongside MDH and DLS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission, a temporary advisory commission authorized to study health coverage issues and make legislative recommendations through June 30, 2029.
The Executive Director of HSCRC (or designee) is named as a Commission member, and the Commission is specifically tasked with monitoring and assessing impacts on the Maryland All-Payer Model.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (or designee) serves on the Commission, which is tasked with monitoring and addressing potential changes to the ACA and state health insurance markets.
The Governor is responsible for appointing four members to the Commission and receives the Commission's annual reports and legislative proposals.
The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the four gubernatorial appointments to the newly created Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the State Boat Act by revising the definitions of personal watercraft and personal flotation devices, eliminating newspaper advertising and petition hearing requirements for proposed boating regulations, and establishing authority to set speed zones by public notice for emergent or restricted situations. It also increases several vessel-related fees—including certificates of title, two-year certificates of number, Maryland use stickers, and manufacturer/dealer licenses—creates a voluntary nonmotorized vessel decal, and expands funding thresholds and expenditure flexibility under the Waterway Improvement Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Recreational boaters, vessel owners, boat dealers and manufacturers, livery vessel operators, and local governments applying for waterway improvement funding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources increase by approximately $4.9 million annually beginning in FY 2026 due to increased vessel registration, titling, and dealer fees. Federal fund revenues may increase modestly starting in FY 2027 based on vessel counts. Special fund expenditures are projected to increase by $100,000 or more annually due to higher expenditure limits for small Waterway Improvement Fund (WIF) projects, slightly offset by minor savings from eliminated newspaper publication requirements. Local governments benefit from expanded access to 100% and 50% WIF grants for marina construction and small emergency projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 719 is a departmental bill sponsored on behalf of the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It directly alters provisions of the State Boat Act administered by DNR, including fee structures for vessel titling, certificates of number, dealer licenses, Maryland use stickers, and the Waterway Improvement Fund, resulting in an estimated $4.9 million annual increase in DNR special fund revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals provisions establishing the Somers Cove Marina Commission and the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund, transferring the management, operations, and property oversight of the marina directly to the Department of Natural Resources. It authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to lease property, procure operating contracts, employ staff, and assess fees, while directing marina revenues into the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund and establishing the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Boaters, slip holders at Somers Cove Marina, marina employees and contractors, the commercial fishing industry, tourism and business communities in Somerset County and the City of Crisfield.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State special fund revenues and expenditures may increase significantly (potentially exceeding $1,000,000 annually if DNR operates the marina directly, or less if operations are leased out to a third party). Special fund revenues also increase in FY 2026 from the transfer of the remaining balance of the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund (estimated illustratively at $336,671). General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 due to interest earnings. Local finances for Somerset County and the City of Crisfield are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which repeals the independent Somers Cove Marina Commission and transfers full management, operations, maintenance, leasing, fee-setting, and staffing authority of the Somers Cove Marina to the department and the Secretary of Natural Resources. DNR also administers the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund, which receives all marina revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the existing Somers Cove Marina Commission and creates a new advisory body, the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission within DNR, tasked with advising the Secretary on marina operations, management, and development.

The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund separately, invest money of the fund, and allocate interest earnings back to the fund as exempted under the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill specifically designates the Comptroller to account for the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund.

DBM was consulted as an information source on the bill regarding fiscal and personnel impacts, as the bill authorizes new state employee compensation structures, potential new state positions, and alterations to special fund expenditures through the state budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports to specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, regarding the revision of COMAR 10.63, improvements to the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs, and enhanced procedures for the certification, monitoring, and oversight of recovery residences. The reports must also analyze how regulatory revisions and other departmental actions will prevent incidents such as patient relapse and death in provider-owned housing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Substance use disorder treatment program operators, recovery residence operators, and individuals receiving substance use disorder treatment or living in recovery residences.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Health can likely fulfill the bill's reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. Although the department advised it would require four staff members costing $318,716 in fiscal 2026, the Department of Legislative Services determined that additional personnel are not necessitated by the bill because it mandates reporting rather than implementation. State revenues are unaffected. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports to General Assembly committees regarding the revision of COMAR 10.63, improvements to oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs, and certification and monitoring procedures for recovery residences.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to issue licenses or certifications within 15 business days to qualified dentists, dental hygienists, and dental radiation technologists who are licensed or certified in another state. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and submit a plan to authorize certain individuals who left federal employment after January 20, 2025, and hold equivalent out-of-state licenses, to practice health occupations in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed dentists, dental hygienists, dental radiation technologists, and former federal health occupation employees seeking authorization to practice in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Dental Examiners and the Maryland Department of Health can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Any impact on special fund revenues from application fees is indeterminate but anticipated to be minimal. There is no direct effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Dental Examiners and the health occupations boards. Under the bill, the department is directly required to develop and submit a plan for authorizing certain former federal employees licensed in other states to practice health occupations in Maryland, and its Board of Dental Examiners must issue licenses and certifications within 15 business days to qualified out-of-state applicants.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the allowable uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to include covering operating expenses and personnel costs for investigations, enforcement actions, and related activities conducted by the Opioids Enforcement Unit within the Office of the Attorney General to recover opioid-related judgments and settlements. It also requires an annual activity and case disposition report by the Attorney General.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General (Opioids Enforcement Unit), Maryland's Office of Overdose Response, local health departments, community recovery organizations, and individuals receiving opioid prevention and treatment services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The FY 2026 budget includes a $1.5 million special fund appropriation from the Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) for the Office of the Attorney General's Opioids Enforcement Unit, an allocation assumed to continue through FY 2029. While this shifts $1.5 million annually from discretionary opioid abatement grant programs managed by the Maryland's Office of Overdose Response to the Attorney General, there is likely no net impact on total ORF expenditures, and state revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to support the operating expenses and personnel costs of the Opioids Enforcement Unit within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG), authorizing an estimated $1.5 million annually in special fund expenditures from FY 2026 through FY 2029, and establishes annual reporting requirements for OAG.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) manages and distributes Opioid Restitution Fund revenues. Expanding the fund's allowable uses to support OAG's enforcement unit reduces the amount of discretionary grant funding available for MDH and community-level substance use disorder abatement programs by $1.5 million annually.

The bill mandates that the Office of the Attorney General submit an annual report to the Governor by October 1 detailing the status, investigations, lawsuits, and case dispositions of the Opioids Enforcement Unit.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill aligns the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund with the purposes specified in settlement agreements and court judgments involving the opioid industry, including addressing racial and socioeconomic disparities in access to prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services. It also updates the Maryland Department of Health's Overdose Response Program training to emphasize restoring breathing, avoiding withdrawal, and providing compassionate post-overdose support and care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with substance use disorders or at risk of opioid overdose, communities facing racial and socioeconomic healthcare disparities, harm reduction and treatment providers, and community-based nonprofit recovery organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal or operational impact on State or local finances. It modifies the permissible uses of existing Opioid Restitution Fund monies to align with allowable uses under national settlement agreements without affecting existing funded programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Overdose Response Program (ORP), is authorized to alter training components under the program, and manages and distributes monies from the Opioid Restitution Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references and assigns decision-making authority to the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council to review and approve distributions for non-evidence-based pilot programs and demonstration studies.

The Office of the Attorney General negotiates and enforces the settlement agreements and judgments against the opioid industry that dictate the terms and allowable expenditures of the Opioid Restitution Fund, and served as an information source on the bill.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutory custodian tasked with accounting for the Opioid Restitution Fund pursuant to the reenacted provisions of the bill.
The State Treasurer is statutory custodian responsible for holding the Opioid Restitution Fund separately pursuant to the reenacted provisions of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Connectivity Coalition to improve wildlife habitat connectivity, protect threatened and endangered species, and reduce collisions between vehicles and wildlife. The bill gives the State Highway Administration final decision-making authority over wildlife crossing projects, requires reporting on wildlife crossings in the Consolidated Transportation Program, and mandates that local jurisdictions consider wildlife movement and habitat connectivity in their comprehensive plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists, wildlife populations (especially threatened and endangered species), local governments, and transportation and conservation agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund special fund expenditures increase by an estimated $50,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 for the State Highway Administration to hire consultant services for coalition research and staffing. The Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland Department of Planning can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government operations and finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administrator (or designee) serves as Chair of the newly created Maryland Connectivity Coalition, co-adopts rules for the coalition with DNR, maintains final decision-making authority over the placement, funding, and design of wildlife crossings, and must report on wildlife crossings in each Consolidated Transportation Plan, resulting in an estimated $50,000 annual fiscal impact from the Transportation Trust Fund.

The Secretary of Natural Resources is a designated statutory member of the Maryland Connectivity Coalition, co-adopts coalition rules with the State Highway Administration, and coordinates with the Department of Planning to supply local governments with wildlife connectivity and crossing information.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT's Consolidated Transportation Program must incorporate required wildlife crossing reports, and the bill results in ongoing expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill mandates the Department of Planning to coordinate with the Department of Natural Resources and the State Highway Administration to provide updated information on habitat connectivity and planned wildlife crossings to charter counties and local jurisdictions for their comprehensive plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes the Maryland Connectivity Coalition as a permanent interagency and stakeholder body tasked with setting project criteria, performance metrics, and funding recommendations for wildlife habitat connectivity.

Under existing Land Use provisions referenced in the bill, the Department of the Environment reviews local comprehensive plan sensitive areas elements, which now must incorporate wildlife movement and habitat connectivity considerations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the statutory framework governing the funding, management, and oversight of major information technology (IT) development projects across Maryland State executive branch agencies. It establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience (MODE), along with the Maryland Digital Service Unit and the Major IT Development Project Oversight Division within the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), and creates the Information Technology Advisory Board to advise the General Assembly while repealing the Modernize Maryland Commission. Additionally, the bill strengthens oversight and reporting requirements, mandates a public online dashboard for major IT projects, and authorizes the withholding or reallocation of project funds under specified conditions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: State executive branch agencies, State IT personnel and contractors, and Maryland residents accessing State digital services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) increase by at least $4,300,000 in FY 2026 to support staffing for the new Maryland Office of Digital Experience, with out-year expenditures likely increasing by at least that amount. General funds could be required if ITIF resources are insufficient. Potential cost reductions from IT efficiencies and economies of scale across agencies cannot be reliably estimated. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The legislation substantially alters and expands DoIT's oversight over major IT development projects, establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience (MODE), the Maryland Digital Service Unit, and the Major IT Development Project Oversight Division within the department, and mandates the creation of a public project dashboard.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is directly tasked with fiscal oversight alongside DoIT, including withholding and reallocating major IT project funds upon recommendation, approving compensation levels for MODE staff, and executing budget amendment transfers of ITIF funds.

DGS is required to consult on the procurement assessment for IT modernization projects and submit recurring reports to legislative committees on projects over $1,000,000 under the Statewide Agile Resources and Teams master contract.

Managing units must provide notice to the Board of Public Works within 30 days of awarding contracts for major IT development projects affirming project team identification, DoIT approval, and agency head accountability.

The Governor is authorized to transfer up to 50 positions to the newly created Maryland Office of Digital Experience, approves budget amendment transfers with the Secretary of Budget and Management, and receives reports when IT project funding is withheld.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals the Modernize Maryland Commission and alters statutory advisory frameworks regarding state IT modernization.

Members of the newly established Information Technology Advisory Board are made subject to the Public Ethics Law and must submit specific employment and financial interest disclosures to the State Ethics Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as the Sergeant Patrick Kepp Act, this bill alters penalties, offenses, and point assessments for reckless, negligent, and aggressive driving. It classifies driving 30 miles per hour or more over the posted speed limit as reckless driving, designates reckless driving as an incarcerable offense punishable by up to 60 days in jail and/or a $1,000 fine, increases maximum fines for negligent driving ($750) and aggressive driving ($1,000), increases driver's license points for negligent driving and extreme speeding, and expands the list of violations that qualify toward an aggressive driving charge.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and the Office of the Public Defender (OPD)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland motorists, individuals cited for traffic infractions (specifically speeding 30+ mph, reckless driving, negligent driving, or aggressive driving), indigent defendants facing traffic-related criminal charges, pedestrian and bicycle road users, and law enforcement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by at least $534,800 in FY 2026 (growing to $725,500 by FY 2030) for the Office of the Public Defender to add staff for reckless driving cases, which become incarcerable must-appear offenses. General Fund revenues increase minimally from higher District Court fines. State correctional expenditures may see a minimal increase for Baltimore City detentions. Local governments may experience minimal increases in revenues from circuit court fines and minimal increases in detention facility expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the points assessed by MVA against individuals' driver's licenses for negligent driving convictions and speeding 30 mph or more above the posted speed limit, leading to increased license suspensions and revocations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill makes reckless driving an incarcerable offense (up to 60 days imprisonment), indigent defendants charged with reckless driving become eligible for public defender representation, resulting in a substantial caseload increase and a fiscal impact of over $534,000 annually for additional attorneys and staff.

Reckless driving becomes a must-appear violation in District Court and Circuit Courts due to potential incarceration, eliminating prepayment options and increasing court appearances and trials managed by the Judiciary.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration of Maryland's Vehicle Law and the Transportation Trust Fund.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws on Maryland roadways, MSP will enforce the expanded definitions of reckless and aggressive driving.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The addition of a 60-day incarceration penalty for reckless driving may result in a minimal increase in commitments to State-operated correctional facilities, primarily the Baltimore Pretrial Complex.
OAH adjudicates administrative appeals of driver's license suspensions and revocations initiated by the MVA following points assessments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists to issue behavior analyst licenses within specified timeframes (30 days for complete applications, 50 days for incomplete applications once additional information is received) and to provide regular email status notifications to applicants.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for behavior analyst licensure and practicing behavior analysts in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists is a health occupations licensing board operating under the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the board's licensure application processing times and notification requirements for behavior analysts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to approve the transfer of up to five existing Class B or Class D alcoholic beverages licenses from an eligible transferor election district to other election districts in the county between June 1, 2025, and May 31, 2028, subject to certain economic and district caps and requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders, commercial property owners, and business communities within election districts in Baltimore County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Locally, the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners can administer license transfers using existing resources. County revenues are unaffected because no new licenses are created, only transferred between election districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds Washington County to the list of Maryland counties that exempt agricultural buildings used for agritourism from Maryland Building Performance Standards, and allows existing agricultural buildings used for agritourism to be exempt from change-of-occupancy building permit requirements if occupancy does not exceed 200 people and egress standards are met.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Farm owners and agricultural business operators in Washington County, agritourism visitors, and Washington County local code and permitting authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or Washington County finances or operations. The effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor adopts and oversees the Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS) under the Public Safety Article and is responsible for adopting regulations governing building permit and occupancy exemptions for agritourism buildings.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture promotes and supports agribusiness and the economic viability of farms, including agritourism operations affected by the building code exemptions in Washington County.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the local property tax credit in Washington County for economic development projects by expanding eligible property to include renovated premises, altering the required job creation and capital investment thresholds, and adjusting the percentage and duration of property tax credits granted to qualifying new and existing businesses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing body of Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: New and existing business entities in Washington County investing in real property and creating jobs, commercial property lessors, and Washington County taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Washington County property tax revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $710,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2026 due to the reduction in tax credits provided under the adjusted credit schedules and higher qualification thresholds. County expenditures are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to publish hearing notices for proposed regulatory changes and license applications, as well as decisions on certain license applications, either in a newspaper of general circulation or online, rather than requiring both.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants, existing license holders, local newspaper publishers, and the Harford County public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations. The effect on small businesses is minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits cooperative housing corporations, condominium associations, and homeowners associations from requiring sensitive personal information—such as Social Security numbers, citizenship or immigration status, birth certificates, or medical records—as a condition for residents, owners, occupants, or their guests and children to access or use shared recreational common areas.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, unit and lot owners, occupants, and their guests and children in common ownership communities, as well as cooperative housing corporations, condominium associations, and homeowners associations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts statutory restrictions governing common ownership communities (cooperatives, condominiums, and homeowners associations). Any legal disputes or civil enforcement actions arising from these provisions fall under the jurisdiction of the state court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, which was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the discretionary annual budget authorization for the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program from at least $500,000 to at least $1.0 million. It also authorizes the Secretary of Health to allocate up to 20% of the program's funds to research centers, including the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing, to collect, analyze, and process outcome data to assess and enhance the effectiveness of the cancer screenings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional and volunteer firefighters, local fire departments and volunteer fire companies, and academic medical research centers (including the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $400,000 annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030, assuming the full discretionary funding level of $1.0 million is provided above the $600,000 already budgeted. In FY 2026, program spending includes $59,757 for a part-time program administrator, up to $200,000 for research center data analysis, and at least $740,000 in grants. State revenues are unaffected. Local fire departments and companies may experience increased grant revenues and operational expenditures to conduct innovative cancer screenings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program, manages the grant distribution, handles program administrative requirements (including hiring additional personnel), and is authorized to allocate up to 20% of program funds to research centers.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Secretary of Health to allocate up to 20% of program funds (potentially up to $200,000 annually) to support academic medical research centers, specifically naming the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing for data collection, analysis, and processing.

The bill amends statutory provisions that govern the amount the Governor is authorized to include in the annual state budget for the program, increasing the authorization from at least $500,000 to at least $1,000,000.

As the principal agency overseeing state budget development and fiscal planning for the executive branch, DBM is responsible for implementing the altered discretionary budget authorization for the program.
Program appropriations, expenditures, and grant funds remain subject to statutory audit by the Office of Legislative Audits under the Health - General Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 761 updates the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act by making virtual currency subject to abandoned property laws and requiring holders to liquidate it after five years of inactivity. The bill also establishes standards for determining apparent owner interest and addresses, requires life insurers to run annual comparisons against the Death Master File, lowers the threshold for publishing unclaimed property notices from $100 to $50, permits the Comptroller to apply unclaimed property toward outstanding state and local debts, and authorizes the Comptroller to retain up to $5 million for IT and cybersecurity modernization.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and apparent owners of abandoned property, financial organizations, insurers, virtual currency holders, businesses holding unclaimed funds, and the Comptroller's Office.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are expected to increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2026 due to expanded abandoned property categories such as virtual currency, partially balanced by provisions recognizing additional account activity as continued ownership. Special fund expenditures will increase as the Comptroller's Office is authorized to retain up to $5.0 million from proceeds for information technology and cybersecurity costs, as well as an amount reasonably sufficient to pay claims. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland acts as the Administrator of the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act, requested the legislation, and is the primary implementing agency. The bill alters definitions, establishes procedures for handling virtual currency and retirement accounts, adjusts claim processes, and authorizes the Comptroller to retain up to $5 million from unclaimed property proceeds for information technology and cybersecurity.

The bill establishes statutory criteria and requirements for life insurance and annuity holders regarding the Social Security Administration Death Master File and presumptions of abandonment, directly referencing rules and policies adopted by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

The bill alters statutory deadlines and timeframes under which claimants aggrieved by the Comptroller's determinations regarding abandoned property may file actions in the circuit courts to establish their claims.

The Department of Labor regulates state financial institutions and banking organizations that hold customer deposits and are subject to the revised dormancy, communication, and abandonment provisions under the Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland hospitals to sell patient medical debt to a governmental unit, a contractor of that unit, or a tax-exempt nonprofit organization for the sole purpose of canceling the debt. It establishes eligibility criteria for debt that can be sold, requires hospitals to dismiss pending collection actions and cease collection activities on sold debt, requires purchasers to notify patients and vacate adverse credit reports or judgments, and mandates related reporting to the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC).
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals, qualifying patients with outstanding medical debt (family income at or below 500% of the federal poverty level or medical debt exceeding 5% of family income), nonprofit organizations purchasing medical debt, and state and local governmental units.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: HSCRC can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State and local government expenditures increase to the extent that any governmental unit elects to purchase patient medical debt for cancellation from FY 2026 through FY 2028. Any impact on the uncompensated care pool and hospital rates is indeterminate but expected to be minimal overall, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, including receiving hospital debt collection policies and reports, monitoring hospital compliance, offsetting uncompensated care amounts, and posting reporting data on its website.

HSCRC is an independent commission housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). Additionally, MDH administers the Medicaid program, which participates in the state's hospital all-payer rate-setting system and could experience indirect rate adjustments resulting from changes to hospital uncompensated care balances.

The Office of the Attorney General (specifically its Consumer Protection Division) enforces Maryland consumer protection and debt collection laws and served as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 767 establishes additional procedures and notice requirements following the issuance of a warrant of restitution in residential eviction cases (failure to pay rent, breach of lease, and tenant holding over). Landlords must provide written notice of scheduled repossession at least six days in advance by mail, door posting with a timestamped photograph, and electronic communication, while permitting landlords to charge up to $5 for notice expenses. It also details sheriff verification procedures, court actions for noncompliance, and tenant civil remedies for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland and county sheriffs or constables
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential landlords, residential tenants facing eviction, and county sheriffs and constables executing warrants of restitution
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Landlords may charge tenants up to $5 for expenses incurred in providing notice. Small business landlords may experience meaningful operational impacts and exposure to civil remedies for noncompliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters judicial procedures in the District Court regarding summary ejectment, warrants of restitution, and eviction notice filings, requiring court clerks to receive documentation, the court to vacate warrants if proper notice was not given, and notices to include information about the District Court Help Center.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for designation as a "hunger-free campus" by the Maryland Higher Education Commission to include qualifying private two-year and four-year institutions of higher education, while prohibiting those private institutions from receiving grant funding under the Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Private two-year and four-year institutions of higher education and their students experiencing food insecurity.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can designate private institutions as hunger-free campuses using existing resources, and overall grant funding and revenues are not affected because private institutions are ineligible to receive grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) administers the Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program. HB 774 directly requires MHEC to expand the 'hunger-free campus' designation to qualifying private institutions of higher education while ensuring they remain ineligible for program grant funding.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission administers the Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program and is the primary entity tasked with designating qualifying private institutions of higher education as hunger-free campuses under the provisions of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Correction to notify specific state legislators, the local governing body, and the local chief executive or Mayor whenever an incarcerated individual dies in a Division of Correction facility. The notification must include the cause of death while excluding protected health information in accordance with regulations compliant with HIPAA.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (Division of Correction)
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in state correctional facilities, state legislators, and local elected officials (county executives, county councils, and the Mayor/City Council of Baltimore).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may increase minimally to provide the required notifications. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 775 directly impacts the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) by requiring its Commissioner of Correction to provide formal notification to designated state and local officials upon the death of an incarcerated individual in a Division of Correction facility, and mandates that DPSCS adopt HIPAA-compliant regulations to implement these requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates, clarifies, and standardizes provisions of the Maryland Medical Practice Act and the Maryland Physician Assistants Act governing the State Board of Physicians and allied health professionals. It alters licensure requirements, reporting and notification mandates, and disciplinary grounds and procedures; standardizes the structure, membership, and duties of allied health advisory committees; authorizes new administrative penalties and raises existing civil penalties for violations such as employing unlicensed individuals or knowingly failing to report adverse actions; and expands the physician rehabilitation program into a comprehensive program covering all licensees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: Physicians, physician assistants, allied health professionals (such as respiratory care practitioners, polysomnographic technologists, athletic trainers, perfusionists, naturopathic doctors, and genetic counselors), healthcare employers and facilities, and Maryland healthcare patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Board of Physicians Fund and General Fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning as early as FY 2026 due to new administrative penalties and increased civil fines. The Maryland Board of Physicians and the Office of Administrative Hearings can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians and its advisory committees operate within the Department of Health. The bill substantially revises the Maryland Medical Practice Act and the Maryland Physician Assistants Act, modifying licensing requirements, disciplinary panel procedures, reporting mandates, and administrative penalties for physicians, physician assistants, and allied health professionals.

The bill alters disciplinary hearing procedures and explicitly mandates that complaints proceeding to an evidentiary hearing be referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH). The fiscal note highlights that this will increase hearings delegated to OAH and necessitate Administrative Law Judge training.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the statutory requirement that the Board of Physicians include a blank panel data sheet supplied by the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office with every license renewal notice.

The bill governs the collection and distribution of licensing fees and civil penalties paid to the Comptroller, specifically detailing the allocation between the Board of Physicians Fund and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians and Physician Assistants.

The bill maintains statutory provisions directing the Legislative Auditor to audit the accounts and transactions of the Board of Physicians Fund and the Rehabilitation Program, as well as access records upon request.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to conduct a comprehensive study and evaluation on how best to detect deadly weapons in public middle and high schools and rapidly report them to law enforcement, evaluating current security infrastructure, cameras, metal detectors, and safety software, with interim and final reports due to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, respectively.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public middle and high school students, teachers, administrators, local school systems, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase in FY 2026 and FY 2027 if the Maryland Center for School Safety requires an outside consultant with specialized expertise to evaluate weapons-detection strategies and technology, though a reliable estimate is unavailable; there is no effect on State revenues. Local school systems can likely participate in the required study and evaluation using existing resources, with no local revenue impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) to conduct a comprehensive study and evaluation on detecting deadly weapons in public middle and high schools, evaluate current security infrastructure across all public school systems, assess weapons detection technologies, and submit interim and final reports to the General Assembly.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's 24 public school systems that are subject to the evaluation, houses the Maryland Center for School Safety as an independent unit within the department, and served as an information source for the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands mandatory continuing education requirements for health care professionals by requiring applicants for a license or certificate renewal to complete an approved training program covering both implicit bias and structural racism for their first renewal after April 1, 2026. It also directs the Cultural and Linguistic Health Care Professional Competency Program, in coordination with the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, to approve qualifying training programs and authorizes health occupations boards to grant continuing education credits for them.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (specifically the Cultural and Linguistic Health Care Professional Competency Program and the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities) and Maryland health occupations licensing boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed and certified health care professionals in Maryland, health occupations licensing boards, and patients receiving health care services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026 for contractual support to review and approve training programs. Special fund expenditures for health occupations boards may increase by between $1,500 and $30,000 in FY 2026 for IT modifications to licensing software to accommodate the updated attestation. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) houses the health occupations licensing boards, the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, and the Cultural and Linguistic Health Care Professional Competency Program, which are responsible for identifying and approving the training programs and updating renewal requirements for licensed health professionals.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters alcoholic beverages license regulations in Baltimore City, primarily in the 46th district. It authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to waive the 40% food sales receipt requirement for restaurants in a specific bounded area and permits expansion onto noncontiguous properties with a City use permit. It expands conditional license issuance/renewal based on a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a community association to cover all alcoholic beverage license types, and requires an MOU for licenses near schools or places of worship in a certain area. Additionally, it extends the expiration dates for several specified licenses to facilitate transfers of ownership or location, including five Class B licenses at Harborplace through June 30, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders, restaurant owners, community associations, places of worship, schools, and patrons in Baltimore City (specifically in the 46th legislative district, Harborplace, and downtown Baltimore).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no State fiscal effect and does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. The small business effect is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller has general regulatory oversight over the alcoholic beverages industry in Maryland and collects state taxes. Although this bill specifically alters local retail licensing and operations administered by the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City, it touches upon alcoholic beverages administration and preserves liability for unpaid state personal property taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits common ownership communities—including cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations—and local jurisdictions from prohibiting or restricting the operation of family child care homes or large family child care homes, or limiting the number of children in care below the threshold authorized by the Maryland State Department of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Family child care providers, families seeking child care, common ownership communities (HOAs, condominiums, and housing cooperatives), and local zoning authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, nor directly affect local government finances. It may have an operational impact on local governments by preempting their authority to enforce local capacity limitations or related regulations on family child care homes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) regulates, registers, and licenses family child care homes and sets authorized child capacity limits. The bill directly ties common ownership community rules and local zoning restrictions to the capacity limits established and authorized by MSDE.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides guidance and data on local land use planning and zoning policies. The bill amends the Land Use Article to prohibit local jurisdictions from restricting family child care capacities below state-authorized levels.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Appellate Court of Maryland to hold court sessions at secondary and postsecondary educational institutions throughout the State, as designated by the Chief Judge in conjunction with school administrations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Students, faculty, community members, secondary and postsecondary educational institutions, and litigants appearing before the Appellate Court of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by authorizing the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland to designate sessions to be held at secondary and postsecondary educational institutions across the State, supported administratively and operationally by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The bill allows the Appellate Court of Maryland to hold official court sessions at secondary educational institutions in Maryland in conjunction with school administrations.
The bill authorizes the Appellate Court to hold sessions at postsecondary educational institutions throughout Maryland in coordination with institutional administrations.
The bill expands the authority of the Appellate Court to hold court sessions on campuses across Maryland postsecondary educational institutions, which includes USM member institutions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals an obsolete statutory requirement that the State Reporter secure a copyright for the State of Maryland for published opinions of the Supreme Court of Maryland and the Appellate Court of Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Reporter
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland Judiciary, the State Reporter, legal professionals, and members of the public seeking access to court opinions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill reflects current practice by repealing an obsolete provision in accordance with federal copyright law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly relates to the operations of the Judicial Branch and the State Reporter, who prepares official case reports under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Maryland. The Administrative Office of the Courts requested this legislation to remove an obsolete statutory requirement concerning copyright for appellate court opinions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment authorizing the chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to recall a former member to serve as a temporary substitute, or to request that the Governor appoint a temporary substitute member or extend an existing member's term, in the event of a member's recusal, disqualification, or term expiration without a replacement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and former members of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, Maryland state judges and justices subject to commission proceedings, and Maryland voters.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: If approved by voters at the November 2026 general election, the Commission on Judicial Disabilities will experience operational efficiencies. There is otherwise no material fiscal impact on State finances or operations, and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly affects the operations and membership of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities within the Judicial Department.
The bill authorizes the Governor, upon request of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities chair, to appoint temporary substitute members or extend the terms of current members.
The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be placed on the statewide ballot and administered by the State Board of Elections for the November 2026 general election.

As the office assisting the Governor with vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, it is involved when the Governor is requested to appoint temporary substitute members to the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires county tax collectors to include a separate insert with each property tax bill providing information on State and local installment payment programs for property taxes, and to publish the same information conspicuously on their websites. It also requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to include program descriptions and enrollment instructions on its website and design the standard insert, while requiring tax sale notices to include information about installment payment plans for overdue taxes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and local tax collectors
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, residential property taxpayers (especially those with delinquent taxes), and county tax collectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as SDAT can implement the requirements with existing resources. Local county expenditures are estimated to increase by approximately $500,000 annually starting in FY 2027 to cover the costs of printing and mailing the additional insert with property tax bills. Local revenues are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Somerset County to impose an annual emergency services property tax on all property subject to the county property tax to fund fire, rescue, and emergency medical services, following advance notice and a public hearing held during the annual budget hearing.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Somerset County
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners in Somerset County, local fire, rescue, and emergency medical services providers, and Somerset County residents receiving emergency services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Local effect is a potential increase in Somerset County property tax revenues depending on the tax rate imposed by the county commissioners. Based on the current tax base, each 1 cent increase generates approximately $170,000 from real property and $16,825 from personal property. County expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that unpaid emergency services taxes become liens and subject property to tax sales in accordance with Title 14, Subtitle 8 of the Tax - Property Article, which involves circuit court foreclosure and tax sale proceedings managed within the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue, sell, and deliver up to $30.0 million in academic facilities bonds to finance and refinance capital facilities renewal projects across the system ($25.0 million) and campuswide building systems and infrastructure improvements at the University of Maryland, College Park ($5.0 million).
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, students, faculty, and staff, particularly at the University of Maryland, College Park.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Revenues and expenditures from bond proceeds increase by $30.0 million in FY 2026 for capital projects. Beginning in FY 2027, higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $2.5 million annually for 20 years to pay debt service on the bonds. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue $30 million in academic facilities bonds to finance campuswide improvements at UMCP and systemwide facility renewal projects.
The Board of Public Works reviews and approves significant state capital projects, procurements, and contracts related to state higher education facility renewals and improvements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for public service employers to certify employment under the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program, including adopting hours-worked calculation methods that maximize full-time status determinations (specifically setting credit-hour conversion rules for higher education faculty). It requires employers to certify employment without unreasonable delay upon employee request or separation and directs the Student Loan Ombudsman to develop PSLF awareness materials for public service employers to distribute to employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Student Loan Ombudsman in the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and former employees of public service employers (including State and local government employees, adjunct and tenured higher education professors, and 501(c)(3) nonprofit staff) eligible for PSLF, as well as qualifying public service employers across Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies, including the Student Loan Ombudsman and the Department of Budget and Management, can handle the bill's implementation and distribution requirements with existing budgeted resources. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to adjust personnel practices, but costs are expected to be absorbable within existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Student Loan Ombudsman (located within the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation under the Department of Labor) with developing and distributing PSLF awareness materials, and requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to adopt implementing regulations.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government employees, DBM is responsible for implementing the bill's required hours-worked calculation standards for State workers, certifying qualifying employment, and distributing the ombudsman's PSLF materials during onboarding and annually.

The bill explicitly establishes PSLF certification and calculation standards for institutions of higher education, requiring a 3.35-hour credit multiplier per contact hour for adjunct and tenured professors and treating consecutive academic terms as continuous employment, creating operational impacts for USM human resources units.

As an independent public institution of higher education and qualifying public service employer, Morgan State University must comply with the bill's specific faculty workload calculation rules and employee notification requirements.
As an independent public college, St. Mary's College must adopt the bill's specific higher education faculty calculation rules and provide the required PSLF awareness materials to its employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the filing fee that must accompany an order to docket or a complaint to foreclose a mortgage or deed of trust on residential property from $300 to $450.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Mortgage lenders, loan servicers, foreclosing attorneys, homeowners facing foreclosure, and housing counseling and legal assistance non-profit organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues to the Housing Counseling and Foreclosure Mediation Fund administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development increase by approximately $525,600 in FY 2026 (reflecting the October 1, 2025 effective date) and by $700,800 annually thereafter. State general fund revenues increase minimally beginning in FY 2026 from accrued interest. Expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD administers the Housing Counseling and Foreclosure Mediation Fund, which receives the revenues generated from the increased residential mortgage foreclosure filing fee, resulting in an estimated special fund revenue increase of over $500,000 to $700,000 annually.
The Maryland court system receives orders to docket and complaints to foreclose, and is responsible for collecting the statutory filing fees upon docketing.

The Housing Counseling and Foreclosure Mediation Fund supports efforts by the Maryland Department of Labor to provide advice and assistance to homeowners, and the bill references loss mitigation affidavits prescribed by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation housed within the department.
Revenues from the fund assist in covering the costs of foreclosure mediation services administered and conducted by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Office of Overdose Response, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health, to create and maintain an interactive public dashboard displaying Opioid Restitution Fund spending and prescription opioid-related settlement data disaggregated by State, county, and municipality, funded through the Opioid Restitution Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Office of Overdose Response, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: The general public, Maryland counties and municipalities receiving opioid settlement funding, local health departments, and organizations utilizing Opioid Restitution Fund resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) increase by approximately $70,000 in FY 2026 for contractual dashboard development and $2,000 annually starting in FY 2027 for maintenance. Because these costs are drawn from existing ORF resources, there is no net impact on total state spending or revenues, though funds available for other discretionary opioid abatement purposes will decrease by an equivalent amount. Local governments and local health departments may be impacted to the extent that less ORF funding is available for other local grant allocations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in collaboration with the Maryland Office of Overdose Response, to develop and maintain the interactive dashboard on Opioid Restitution Fund spending. MDH is also tasked with establishing an online reporting portal, uploading settlement data, and using special funds from the Opioid Restitution Fund ($70,000 in FY 2026 and $2,000 annually thereafter) to support the dashboard.

The bill specifically mandates the Maryland Office of Overdose Response (MOOR), an executive-level entity coordinating the administration's statewide overdose prevention and response policies, to develop and maintain the interactive dashboard in collaboration with MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) Institution Partnership Extension Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to expand opportunities for technology validation, entrepreneurial development, and industry engagement at Bowie State University, Frostburg State University, and other eligible public or private nonprofit higher education institutions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) / Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Bowie State University, Frostburg State University, other Maryland public and private nonprofit higher education institutions, technology-based entrepreneurs, and regional industry partners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal effect in FY 2026. Assuming discretionary funding is provided, General Fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 (and are estimated at $1.0 million annually thereafter if expanded), with corresponding increases in MII Fund special fund revenues and expenditures. Participating public institutions incur higher education matching expenditures of $15,000 annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 based on the 10% cash match requirement. Local community colleges may see matching revenue and expenditure increases in future years if deemed eligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO houses the Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII), which is directly tasked with implementing, administering, evaluating proposals for, and distributing grants under the newly established Maryland Innovation Initiative Institution Partnership Extension Program, as well as submitting required reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

Two USM member institutions, Bowie State University and Frostburg State University, are explicitly designated as the eligible universities under the program, enabling them to submit project proposals, receive funding, and commit required matching funds.

The bill authorizes the Governor to include discretionary appropriations of $250,000 for the program in the annual budget bill for FY 2027 and FY 2028, and mandates that TEDCO submit an economic impact report to the Governor by January 1, 2026.
DBM oversees the development of the annual state budget and fiscal planning, which is impacted by the discretionary general fund appropriations authorized for the program in FY 2027 and FY 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires landlords of residential and commercial real property in Howard County subject to Columbia Association covenants to disclose in written leases any annual Columbia Association charges included in rent, explain how the charges are calculated, provide information on tenant rights and privileges, and provide copies of relevant covenants and governing documents when a lease is signed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential and commercial landlords and tenants of properties subject to Columbia Association covenants in Howard County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or Howard County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees and enforces statutory requirements and consumer protections related to residential leases and landlord-tenant transactions, and was consulted in the preparation of this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals enrolled in an accredited institution of higher education or a residential vocational training program to temporarily return to an out-of-home placement provider where they were previously placed during scheduled breaks, temporary closures, or leaves of absence, subject to mutual agreement and approval by the local department of social services and the Department of Human Services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: College and vocational students formerly in foster care or out-of-home placement, out-of-home placement providers, and child placement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Human Services can process and make determinations regarding requests using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for child welfare and out-of-home placements in Maryland. The bill establishes a process whereby local departments of social services submit recommendations to DHS, and DHS makes final determinations on whether individuals enrolled in higher education or vocational training can return to out-of-home placement providers during breaks.
