qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, to convene a stakeholder workgroup to study pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs), pharmacist reimbursement, specialty drug definitions, and ERISA regulation exemptions, and to report findings and recommendations by December 31, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Pharmacies (independent and chain), pharmacists, pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs), health insurance carriers, drug manufacturers and distributors, managed care organizations, and Medicaid enrollees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by $51,292 in FY 2026 and $21,134 in FY 2027 (funded 50% general funds and 50% federal funds) for one part-time contractual health policy analyst at MDH to staff the workgroup. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly by $25,646 in FY 2026 and $10,567 in FY 2027. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026 and FY 2027 for contractual consultant services. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Insurance Administration, jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to convene a stakeholder workgroup to study pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs) and submit interim and final reports to the General Assembly. MIA may incur special fund expenditures to contract for consulting services.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health, alongside the Maryland Insurance Administration, to convene the PBM workgroup, review Medicaid reimbursement and drug pricing issues, and report findings to the General Assembly. MDH will incur Medicaid expenditures to hire staff to support the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a specialized temporary study workgroup comprised of interested stakeholders and experts to analyze pharmacy benefits management, pharmacist reimbursement, specialty drug coverage, and related statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Juvenile Services to submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding youth service bureaus and delinquency prevention efforts, including technical assistance to local governments and program assessments, beginning by October 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: At-risk youth, local governments, and community youth service bureaus in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Juvenile Services can implement the reporting requirement using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 814 directly places a statutory mandate on the Department of Juvenile Services to submit an annual report on youth service bureaus, predelinquent programs, technical assistance to local governments, and youth offense prevention efforts.

The Governor's Office for Children administers the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund, which is currently the primary source of State grant funding awarded to local management boards supporting Youth Service Bureaus covered under the required reporting.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy allocates funding for youth programs and juvenile delinquency reduction, including grant funding directly provided to youth service bureaus reviewed under this reporting mandate.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Stadium Authority, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College to establish a technical evaluation factor of up to 10%, subject to Board of Public Works approval, for offerors utilizing an approved Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) in competitive sealed proposals for procurements valued under $80 million.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, Baltimore City Community College, and the Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Offerors and contractors with or without Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs), small businesses, and the procuring state entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State procurement expenditures (general, nonbudgeted, and higher education funds) may increase by up to 10% for each covered contract to which the participating institutions choose to apply the ESOP evaluation factor. A reliable overall dollar estimate is unavailable because the program is optional and contract amounts vary. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Stadium Authority is one of the primary covered units authorized to establish an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) procurement preference/evaluation factor and is required to report on its implementation to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.
Morgan State University is directly authorized as a covered unit to establish the ESOP evaluation factor for covered procurements and is required to submit an evaluation report by December 1, 2028.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly authorized as a covered unit to establish an ESOP procurement evaluation factor of up to 10% and must submit an implementation report by December 1, 2028.
Under the bill, the establishment of the ESOP evaluation factor by any participating unit is subject to the approval of the Board of Public Works.
The University System of Maryland is explicitly required under § 14-806 to submit the report evaluating ESOP preference usage and effectiveness to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence, algorithms, and software tools in health insurance utilization reviews by carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and private review agents. It prohibits AI tools from denying, delaying, or modifying health care services or replacing a health care provider's role, mandates that AI determinations be based on individual clinical history rather than solely on group datasets, and requires carriers to report whether AI was used in adverse coverage decisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs), private review agents (PRAs), health care providers, and health insurance enrollees/patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) increase by a minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 due to $1,500 PRA application filing fees. Special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate, potentially significant amount beginning in FY 2026 for contractual subject matter experts to conduct compliance and audit oversight of AI tools, though examination costs may be passed on to the examined entities. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for enforcing the bill's provisions. MIA will review private review agent (PRA) filings, adopt regulations, receive quarterly adverse decision reports, conduct audits and compliance examinations on artificial intelligence software tools used by insurers, and compile an annual report.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates aspects of health maintenance organizations and provides related data to the Insurance Commissioner under the Health - General Article for inclusion in the annual summary report on adverse decisions and utilization review.
The Department of Budget and Management oversees health benefits for state employees and was consulted as an information source regarding potential impacts on state-sponsored health plans.

The Governor's Office receives copies of the annual summary report compiled by the Insurance Commissioner regarding adverse decisions, grievances, and the use of artificial intelligence in utilization review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds the Comptroller of Maryland, or the Comptroller's designee, as an ex officio member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, the Comptroller of Maryland, and small business employers and employees participating in the MarylandSaves program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. Adding the Comptroller or their designee to the board does not impact State finances or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 825 directly adds the Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, as an ex officio member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board.
The bill directly alters the membership structure and composition of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, which governs and administers the MarylandSaves program.
The Secretary of Labor is an existing ex officio member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, whose board composition is altered by this bill.
The State Treasurer is an existing ex officio member of the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, whose board composition is altered by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the inactive Interdepartmental Advisory Committee on Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs and creates the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation. Chaired by the Special Secretary of the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, the Subcabinet is tasked with studying socioeconomic procurement practices in other states, developing accountability measures, working to improve state contracting access, and reporting annually to the Governor with recommendations to enhance programs like the Small Business Reserve, Minority Business Enterprise, and Veteran Small Business Enterprise programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses seeking Maryland State procurement contracts, as well as State executive agencies and procurement officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Governor's Office and participating executive agencies can implement the bill and staff the Subcabinet using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by GOSBA, repeals the Interdepartmental Advisory Committee within the office, and establishes the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation, which is chaired by the Special Secretary of GOSBA.

The Subcabinet is established under the executive branch and reports annually to the Governor. The Governor may appoint additional department or agency heads to the Subcabinet, and the Governor's Office will staff the body.

The Secretary of General Services and the Chief Procurement Officer are designated members of the Subcabinet. In addition, the Subcabinet is directed to work with the Office of State Procurement (housed within DGS) to implement process improvements.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the newly created Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Subcabinet.

The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families (or designee) is a statutory member of the Subcabinet, which is also tasked with recommending actions to improve the Veteran Small Business Enterprise Program.
The Minority Business Enterprise Ombudsman, housed within the Office of the Attorney General, is designated as a member of the Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals an advisory committee and creates a new executive subcabinet charged with studying socioeconomic procurement and reporting annually.
The State Superintendent of Schools was a designated member of the repealed Interdepartmental Advisory Committee on Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs.
The Secretary of Higher Education was a statutory member of the repealed Interdepartmental Advisory Committee on Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Human Resources of Carroll County to request a State and national criminal history records check for any prospective employee or volunteer of Carroll County by removing previous job-specific limitations on who could be checked.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Resources of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective employees and volunteers of Carroll County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) can handle requests using existing resources. Carroll County may experience a minimal annual expenditure increase starting in FY 2026 to cover background check costs ($50 per check) for additional prospective employees and volunteers. Carroll County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Carroll County Department of Human Resources to request State and national criminal history records checks for all prospective employees and volunteers from the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), which is administered by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to issue and sell up to $36.9 million in general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, improvement, and development of various public facilities, public works, school projects, and agricultural land preservation, as well as to finance loans for volunteer fire department equipment and facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, taxpayers, public school students and staff, and volunteer fire departments in Carroll County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Carroll County revenues increase by up to $36.9 million from bond proceeds. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $2.6 million annually over a 20-year period based on a 3.72% interest rate.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 835 alters the regulations governing Class B-Stadium (baseball stadium) beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Charles County. It prohibits the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages in stadium parking areas, permits patrons to carry and consume liquor anywhere on the stadium premises outside of parking areas rather than restricting liquor to enclosed dining areas or bars, and eliminates Styrofoam while permitting plastic, paper, or other nonglass serving containers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Charles County baseball stadium license holders (franchise owners and concessionaires), stadium event patrons, and concession workers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State finances and does not materially affect Charles County finances or operations. The small business effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state alcohol taxation. While this bill strictly modifies local licensing and container rules for a baseball stadium administered by the Charles County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's broader alcoholic beverages framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill specifies that the practice of direct-entry midwifery is independent and does not require oversight by another health care practitioner. It revises the scope of practice and the clinical conditions requiring consultation with or transfer of care to a health care practitioner, modifies hospital transfer and written plan requirements, repeals specific annual reporting mandates to the Direct-Entry Midwifery Advisory Committee, clarifies disciplinary actions available to the State Board of Nursing, and extends the statutory sunset date for direct-entry midwife licensure to July 1, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed direct-entry midwives, applicants for direct-entry midwifery licensure, pregnant patients and their newborns, collaborating and receiving health care practitioners, and hospitals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the bill's changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect State or local governmental finances. Small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Nursing, which licenses and regulates direct-entry midwives. The bill alters the scope of practice, disciplinary actions, reporting requirements, and extends the termination date of the Maryland Licensure of Direct-Entry Midwives Act.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory duties involving the Direct-Entry Midwifery Advisory Committee, specifically repealing direct annual reporting requirements to the committee and requiring the Board to consult with the committee on new reporting regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 839 qualifies a voter to cast a provisional ballot if the voter claimed a political party affiliation differing from their affiliation on record, provided the voter made a selection in a nonpartisan board of education contest. In such cases, local boards of canvassers are required to count only the votes cast in the nonpartisan board of education contest.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local boards of elections and the Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered Maryland voters who cast provisional ballots due to party affiliation discrepancies, candidates running in nonpartisan local board of education elections, and election administrators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not expected to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Maryland election law regarding provisional ballots and nonpartisan board of education contests. The State Board of Elections oversees local election boards and establishes the regulations and standards governing provisional ballot qualification and canvassing procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Pregnant and Parenting Student Support Act requires specified Maryland public senior higher education institutions to adopt and post on their websites a plan supporting pregnant and parenting students. The plan must comply with Title IX and include referrals to government assistance programs, adoption resources, and healthcare service providers, as well as institutional accommodations such as priority registration and flexible scheduling.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public senior higher education institutions (University System of Maryland constituent institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland, excluding UMCES, UMGC, and the University of Baltimore)
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and parenting students enrolled at Maryland public senior higher education institutions, along with the universities and their administrative and student support offices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education institutions can adopt and publish the required plans using existing resources. Expenditures may increase by an unknown, minimal to moderate amount if institutions provide additional services. Furthermore, State general and federal fund expenditures could increase, potentially significantly, if referrals result in increased enrollment in entitlement programs such as Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), with federal fund revenues increasing correspondingly. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (with specified exceptions) are directly mandated by the bill to develop, adopt, and post on their websites comprehensive support plans for pregnant and parenting students.
Morgan State University is explicitly required to adopt and publish on its website a plan providing accommodations, referrals, and resources for pregnant and parenting students.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly required to adopt and publish on its website a plan providing accommodations, referrals, and resources for pregnant and parenting students.

The bill mandates that institutional plans refer students to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), and WIC, which may notably increase enrollment and expenditures for these MDH-administered programs.
The bill specifically requires institutions to include referrals to the Child Care Scholarship Program, which is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education.
The bill requires institutional plans to include referrals and resources regarding adoption services and public assistance programs, which fall under the purview of DHS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the Charles County Gaming Permit Review Board and transfers its powers, duties, and responsibilities regarding gaming permits and regulations in Charles County to the Charles County Attorney.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Attorney
qa_results.stakeholders: Fundraising organizations conducting gaming events in Charles County, the Charles County government, and applicants for county gaming permits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. It also has no local fiscal impact on Charles County, as the Charles County Attorney has already assumed the duties and responsibilities of the Gaming Permit Review Board.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Charles County Gaming Permit Review Board, which under existing law specifically required a member of the Department of State Police to serve on the board, thereby removing that statutory service requirement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salaries for the Sheriff, County Commissioners, President of the County Commissioners, County Roads Board members, and President of the County Roads Board in Somerset County, taking effect at the beginning of the next term of office.
qa_results.responsible_party: Somerset County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Somerset County Sheriff, County Commissioners, County Roads Board members, and Somerset County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are unaffected. Somerset County local expenditures increase by at least $23,300 in FY 2027 and by a minimum of $40,000 annually thereafter when the new terms of office begin in December 2026 (fringe benefits not included). Local revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 848 updates requirements regarding adverse decision and grievance notices, reporting, and examinations for health insurance carriers and private review agents. It mandates specific disclosures and unique identifiers on denial notices, requires private review agents to post utilization review criteria on member and provider webpages and maintain dedicated contact channels, requires carriers to report appeals and grievances data aggregated by zip code and explain significant increases in adverse decisions, and authorizes the Insurance Commissioner to examine carriers using this data.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance policyholders/members, health care providers, health insurance carriers, and private review agents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and any administrative impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the bill's requirements, which include receiving and analyzing enhanced quarterly adverse decision reports by zip code, regulating private review agents, and authorizing the Insurance Commissioner to initiate market conduct examinations based on reported data.

The bill mandates that health carrier denial and grievance notices prominently provide contact information and statements regarding the assistance available through the Health Advocacy Unit, a division housed within the Office of the Attorney General that mediates consumer health coverage disputes.
The bill requires the Insurance Commissioner to provide copies of the annual summary report on health insurance appeals, grievances, and adverse decisions to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on the Creation of a Data Dashboard for Public Work Contracts and Apprentices to study and make recommendations regarding the most efficient and cost-effective method to develop a publicly available dashboard that disaggregates data regarding State public work contracts, wages, classifications, and participating apprentices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: State public works contractors, subcontractors, construction workers, registered apprentices, labor unions, and contractor associations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can staff the workgroup and absorb minimal member travel expense reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues, local finances, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry as members of the newly established Workgroup, and requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to provide administrative and operational staff for the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on the Creation of a Data Dashboard for Public Work Contracts and Apprentices as a temporary advisory body to study and make recommendations on dashboard implementation and reporting.

The Governor is responsible for appointing six members representing various industry associations and unions to the Workgroup, and the Workgroup must submit its final findings and recommendations to the Governor by January 7, 2027.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments for the six industry and labor positions established on the Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Second Look Act expands the provisions of the Juvenile Restoration Act to permit individuals who committed offenses between the ages of 18 and 24 to file a motion to reduce their sentence duration, provided they have served at least 20 years of confinement, were not sentenced to life without parole, are not registered sex offenders, and were not convicted of murdering an on-duty first responder. It also establishes procedural rules, factors courts must consider before granting a reduction, and specific victim protections.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts), Office of the Public Defender, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals who committed crimes between ages 18 and 24 and have served at least 20 years, crime victims and their families, public defenders, and State's Attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase for the Office of the Public Defender by at least $538,100 in FY 2026 (growing to $730,300 by FY 2030) to hire six staff members, with additional indeterminate costs for panel attorneys. Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services expenditures will decrease by an indeterminate amount as individuals are released (saving approximately $312 per month per inmate in variable costs). Local expenditures for State's Attorneys' offices may increase minimally to respond to sentence reduction motions. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for sentence reduction motions under the Maryland Second Look Act, directly increasing caseloads for the Office of the Public Defender and requiring significant additional staff and funding to evaluate case files and represent eligible incarcerated individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts individuals serving sentences within Division of Correction facilities; court decisions granting sentence reductions or releases will directly affect inmate population management, institutional record reporting for hearings, and departmental correctional expenditures.
Circuit courts are tasked with receiving petitions, holding hearings, receiving victim impact statements, issuing written determinations on statutory factors, and ordering release conditions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network by decreasing the number of appointed members across several categories, extends the deadline for its final report to December 1, 2026, and extends the termination date of the workgroup to June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland, Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland citizen scientists, researchers, higher education institutions, private and nonprofit sector technology experts, and the Workgroup members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The University of Maryland, Baltimore County can staff the workgroup for two additional years using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates a representative from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC)—a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland—as a member and specifically requires UMBC to provide administrative and operational staff support for the workgroup through its extension.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the Executive Director's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership composition, reporting requirements, and operating timeline of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members representing higher education and community-based science and technology applications, and the workgroup must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating gubernatorial appointments to state task forces, advisory councils, and workgroups, which are altered under this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals permitted to hunt deer by the Department of Natural Resources who wound a deer during legal hunting hours to pursue and kill the deer after legal hunting hours using a light, spotlight, headlight, or other artificial lighting device, provided they use the authorized means for the applicable hunting season or permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed deer hunters in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article governing deer hunting rules, authorizes hunters licensed by DNR to pursue and kill wounded deer after legal hunting hours using artificial light, and expressly requires DNR to adopt implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in collaboration with the Maryland State Department of Education and other organizations, to promote access to health insurance for child care professionals through targeted outreach, enrollment assistance for health coverage and Medicaid, and conducting a survey on health care access among child care providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Child care professionals, child care employers, and child care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by $250,000 in FY 2026 to transfer funds from the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE). MHBE special fund revenues and expenditures correspondingly increase by $250,000 in FY 2026 for the outreach campaign and survey. Ongoing MHBE expenses and MSDE partnership responsibilities will be absorbed with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) to lead the implementation of the act by conducting outreach to child care professionals, assisting them in obtaining coverage through the exchange or Medicaid, and conducting a survey on health care access across the child care community.

The bill explicitly requires MHBE to partner with the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), utilize prekindergarten provider hubs established by MSDE, and consult with MSDE in developing the required child care health care access survey.

The fiscal note identifies a direct fiscal impact on the Department of Commerce, requiring a $250,000 transfer in special funds from Commerce's Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to MHBE in FY 2026 to fund the outreach and survey activities.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees the state's Medicaid program, which is specifically targeted by the bill's outreach and enrollment assistance initiatives for child care professionals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits common carriers engaged in transporting passengers by land from damaging state or locally owned bridges or highways resulting in their closure, defining such damage as a public nuisance. Authorizes the State or local governments to bring civil actions against common carriers for injunctive relief, declaratory relief, compensatory damages for repair or replacement costs, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per day until the infrastructure is restored or replaced.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Transportation Authority, and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Land-based passenger common carriers (including bus companies, rail companies, taxicab services, and transportation network companies), local governments, and the traveling public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is indeterminate because incident frequency cannot be predicted. When violations occur, state general fund revenues and local revenues may increase from civil penalties of $1,000 per day. Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and local government finances may recoup costs through compensatory damages for infrastructure repair or replacement, partially offset by increased legal and litigation expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT oversees the state's highways and bridges, which constitute the public infrastructure protected under this bill. MDOT and the Transportation Trust Fund are directly affected as the department would initiate civil actions to recover costs, receive compensatory damages for repairs, and incur potential litigation expenses.

As the MDOT modal administration responsible for designing, maintaining, and repairing state non-toll highways and bridges, SHA would directly suffer infrastructure damages, conduct necessary repairs or closures, and provide documentation to recover repair and replacement costs from responsible common carriers.

MDTA finances, operates, and maintains state toll bridges and highways. The fiscal note explicitly notes that MDTA may engage in litigation to pursue compensatory damages and civil penalties, incurring nonbudgeted expenditures and potentially recouping infrastructure repair costs.

The OAG provides legal representation to the State and MDOT. It would be responsible for initiating and litigating public nuisance civil actions against common carriers for injunctive relief, compensatory damages, and civil penalties.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action and statutory remedy under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, which would be filed and adjudicated within the Maryland court system managed by the AOC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires transportation network companies (TNCs) to provide drivers with a weekly fare and earnings summary detailing total fares and additional fees collected, the driver's earnings, and percentage breakdowns. It also requires TNCs to submit an annual report by February 1 to the Public Service Commission containing aggregated data on average fares, total driver time, and driver earnings in Maryland, while protecting nonpublic reported data as confidential trade secrets.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Transportation network companies (such as Uber and Lyft) and approximately 175,000 licensed transportation network drivers/operators in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission regulates transportation network companies (TNCs) in Maryland and is the primary state agency tasked under the bill with receiving annual aggregated reporting regarding operator fares, hours driven, and earnings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the transfer of funds from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund by budget amendment if the fund's balance is depleted or if estimated disaster relief costs exceed the fund's balance, and reduces the Legislative Policy Committee's review and comment period for transfers from 15 days to 10 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) and Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government agencies responding to emergencies, and Maryland residents and communities impacted by natural disasters or catastrophic events
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no net effect on overall State finances. If transfers occur, special fund expenditures from the Catastrophic Event Account and special fund revenues to the State Disaster Recovery Fund increase correspondingly. Interest revenues to the Revenue Stabilization Account (Rainy Day Fund) may decrease minimally if substantial funds are transferred. Local government finances are not significantly impacted, though local jurisdictions may receive disaster relief funding more quickly due to the shortened 10-day review period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM administers the State Disaster Recovery Fund, which under the bill is authorized to receive fund transfers from the Catastrophic Event Account when funds are depleted or disaster relief costs exceed the fund's balance.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account within the State Reserve Fund and oversees the execution of budget amendments and state fund transfers governed by this legislation.

The bill directly amends the statutory procedure and timeframe under which the Governor may transfer funds by budget amendment from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund following a reduced 10-day review period.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class C (theater) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County, allowing qualifying theaters with seating to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption from one hour before to one hour after regular performances, fundraiser performances, or events hosted by outside renters, for an annual fee of $150.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Frederick County theaters, theater patrons, outside groups renting theater facilities, and the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Frederick County revenues increase beginning in FY 2026 by $150 annually for each Class C (theater) license issued. Frederick County can handle any associated enforcement activities using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a local Class C alcoholic beverages license in Frederick County administered by the local Board of License Commissioners. While the state fiscal effect is none, the Comptroller oversees state alcohol taxation and industry regulation generally.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Preserve Telehealth Access Act of 2025 permanently includes certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of telehealth and makes permanent the requirement that Medicaid and commercial health insurers reimburse telehealth services on the same basis and at the same rate as in-person services. It also alters the circumstances under which health care practitioners may prescribe Schedule II opiates for the treatment of pain via telehealth and requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit a telehealth report every four years beginning December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients receiving telehealth services (including Medicaid enrollees and commercially insured individuals), health care providers and practitioners, and commercial health insurers and managed care organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Care Commission increase by an estimated $100,000 in FY 2027, and every four years thereafter, to complete required telehealth reporting. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues decrease minimally in FY 2026. Medicaid expenditures and federal matching funds continue beyond FY 2025 with an indeterminate net effect. Local government health expenditures may increase to continue reimbursing certain telehealth services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission submit a quadriennial report to the Governor and General Assembly starting in 2026 on telehealth advances, modalities, and cost changes, resulting in a recurring $100,000 fiscal impact.

The bill permanently mandates telehealth coverage and payment parity (including audio-only telephone conversations) under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill permanently requires commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration to provide telehealth coverage and reimbursement parity.
The bill amends provisions in the Health Occupations Article establishing clinical requirements and permissions for prescribing Schedule II controlled dangerous substances (CDS) via telehealth.

The bill specifically clarifies that telehealth payment parity requirements do not supersede the authority of the Health Services Cost Review Commission to set hospital rates and hospital facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was evaluated in the fiscal analysis regarding commercial insurance telehealth coverage requirements.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated four-year telehealth status report from the Maryland Health Care Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'community benefit' for nonprofit hospital reporting to include community health worker (CHW) workforce programs established in partnership with community-based organizations. It allows these partnerships to be established through a memorandum of understanding, sets terms for program administration and data sharing, authorizes partnerships to offer health insurance coverage to CHWs, and allows hospitals to provide financial support to community-based organizations for administrative capacity.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, community-based organizations, community health workers, and hospital patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the hospital community benefit statute (§ 19-303 of the Health - General Article) administered by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). It expands the definition of 'community benefit' to include community health worker workforce programs that nonprofit hospitals report in their annual community benefits filings to HSCRC.

The bill references statutory definitions of community health workers governed under the Health - General Article and impacts public health workforce partnerships. In addition, HSCRC is an independent commission established within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that following the closing of a contract of sale between a property owner and a third party, liability for noncompliance with statutory requirements regarding a tenant's right of first refusal is restricted solely to the owner and does not attach to the residential rental property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential rental property owners, residential tenants, and third-party property buyers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions governing the tenant's right of first refusal process under Real Property Section 8-119. The Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs (OTLA), which receives required notices and oversees administrative aspects of this statute, is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill clarifies legal liability and title encumbrances arising from noncompliance with the tenant's right of first refusal law, which may be referenced in judicial litigation regarding residential real property transactions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date and reporting deadlines of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by three years. The commission's interim report deadline is extended to June 1, 2028, the final report deadline to January 1, 2029, and the sunset date to June 30, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, individuals involved in the criminal and juvenile justice systems, and commission members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,500 in FY 2026, $65,600 in FY 2027, $68,400 in FY 2028, and $42,100 in FY 2029 for the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to maintain one contractual program coordinator to support the commission through its extended duration. There is no effect on revenues, and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary staffing agency for the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission and incurs direct general fund expenditures from FY 2026 through FY 2029 to maintain contractual staff to support the commission's extended operational timeline.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date (sunset) and interim and final reporting deadlines of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by three years.
The bill mandates that the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission submit both its extended interim report and final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools to study, analyze data on, and recommend culturally responsive and nonpunitive practices to identify, prevent, and reduce student chronic absenteeism. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to update attendance regulations and distribute guidance and an absenteeism toolkit to local school systems.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Maryland State Department of Education can provide staff support for the task force and update regulations using existing budgeted resources. Local school finances are not expected to be materially affected, although local school operations may be impacted if new regulations impose additional requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary implementing agency required to staff the Task Force, update student attendance regulations based on the Task Force's findings, and distribute chronic absenteeism toolkits and guidance to local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory, temporary body known as the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools to study best practices, analyze attendance data, and make recommendations.
The Task Force includes a designated representative of the Governor's Office among its membership and must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill phases in an increase in the amount of child support collected each month that passes directly to families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance under the Family Investment Program, rather than being retained by the State. Starting in fiscal 2028, the passthrough increases progressively until fiscal 2031, when 100% of collected child support passes through to families and is disregarded when computing benefit amounts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Families and children receiving assistance under the Family Investment Program / Temporary Cash Assistance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $138,067 in FY 2027 for one-time technology updates (matched by $268,013 in federal funds), and then increase by $2.4 million in FY 2028, $6.2 million in FY 2029, $10.1 million in FY 2030, and $13.9 million annually beginning in FY 2031 to offset the loss of retained child support revenue and reimburse the federal government's share. Special fund revenues and expenditures decrease correspondingly. Local governments are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 881 directly amends the Human Services Article governing the Family Investment Program (FIP) and child support pass-through calculations. The Department of Human Services (DHS)—specifically its Family Investment Administration and Child Support Administration—is the primary agency responsible for administering these programs, updating eligibility and child support IT systems, and managing the associated fiscal adjustments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows certain former members of the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers' Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who were members on or before June 30, 2011, separated from service, and later return to service under specified conditions to be subject to the pre-2011 pension benefit structure rather than the post-2011 reformed structure.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Returning members of the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers' Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who were enrolled on or before June 30, 2011, and had a qualified break in service.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is likely no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates, as the State Retirement Agency identified only 16 members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and no members of the other systems who would benefit. The bill has no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including SPRS, CORS, and LEOPS, and is responsible for implementing the altered benefit tiers and record-keeping for returning members.
The bill directly impacts the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), affecting pension rules and benefit eligibility for re-employed State Police personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters retirement system rules for the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS), affecting correctional staff employed by the department who separate and subsequently return to service.

As the principal personnel and state employee benefits administration agency for Maryland, DBM oversees state workforce policies and personnel regulations that interact with re-employment and pension provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications allowing out-of-state certified public accountants (CPAs) to practice in Maryland without obtaining a Maryland license. It repeals requirements for the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy (NASBA) to verify substantial equivalence to the Uniform Accountancy Act, establishing instead that an individual qualifies for practice privileges if they hold a valid CPA license from another state and were required to pass the Uniform CPA Examination to obtain that license.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified public accountants licensed in other states who wish to practice in Maryland, accounting firms, and their Maryland clients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill with existing resources. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are not materially affected. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses and supports the State Board of Public Accountancy, which directly regulates the practice and licensing privileges of certified public accountants in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications for an initial teacher certificate by allowing candidates to qualify by passing a portfolio-based assessment from a nationally accredited teacher preparation program as an alternative to existing portfolio assessment or induction program requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Teacher candidates graduating from approved or alternative teacher preparation programs, accredited teacher preparation institutions, and local school systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal effect on State finances or local school systems, though it may expand the pool of licensed teachers available for local school systems to hire.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) certifies and licenses educators in Maryland. This bill directly amends the qualifications and assessment requirements for individuals seeking an initial teacher certificate.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies administrative penalties for commercial oyster harvesters, replacing the mandatory revocation of an oyster authorization for a first violation with a suspension of up to 5 years, while retaining revocation for second or subsequent violations. It adjusts the violation criteria for using prohibited gear by specifying that the gear must be used while more than 200 feet within a prohibited area, repeals the 90-day deadline for holding an administrative penalty hearing, and allows individuals whose authorizations were revoked prior to July 1, 2025, to have their entitlement to work in the fishery reinstated and reapply for an authorization 5 years after revocation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial oyster harvesters, individuals whose oyster authorizations have been suspended or revoked, and individuals on the commercial license waiting list.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State expenditures increase by an estimated $11,500 annually ($5,300 in general funds and $6,200 in special funds) for the Department of Natural Resources to cover the cost of holding additional administrative hearings with the Office of Administrative Hearings. Special fund revenues may decrease minimally as suspended authorizations are held rather than revoked and reissued to paying applicants on the waiting list. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary regulatory agency responsible for issuing tidal fish license oyster authorizations, conducting administrative penalty proceedings, suspending or revoking authorizations, and processing reinstatements.

The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts contested administrative penalty hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act on behalf of the Department of Natural Resources, with caseload and hearing volumes expected to increase under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to issue incidental taking permits for the Indiana bat, northern long-eared bat, tricolored bat, or eastern small-footed bat, provided an applicant submits an approved conservation plan and the Secretary makes specific determinations regarding species survival and mitigation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Land developers, businesses, and contractors operating in habitats of endangered bats, as well as wildlife conservation groups and threatened/endangered bat populations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and has no local government fiscal effect. It may provide meaningful relief to small businesses by offering an incidental taking permit process rather than requiring full adherence to activity and time-of-year restrictions in areas supporting endangered bats.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 894 directly authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to review conservation plans, make required statutory findings, issue incidental taking permits for specified bat species, and adopt implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Employment and Insurance Equality for Service Members Act establishes uniform statutory definitions across Maryland law to align with federal standards, broadening protections, economic development programs, professional licensing accommodations, insurance provisions, and employment benefits from applying solely to the armed forces to include all uniformed services (such as the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Corps), reserve components, veterans, and military spouses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Department of Commerce, and Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, Public Health Service, and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps), reserve components, veterans, military spouses and families, regulated employers, and insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2026 only due to form filings submitted to the Maryland Insurance Administration. Otherwise, State finances and operations are not materially affected since the expansions apply to a limited number of individuals. Local government finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially amends the Labor and Employment, Business Regulation, and Financial Institutions Articles, directly impacting the department's administration of unemployment insurance benefits, the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) system, apprenticeship credits, workforce development, occupational licensing units, and mortgage loan originator licensing.

The bill amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article—which establishes the statutory framework and definitions governing the department—and requires the Department of Commerce to consult with DVMF in administering the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program.

The bill amends multiple provisions of the Insurance Article concerning insurance producer licensing, reinstatement fee waivers for deployed personnel, underwriting rules, and policy exclusions, which the administration regulates and for which it will process policy and form filings.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article to update the scope, definitions, and naming of the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program administered by Commerce.

The bill amends Section 20-502 of the Insurance Article to broaden the eligibility exceptions for motor vehicle liability insurance coverage provided by MAIF to all active-duty uniformed services members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office monitors and implements the State's Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) Program across state agencies, which is affected by the bill's update to the definition of 'veteran' under Section 14-601 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

The bill amends Commercial Law Section 14-1212.2 regarding protected consumer status under credit reporting laws for active service members, which is subject to enforcement by the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the property tax exemption on dwelling houses owned by qualified blind individuals or their surviving spouses from $15,000 to $40,000 of assessed value.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Legally blind homeowners and their unremarried surviving spouses, as well as county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease by approximately $40,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 due to the increased exemption, resulting in an average state tax savings of $28 per homeowner. Local property tax revenues decrease by an estimated $450,000 annually beginning in FY 2026, saving homeowners an average of $320 each. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding property valuations and disputes over property tax exemptions and credits, which includes the statutory real property tax exemption for blind individuals altered by this bill.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates state programs, advocacy, and policies supporting Maryland residents with disabilities, including blind homeowners impacted by this property tax relief measure.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body adjudicating appeals from the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board concerning real property tax assessments and exemptions.

State property tax collections fund the Annuity Bond Fund, which the Treasurer oversees to pay debt service on State general obligation bonds; the bill reduces Annuity Bond Fund revenues by approximately $40,000 annually.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of speed monitoring systems authorized on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City from two to four, while limiting operation to no more than one camera in each direction at a time, and permanently eliminates the program's June 30, 2026 sunset date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City and the Baltimore City local government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues may increase starting as early as FY 2026 from contested citations decided in District Court, which will handle any added caseload with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 from installing additional cameras (with procurement and installation expenditures potentially beginning in FY 2025). Making the program permanent prevents the authorization from expiring at the end of FY 2026, preserving significant annual city fine revenues (which generated $5.6 million in FY 2024 from the two existing I-83 cameras) and associated operating expenditures beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands and makes permanent speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City. Individuals receiving citations may contest them in the District Court of Maryland, which is administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, resulting in a potential increase in contested caseloads and general fund revenues.

The bill amends the Maryland Transportation Article governing speed monitoring systems on interstate highways and affects highway speed enforcement and signage compliance within the state's broader transportation network.
Under the governing statute for speed monitoring systems, speed camera signage and speed display devices must conform to traffic control device standards adopted by the State Highway Administration.

Under state speed monitoring system laws, any net revenues generated by jurisdictions in excess of statutory caps must be remitted to the Comptroller of Maryland, which also tracks speed camera revenues and citation data.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill allows an individual to consent to the issuance of a permanent protective order against themselves, expanding the statutory circumstances under which a court must issue a permanent protective order.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of abuse seeking protective relief and respondents in protective order proceedings who choose to consent to a permanent protective order.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $30,300 in FY 2026 only for one-time computer programming costs. The bill is not anticipated to materially impact local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory criteria under which courts may issue permanent protective orders by allowing orders to be issued by consent. The Administrative Office of the Courts will incur a direct fiscal impact of $30,300 in FY 2026 for one-time judicial programming and system modifications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund within the Maryland Department of Health to provide operating grants to eligible organizations to improve access to abortion care clinical services for uninsured, underinsured, or vulnerable individuals. The program is financed by transferring excess balances and accrued interest from health insurance carriers' ACA-mandated segregated abortion coverage accounts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals seeking abortion care clinical services who are uninsured, underinsured, or facing privacy risks; health care providers and clinics offering abortion services; and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $19.3 million in FY 2026 and $2.5 million annually thereafter from the transfer of excess funds in carriers' segregated accounts. Special fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million in FY 2026 via a required budget amendment and by $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2027 from a mandated appropriation to fund grants (at least 90%) and administrative personnel costs (1.0 FTE). General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 from fund interest earnings. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 930 establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and the associated special fund within the Maryland Department of Health. The Secretary of Health is responsible for administering the fund, developing grant standards, and awarding operating grants to eligible organizations.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner are tasked with collecting annual accountings of carriers' segregated accounts under the ACA, establishing reporting forms, and ordering the transfer of tens of millions of dollars in excess balances to the new special fund.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund separately and invest the money of the fund in accordance with state investment procedures.
The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly established Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund.

The bill requires the Governor to allocate $2,000,000 to the program by budget amendment on or before October 1, 2025, and mandates the inclusion of specific annual appropriations in the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2027.

As the state's budget agency, DBM must facilitate the Governor's mandated budget amendment in fiscal year 2026 and incorporate the ongoing mandated appropriations for the fund into the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2027.
Under the Insurance Article provisions, carriers aggrieved by an order of the Insurance Commissioner have hearing and appeal rights that may be adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Governor, within six months of taking the oath of office, to place their financial interests into a certified blind trust approved by the State Ethics Commission or divest interests that pose potential conflicts of interest. For exempted interests not included in a blind trust, the Governor must enter into a nonparticipation agreement prohibiting participation in matters involving those interests. In addition, the bill requires business entities in which the Governor or specified family and household members hold a qualifying interest to report those interests when seeking State grants, awards, or contracts.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: The Governor of Maryland, the Governor-elect, specified relatives and household members of the Governor ('restricted individuals'), and business entities seeking State grants, awards, or contracts in which the Governor or restricted individuals hold qualifying ownership interests.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $95,000 in FY 2026 only for contractual IT services, consisting of $75,000 for the State Ethics Commission to update its electronic training systems and website, and $20,000 for the Department of General Services to add a check-off disclosure box to eMaryland Marketplace. Potential fines assessed on violators are distributed to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund but are not expected to materially affect special fund revenues. Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes ethics requirements and restrictions on the Governor and Governor-elect, requiring them to establish a certified blind trust or divest interests, execute nonparticipation agreements for exempted assets, submit annual compliance certifications, and face potential civil fines for noncompliance.

The State Ethics Commission is the primary implementing and regulatory agency responsible for adopting regulations, approving blind trusts, granting exemptions, executing nonparticipation agreements, receiving disclosures from business entities, publishing records on its website, and assessing fines for noncompliance.

DGS is required to modify the eMaryland Marketplace procurement platform by October 1, 2025, to include a check-off box on procurement notices for bidders or offerors to disclose ownership interests held by the Governor or restricted family members, requiring $20,000 in IT expenditures.

The bill prohibits the Governor from participating in matters before the Board of Public Works involving interests not placed in a blind trust, and mandates that copies of any nonparticipation agreements be formally provided to the Executive Secretary and General Counsel of the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data submitted by nursing homes participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program—specifically regarding revenues allocated to contracted nursing care and wages for direct care nonadministrative staff—and to report its findings annually to the Governor and relevant legislative committees through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid-participating nursing homes, nursing home direct care and nonadministrative staff, and nursing home residents and caregivers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Health can review the required cost reports and data and complete the annual reports using existing budgeted resources. Revenues are unaffected. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data submitted by nursing homes participating in Medicaid regarding revenue allocations to contracted nursing care and direct care staff wages, and to submit an annual report of its findings from 2025 through 2029.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report detailing the Department of Health's review and findings on nursing home cost reports through 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to provide notice of cancellation or nonrenewal of a small employer health benefit plan by electronic means in addition to written notice, and requires the notice to include information regarding additional coverage options such as COBRA and plans available through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, small employers, and enrolled employees of small businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal or operational impact. It has a potential meaningful effect on small businesses and their employees by ensuring employees receive comprehensive written and electronic notice of cancellation or nonrenewal along with alternative coverage options.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers and enforces state insurance laws, including carrier compliance with notice requirements for cancellation or nonrenewal of small group health benefit plans.

The bill mandates that carrier notices sent to employees upon cancellation or nonrenewal of coverage include information regarding health coverage options available through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the governing body of a continuing care provider that has only one subscriber member to authorize the appointment of an alternate subscriber member. The alternate subscriber is authorized to attend all meetings and may vote only when the regular subscriber is unable to fulfill their duties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Continuing care retirement community providers, governing bodies of continuing care facilities, and facility subscribers/residents.
