qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Aging can implement the bill's requirements, including modifying existing documents and amending regulations, using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging regulates continuing care retirement communities and providers under Title 10 of the Human Services Article. As noted in the fiscal note, the department is responsible for modifying existing documents and amending regulations to implement the bill's governance requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Commission for Women to establish and staff the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control to study access and coverage options for over-the-counter birth control and submit interim and final recommendation reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission for Women
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers seeking over-the-counter birth control, pharmacies and retailers, health care providers, and health insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not impacted; the Maryland Commission for Women can staff the collaborative with existing budgeted resources. Revenues and local government operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Commission for Women, which is housed within the Department of Human Services, to establish, lead, and provide staff support for the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control. The Secretary of Human Services is also tasked with appointing numerous collaborative members.

The bill requires the Commissioner of the Maryland Insurance Administration to designate a representative to the Collaborative, which directly examines and recommends regulatory and point-of-sale coverage requirements for state-regulated health insurance plans.

The Secretary of Health is required to designate two representatives to the Collaborative (one from the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and one from public health) to assist in evaluating OTC birth control coverage and public health initiatives.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is required to designate a representative to serve on the Collaborative to address coverage access across individual and small business exchange plans.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must designate a representative with expertise in the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program to serve on the Collaborative.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a multi-stakeholder body, the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control, which functions as a temporary advisory board to study and report on OTC contraception coverage before abrogating in 2028.

The Collaborative includes a representative from the Consumer Health Information Hub at the University of Maryland School of Public Health and may include representation from a constituent institution providing student health insurance.
The Collaborative is statutorily mandated to submit an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report by December 1, 2027, detailing its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a felony offense prohibiting a person from committing a crime of malicious or fraudulent burning that causes the death of or serious physical injury to a firefighter, punishable by up to 10 years of imprisonment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Firefighters and individuals charged with or convicted of malicious or fraudulent burning crimes resulting in firefighter injury or death.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally due to increased incarceration costs from the 10-year felony penalty. Workload impacts on the Judiciary and the Office of the Public Defender are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense punishable by up to 10 years of imprisonment, which can run consecutively to underlying offenses, directly impacting DPSCS correctional facility populations and incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys will be responsible for providing legal defense to indigent individuals facing charges under this new felony provision.
The Judiciary and state courts are responsible for presiding over the filing, trials, and sentencing of individuals charged under the newly established criminal offense.

As the primary state law enforcement agency (which includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal), MSP investigates state criminal violations, including arson and malicious burning incidents resulting in serious injury or death to firefighters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the date of Maryland's statewide primary election in gubernatorial election years from the last Tuesday in June to the fourth Tuesday in June.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, political candidates, and state and local election officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering and supervising statewide elections, and it will be directly responsible for scheduling and conducting the gubernatorial primary election on the newly designated fourth Tuesday in June.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters provisions related to the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP), which diverts vulnerable homeowners from the private tax lien sale process. It requires local tax collectors with websites to display a program description and application link, mandates that the State Tax Sale Ombudsman actively screen and maximize enrollment, prohibits the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from charging interest on unpaid taxes owed by enrolled homeowners, and expands reporting requirements. It also creates a recurring funding mechanism for the Homeowner Protection Fund consisting of an annual state appropriation of $250,000 from interest on overdue state property taxes and $500,000 collectively from county governments derived from interest on overdue county property taxes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (specifically the State Tax Sale Ombudsman)
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners delinquent on property taxes or facing tax sales, local tax collectors, county governments, and tax lien purchasers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Homeowner Protection Fund increase by $750,000 annually ($250,000 from State property tax interest and $500,000 from county payments). State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually to replace the State property tax interest diverted from the Annuity Bond Fund for debt service. Local government expenditures increase collectively by $500,000 annually, apportioned among counties based on their share of real property accounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $250,000 from the interest on overdue State property taxes to the Homeowner Protection Fund in the annual budget bill.
DBM prepares the executive budget and oversees state fiscal planning, and this bill establishes a mandated annual state budget appropriation of $250,000 for the Homeowner Protection Fund.
Under Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article, the State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Homeowner Protection Fund separately and invest the money of the Fund.
Under Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article, the Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Homeowner Protection Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation to examine issues and provide annual recommendations regarding the regulation of artificial intelligence, consumer and privacy protections, developer obligations, and the impact of AI on employment and government benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers, private sector AI developers and deployers, labor and workforce organizations, and industries including technology, e-commerce, biotechnology, real estate, healthcare, and education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally in FY 2026 for costs associated with the workgroup. From FY 2027 through FY 2029, general fund expenditures may increase by up to $100,000 annually if the Governor exercises the discretionary authority to include an appropriation to support the workgroup in the state budget. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security provide staff support for the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, and the fiscal analysis assumes funding up to $100,000 annually will be provided through the USM budget.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, a temporary multi-stakeholder body tasked with studying AI issues, monitoring implementation, and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.

The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically charged with evaluating and recommending enforcement authority for the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the CEO's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the workgroup.
The Governor is tasked with appointing 19 members from diverse sectors to the workgroup and is authorized to include an annual appropriation of $100,000 in the State budget to support the workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Department of Human Services (DHS) to ensure pediatric hospital overstay patients are transferred to the least restrictive clinically indicated setting and to establish a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator within each department. It allows hospitals to concurrently explore in-state and out-of-state placements, establishes the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays, clarifies the scope of the State's Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry, and authorizes funding to staff five additional beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents (JLG RICA).
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Pediatric patients under age 22 experiencing hospital overstays in inpatient or emergency departments, children in out-of-home or unlicensed placements, hospitals, and behavioral health and residential treatment providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026 to fund staffing for five additional beds at the JLG RICA. The FY 2026 budget as passed includes $6.0 million in general funds for pediatric overstays, sufficient to cover initial costs. MDH, DHS, and the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect can implement the coordinator and workgroup responsibilities using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency responsible for ensuring pediatric hospital overstay patients are placed in the least restrictive setting, establishing a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, maintaining the Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry and Referral System, staffing five additional beds at John L. Gildner RICA ($3.0 million annual fiscal impact), and serving on the Workgroup.

DHS is a primary implementing agency tasked with establishing a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, ensuring children committed to its custody who experience pediatric hospital overstays are placed in the least restrictive setting, and serving on the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays to evaluate bed needs and develop plans to end unlicensed placements and overstays, and tasks the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect (SCCAN) with staffing the workgroup.

The Governor is authorized to appropriate funding to staff additional beds at RICA, appoints 11 members to the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays, and receives the Workgroup's final report.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services or their designee is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Public Defender or their designee is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel allocations, which is impacted by the bill's estimated $3.0 million annual general fund expenditure and filling of positions to staff five beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the 11 specialized stakeholder members to the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove to study the impacts of the urban renewal program carried out from 1960 through 1985 in the Emory Grove community and to recommend potential remedies for displaced residents and former landowners.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Office of Human Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Displaced residents and former landowners of the Emory Grove community, Emory Grove United Methodist Church, and Montgomery County residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Montgomery County can implement the bill and staff the task force using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 964 establishes the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove, a temporary statutory body created by the General Assembly to study the historic displacement of residents due to urban renewal and recommend potential remedies.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement containing laws enacted by the General Assembly, establishing it as recognized evidence of the law in Maryland courts and by public officials.
qa_results.responsible_party: Somerset County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Somerset County government officials, Maryland state and local courts, legal professionals, and residents of Somerset County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Somerset County local expenditures for publication costs are expected to be minimal in FY 2026 and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that the 2025 Edition of the Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws shall be recognized and admitted as evidence of the law in all Maryland state courts, which are operationally supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "storage warehouse" under Maryland's business licensing laws to exclude self-service storage facilities, thereby exempting them from the requirement to obtain a storage warehouse license and pay associated licensing fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of self-service storage facilities, the Judiciary, and the Comptroller of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2026 due to self-service storage facilities no longer paying annual warehouse licensing fees ($30 to $150 based on population). State expenditures are not materially affected. Local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Storage warehouse licenses are issued by the clerks of the circuit courts, which receive operational and administrative support from the Administrative Office of the Courts. The bill exempts self-service storage facilities from the requirement to obtain a license from the clerks.

Storage warehouse licensing fees collected by the court clerks are remitted to the Comptroller for deposit into the State's general fund. The exemption will result in a minimal reduction in general fund revenues remitted to the Comptroller.
The Department of Labor regulates businesses and professional licensing under the Business Regulation Article and was consulted as an informational source regarding the licensing scope change.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes county governments to enter into payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements with broadband service providers for provider-owned real and personal property in the county, exempting all or specified portions of that property from county property tax in exchange for negotiated annual payments.
qa_results.responsible_party: County governing bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Broadband service providers and county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent counties enter into PILOT agreements and exempt provider property; however, any tax revenue reduction will be mitigated by the negotiated payments in lieu of taxes. Specific revenue impacts are indeterminate and depend on individual agreements. Local expenditures are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from requiring step therapy or fail-first protocols for FDA-approved insulin or insulin analogs prescribed to treat Type 1, Type 2, or gestational diabetes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with Type 1, Type 2, or gestational diabetes, health insurance carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and healthcare prescribers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 resulting from $125 rate and form filing fees, with form reviews managed using existing resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency tasked with enforcing state health insurance mandates. It is responsible for reviewing policy and form filings from carriers to ensure compliance with the prohibition on step therapy or fail-first protocols for insulin, and will collect form filing fees associated with updated policies.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Although the program is already compliant and does not impose step therapy or fail-first protocols on diabetes medications, DBM is directly reviewed for potential state benefit plan impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee to advise on the planning process, collect public input, and make recommendations regarding the development and historical preservation of Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park, with annual reports required through 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of Anne Arundel County, adjacent communities to Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park, historical and cultural preservationists, and park visitors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or Anne Arundel County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives (or their designee) as a statutory member of the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee.
The bill requires the Governor to appoint one member representing the Office of the Governor to serve on the newly established advisory committee.
The committee includes a representative of Bowie State University, designated by the university's president. Bowie State University is a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a state-authorized advisory body, the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee, to advise on site planning, historical preservation, and development.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the representative of the Office of the Governor to the advisory committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters continuing education requirements for license renewal of real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons in Maryland. The bill modifies required clock hours and topics for courses including fair housing, Americans with Disabilities Act compliance, and broker supervision; repeals the topic of property flipping from required ethics coursework; specifies that course providers select instructors; and authorizes the State Real Estate Commission to set continuing education course application fees rather than keeping the statutory $25 fee.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, real estate salespersons, and real estate continuing education course providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Real Estate Commission can implement the bill's changes with existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected, as the Commission does not plan to change the course application fee from its current $25 level. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Department is directly responsible for administering the licensing, continuing education requirements, and fee schedules for real estate brokers and salespersons.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 974 requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce coverage mandates for preventive health services without cost-sharing consistent with federal guidelines and recommendations in effect on December 31, 2024. The bill permits the Commissioner to adopt regulations expanding coverage or incorporating future recommendations, and clarifies how deductibles apply to preventive services under high deductible health plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, Maryland insureds and enrollees (including those enrolled in high deductible health plans), healthcare providers, and religious organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article and directly mandates the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce health insurance preventive services coverage requirements without cost-sharing and authorizes the Commissioner to adopt regulations to implement and enforce these standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires self-service storage facility operators to notify occupants of the time, place, and terms of a public sale at least 10 days before selling stored personal property to satisfy a lien. If the operator sends the notice via email and does not receive a response or delivery confirmation at least 5 days before the sale, the operator must promptly send a second notice by verified mail.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators of self-service storage facilities and occupants leasing storage space.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General houses the Consumer Protection Division, which enforces statutory provisions under the Commercial Law Article concerning consumer protections, notices, and commercial transactions like self-service storage lien sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Language Assistance Program requiring the State Board of Elections (SBE) to determine counties where there is a significant need for language assistance for voters in languages other than English based on specific demographic thresholds. Local boards of elections in designated counties must provide translation services at early voting centers and polling places, post notices in designated languages, provide online voting materials in those languages, and make reasonable efforts to recruit bilingual election judges.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Voters with limited English proficiency, local boards of elections, and county election officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $122,000 in FY 2026, reflecting $50,000 for a demographics consultant and $72,000 for translation software service licenses, with ongoing costs of at least $50,000 in FY 2028 and FY 2030. Local government expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 for qualifying counties to cover hardware, software usage fees, polling place signage, and written translation of materials. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 983 establishes the Language Assistance Program under the oversight and administration of the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE). SBE is directly responsible for determining county need, designating languages, publishing lists on its website, adopting regulations, and procuring licensed translation software services, resulting in direct general fund expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill incorporates electric cooperatives into existing "make whole" rate proceedings before the Public Service Commission (PSC) to evaluate whether additional revenues are needed to meet an authorized debt service coverage ratio established in a prior base rate proceeding. It also requires the PSC to order an electric cooperative to conduct a public hearing regarding proposed rate adjustments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric cooperatives in Maryland and their customers/ratepayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly impacted; the Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body directly responsible for implementing the bill, conducting the specified rate proceedings for electric cooperatives, evaluating debt service coverage ratios, and ordering cooperatives to conduct public hearings.

The Office of the People's Counsel (OPC) represents residential utility customers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission, including electric cooperative rate cases and public hearings governed by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class B-OB-CRD (office building – commercial revitalization district) beer, wine, and liquor license in Baltimore County, permitting the Board of License Commissioners to issue up to one such license to a restaurant located in an office building of at least 100,000 square feet within the Towson Commercial Revitalization District. It allows on-premises sale of beer, wine, and liquor and off-premises sale of wine with prepared food, and creates exceptions to distance restrictions near places of worship if written consent is obtained.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurant owners and commercial office building operators in the Towson Commercial Revitalization District, nearby places of worship, and patrons in Baltimore County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore County revenues increase by $1,500 annually beginning in FY 2026 from the license fee for the single Class B-OB-CRD license issued. Baltimore County expenditures are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) to place and operate speed monitoring systems on Maryland Route 200 (the Intercounty Connector) in Montgomery County. The bill directs the District Court to collect and remit civil penalties resulting from these cameras to MDTA, and requires the State Highway Administration to grant MDTA access to its speed monitoring systems and vendor contracts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Maryland Route 200 (Intercounty Connector) in Montgomery County, MDTA, and the District Court of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $277,800 in FY 2026 for one-time District Court system programming upgrades. MDTA nonbudgeted program expenditures are estimated at approximately $1.5 million annually, which are expected to be fully offset by potentially significant nonbudgeted revenues generated from $40 speed camera citations. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDTA is the primary implementing agency under the bill, authorized to deploy and administer speed monitoring systems on Maryland Route 200 (ICC) in Montgomery County, manage vendor contracts, and receive remitted civil penalty revenues.

The District Court of Maryland is tasked with collecting civil penalties from State-operated automated enforcement systems, scheduling contested hearings, remitting revenues to MDTA, and incurring a $277,800 fiscal expenditure in FY 2026 to update cashiering systems.

SHA is specifically required by Section 6 of the bill to provide MDTA with access to its existing speed monitoring systems and vendor contacts, and is consulted regarding signage standards and training programs.

MDOT is the parent department overseeing state transportation infrastructure, including modal administrations like SHA that must collaborate with MDTA on speed monitoring deployment and traffic standards.

The Comptroller coordinates with the Chief Judge of the District Court regarding the system for remitting court-collected costs, fines, and civil penalties, and receives excess speed monitoring system revenues under general statutory provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of Maryland's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program and its application to public-private partnerships, offshore wind projects, video lottery terminals, and sports wagering licensees by one year, to July 1, 2026. It also extends the deadlines for completing the associated disparity study, disparity analyses, implementation guidelines, and related reports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs and Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), women-owned businesses, State procurement contractors, public-private partnership entities, offshore wind developers, video lottery terminal operators, and sports wagering licensees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local government finances. Extending the due dates for the disparity study and related analyses does not affect the total cost of those studies, and restoring the application of the MBE program to public-private partnerships and sports wagering licensees has no practical fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary coordinating entity responsible for administering and monitoring the State's MBE program, establishing policies and guidelines, consulting on MBE goals for public-private partnerships, sports wagering, and capital projects, and submitting required reports and disparity evaluations.

MDOT serves as the State's designated MBE certification agency and is responsible for conducting the comprehensive disparity study, disparity analyses regarding offshore wind and P3s, and studies evaluating MBE participation.

The bill mandates that OAG be consulted in establishing MBE participation goals and procedures for P3s, sports wagering licensees, offshore wind projects, disparity study analyses, and developing race- and gender-neutral program approaches.

The bill prohibits BPW from approving any public-private partnership (P3) agreement until MBE participation goals and procedures are established, and BPW designates the MBE certification agency and adopts regulations related to disparity study data collection.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends MBE compliance requirements for video lottery terminal (VLT) licensees and restores MBE requirements for sports wagering licensees, which are regulated by the agency.

The bill extends the sunset date for MBE participation goals and procedures for approved offshore wind projects, which are regulated by the PSC through offshore wind renewable energy credit (OREC) approvals.
As the State's primary operational procurement authority, DGS is directly impacted by the one-year extension of the statutory MBE program and its procurement requirements.

The bill alters reporting deadlines for a required study regarding minority- and women-owned business participation in brokerage and investment management services used by the State Retirement and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study the Rise in Adverse Decisions in the State Health Care System to review adverse decision reporting requirements across health payers, recommend standardized reporting definitions and processes, develop strategies to reduce adverse decisions, and propose relevant legislation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission and the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care consumers and patients, health insurance carriers, managed care organizations, health care providers, and hospitals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2026 only for the Health Services Cost Review Commission to hire contractual services for data collection, analysis, and reporting. The Maryland Insurance Administration can participate using existing resources. There is no effect on revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is required to jointly staff the Workgroup with the Maryland Insurance Administration and its Executive Director serves as a member. Additionally, the bill incurs a direct fiscal impact of $50,000 in FY 2026 special fund expenditures for HSCRC to procure contractual services to support the workgroup.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Workgroup, and the Maryland Insurance Administration is jointly responsible for providing staff support for the Workgroup and its study of adverse health decisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary entity, the Workgroup to Study the Rise in Adverse Decisions in the State Health Care System, tasked with conducting a study, developing recommendations, and reporting to the General Assembly before terminating in 2026.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission (or their designee) is designated by statute as a voting member of the Workgroup.

The Deputy Secretary of the Maryland Medicaid Program (within the Department of Health), or their designee, is mandated to serve as a member of the Workgroup to examine adverse decisions across health payers.
The Director of the Health Education and Advocacy Unit of the Office of the Attorney General (or their designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup.
The bill requires the Governor to appoint multiple stakeholder members to the Workgroup, representing hospitals, insurers, providers, physicians, and consumer advocacy organizations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the appointment of the eleven non-governmental Workgroup members.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Phenibut Consumer Protection Act regulates the distribution, marketing, and sale of phenibut products in Maryland. It requires retailers to disclose the factual basis of product representations on labels, prohibits the sale of phenibut products to individuals under 21, and bans adulterated products, therapeutic claims, and marketing targeted toward minors. Violations are subject to civil and criminal penalties, as well as liability for civil damages.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers, manufacturers, and distributors of phenibut products, consumers of dietary and supplement products, and individuals under the age of 21.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances and operations. The Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations and local health departments can handle enforcement with existing budgeted resources. Civil and criminal penalty provisions are not expected to have a material financial impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds the Phenibut Consumer Protection Act under the Health - General Article and explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health adopt regulations to implement and carry out the subtitle.

The bill creates consumer protection standards, advertising bans, and civil penalty structures regarding phenibut products, falling within the regulatory and enforcement scope of the Consumer Protection Division.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense punishable by fines and up to 90 days imprisonment, authorizes civil penalties, and establishes civil liability for damages, which impacts court dockets and judicial operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to integrate information regarding FDA-approved treatments for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias into public health outreach programs for healthcare providers and the public. It also directs MDH, in collaboration with the State-designated health information exchange, to create and maintain a publicly accessible website providing downloadable data on the prevalence and hospitalization rates of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias in Maryland, updated annually beginning in 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals living with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, their caregivers, healthcare providers, and the general public (particularly Black and Latino communities at higher risk of cognitive decline).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $59,019 in FY 2026 to hire a part-time contractual epidemiologist and cover technology costs to launch the website. Expenditures total $40,822 in FY 2027 and $21,000 annually thereafter for ongoing technology and licensing fees. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including updating public health outreach programs to include information on FDA-approved treatments and establishing and maintaining a public website with data on the prevalence and hospitalization rates of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

The Department of Aging is designated in the statute as an explicit partner agency required to work alongside the Department of Health in incorporating the new educational and treatment awareness information into public health outreach programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Encompasses the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, which is explicitly named in the legislation as a collaborating entity responsible for partnering with the Department of Health on outreach programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits life and disability insurance carriers from unfairly discriminating against individuals based on medical information or genetic test results unless supported by actuarially sound principles or actual/reasonably anticipated experience. Additionally, prohibits insurers from accessing sensitive medical information without written consent and from mandating genetic testing or full genome sequencing as a condition of eligibility or coverage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants, policyholders, and insurers of life and disability insurance in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee, with form reviews handled within existing resources. General fund revenues from the 2% insurance premium tax may be affected if premium rates change, but any impact is expected to be minimal and indeterminate. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates life and disability insurance carriers by prohibiting certain uses of genetic test results and sensitive medical information under the Insurance Article. The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for reviewing rate and policy form filings and enforcing compliance through the Insurance Commissioner's administrative and enforcement powers.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the African American Heritage Preservation Program and Grant Fund to allow the receipt of grants and donations, and authorizes the Secretary of Planning to use these funds to award noncapital grants for preserving or sharing African American history and culture in Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust and the Maryland Department of Planning, in partnership with the Commission on African American History and Culture
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, business entities, nonprofit organizations, and local governments applying for or receiving grants to preserve or share African American history and culture in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, special fund revenues and expenditures for the African American Heritage Preservation Grant Fund will increase correspondingly as grants and donations are received and disbursed for noncapital grants or projects. The specific annual amounts cannot be reliably estimated. Local government revenues and expenditures may also increase if they receive and spend noncapital grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust operates within the Department of Planning and administers the African American Heritage Preservation Program and Grant Fund. The Secretary of Planning makes final award decisions for the newly authorized noncapital grants and adopts implementing regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on African American History and Culture co-develops and administers the Program in partnership with the Maryland Historical Trust, reviews grant applications, and makes award recommendations to the Secretary of Planning.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the African American Heritage Preservation Grant Fund, which will receive and disburse new revenues from grants and donations.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the African American Heritage Preservation Grant Fund, which will experience increased transactions and balances from incoming grants and donations.
The Board of Public Works is referenced in statute to approve certain program regulations and specific grants financed through the sale of State general obligation bonds.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force by one year to June 30, 2026. It requires the task force to identify funding sources and mechanisms to redevelop the Baltimore Convention site and its surrounding area, establish and sustain the operations of a redevelopment authority, and report its findings and recommendations by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force (staffed by the Maryland Department of Commerce)
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City government, convention visitors, tourists, and local businesses in the hospitality, restaurant, lodging, and tourism industries in Baltimore City and surrounding counties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $350,000 in FY 2026 for the Department of Commerce to hire consultants specializing in convention center funding and governance to assist the task force. Member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce provides primary staff support to the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force and is projected to incur $350,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2026 to procure consultant services to complete the study on funding sources and governance mechanisms.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date of the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force by one year to June 30, 2026, and expands its charge to identify specific funding sources and mechanisms for redeveloping the Baltimore Convention site and establishing the authority.

The Maryland Stadium Authority has existing statutory responsibilities and financial agreements governing the Baltimore Convention Center, including administering capital improvement funds and co-funding operating reserves, which will be directly impacted by the task force's findings and redevelopment proposals.
The bill requires the Task Force to submit its findings and recommendations regarding funding sources and mechanisms directly to the Governor on or before December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires banking institutions, credit unions, and mortgage lenders to include a provision in conventional home mortgage loans authorizing an existing borrower to purchase the property interest of another borrower by assuming the seller's share of the mortgage in connection with a decree of absolute divorce, provided the assuming borrower qualifies. It also requires written disclosure of this assumption provision to loan applicants prior to completing an application and applies retroactively to pre-existing conventional home mortgage loans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Borrowers undergoing absolute divorce, conventional mortgage loan applicants, banking institutions, credit unions, and mortgage lenders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local government fiscal impact. Small business lenders may experience a potential minimal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), which supervises and regulates state-chartered banks, credit unions, and licensed mortgage lenders. OFR is responsible for enforcing compliance with the lending, contract term, and disclosure requirements established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Fair Medical Debt Reporting Act prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including medical debt or medical debt collection information in consumer reports and bars using such information to determine a consumer's creditworthiness. It also prohibits healthcare providers and medical businesses from reporting medical debt to credit reporting agencies, requires medical debt collection contracts to prohibit such reporting, and requires hospitals by November 1, 2025, to instruct consumer reporting agencies to delete previously reported adverse credit information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division) and the Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers with medical debt, healthcare providers, hospitals, medical facilities, debt collection entities, and consumer reporting agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect Maryland State or local governmental operations or finances. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Section 19-214.2 of the Health - General Article, which mandates the debt collection policies and reporting requirements that Maryland hospitals must annually submit to the Commission.

The bill amends the Commercial Law Article to restrict medical debt reporting and creditworthiness determinations, which falls directly under consumer protection enforcement administered by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill adds a new subtitle to Title 24 of the Health - General Article establishing restrictions and contract requirements on medical debt disclosure by healthcare facilities, practitioners, and medical service providers.
The Department of Labor regulates collection agencies and financial institutions that interact with consumer credit reporting and debt collection practices affected by the bill's provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors from requiring an applicant to hold a bachelor's degree or higher to qualify for licensure as a real estate appraiser or certification as a residential real estate appraiser.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors (Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants seeking licensure as real estate appraisers or certification as residential real estate appraisers, certified appraisers, trainees, and the Maryland appraisal industry.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected as the commission can implement the requirements with existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs licensing and certification standards enforced by the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, an occupational licensing unit housed within the Maryland Department of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames Frederick County's beer and wine consumption permit and beer, wine, and liquor consumption permit as tasting permits, alters restrictions on sample amounts, and requires the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to regulate the quantities served to individuals and the number of containers used.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverage license holders and retail customers/patrons in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill does not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees statewide regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry. Although this bill specifically alters local retail tasting permits administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System to review existing services, assess best practices, and develop plans for implementing an expanded 3-1-1 nonemergency system and virtual portal in Maryland, with a final report due by November 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking nonemergency government services and information, local 9-1-1 and 3-1-1 public safety answering points, local governments, and telecommunications providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2026 only for the Department of Information Technology to hire a consultant to provide research, subject matter expertise, and staffing support for the workgroup. Workgroup member reimbursements are absorbable within existing resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) chairs the Workgroup, and the department is responsible for providing staff support. Additionally, DoIT has a direct fiscal impact of $50,000 in FY 2026 to hire a consultant to support the Workgroup and draft the report.

The Secretary of Emergency Management and the Executive Director of the Maryland 9-1-1 Board (housed within MDEM) are designated statutory members of the Workgroup, which evaluates nonemergency systems to reduce 9-1-1 congestion.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup to study and plan the expanded 3-1-1 system.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the Workgroup to ensure accessibility and representation in the expanded nonemergency system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup to Study Implementation of an Expanded 3-1-1 Nonemergency System, to study best practices and report recommendations.
The Workgroup is mandated to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by November 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the Objective Criteria Committee of the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and establishes a new Compensation and Staffing Committee in its place. It transfers responsibilities regarding the establishment of objective criteria for staffing levels, qualifications, compensation, and incentive pay to the new committee. Additionally, it clarifies the conditions under which the Chief Investment Officer and Investment Division personnel can receive awarded incentive compensation if they retire directly from the division after a separation or furlough.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Chief Investment Officer and professional staff of the Investment Division of the State Retirement Agency, and the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $10,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 (with the exception of FY 2029, when a consultant would have been hired under current law) to retain a consultant assisting the Compensation and Staffing Committee. Expenditures may increase further if the consultant is engaged to provide executive search services. The State Retirement Agency can otherwise staff the committee with existing resources. There is no effect on revenues and minimal local impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Board of Trustees and the Investment Division of the State Retirement Agency, altering committee structures (replacing the Objective Criteria Committee with the Compensation and Staffing Committee), setting rules for CIO and investment staff compensation and incentives, and requiring special fund expenditures for a consultant.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or the Secretary's designee) is statutorily designated as a required member of the newly created Compensation and Staffing Committee of the Board of Trustees.
The State Treasurer (or the Treasurer's designee) is explicitly identified as an official who may be appointed to the Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The Comptroller of Maryland (or the Comptroller's designee) is explicitly identified as an official who may be appointed to the Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill makes certain Maryland Department of Health employees at specified facilities members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) as a condition of employment rather than the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System. It also provides for the transfer of prior service credit and clarifies membership, vesting, and retirement allowance calculations for affected employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Up to 30 Maryland Department of Health employees in specified supervisory and managerial positions across seven state health and psychiatric facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities increase by $470,000, resulting in an increase in State pension contributions of $53,600 in FY 2028 (allocated 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal and other funds), with annual increases thereafter according to actuarial assumptions. The State Retirement Agency can administer transfers using existing resources. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Employees' Pension System (EPS). The agency is directly responsible for administering the transfer of service credit, calculating retirement and disability benefits, and processing opt-out elections under the bill.

The bill specifically applies to designated positions and facilities within the Maryland Department of Health (such as Eastern Shore Hospital Center, Spring Grove Hospital Center, and others), moving certain supervisory and direct care staff into CORS as a condition of employment.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and personnel classifications, and is responsible for incorporating the increased state employer pension contributions into future state budgets.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the threshold for exempting certain State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) service and disability retirees from reemployment earnings limitations and benefit suspensions. Instead of a fixed average final compensation (AFC) cap of less than $25,000, the bill establishes that retirees are exempt if their AFC was less than the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale as of January 1 of the preceding calendar year.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System Board of Trustees
qa_results.stakeholders: Reemployed service and disability retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System whose average final compensation was below the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale, as well as participating public employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates because the State Retirement and Pension System does not account for foregone benefit offsets. It has no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), including calculating average final compensation, enforcing reemployment earnings limitations, and applying exemptions from benefit offsets or suspensions.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM establishes and maintains the standard State pay scale, the minimum annual salary of which serves as the statutory benchmark for the reemployment earnings limitation exemptions in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1034 extends the statutory due dates for two annual reports prepared by the State Retirement Agency regarding minority business enterprise utilization and Maryland-based venture capital investments. It also clarifies eligibility for the State Police Retirement System's Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) by basing the participation duration on years of employment in an eligible position rather than years of eligibility service credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (including Maryland State Troopers and State Police Cadets), minority business enterprise brokerage and investment management services firms, and the State Retirement and Pension System.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material effect on State governmental operations or finances, and no local fiscal effect. Linking DROP eligibility to years of employment rather than service credit restores eligibility to intended levels, affecting an estimated single individual, and has no material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1034 directly alters reporting deadlines for reports issued by the State Retirement and Pension System's Investment Committee and Board of Trustees, and clarifies statutory eligibility criteria for the State Police Retirement System's Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP), which the agency administers.

The bill directly modifies eligibility standards for participation in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) for members of the State Police Retirement System, including Maryland State Troopers and the Secretary of State Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the annual statutory deadline from September 1 to November 1 for a report submitted to this office regarding minority business enterprise (MBE) brokerage and investment management utilization by the State Retirement and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Next Generation Energy Act comprehensively alters Maryland's regulation and procurement of electricity and gas infrastructure. Among other provisions, the act authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to issue loans for emissions-reduction projects; establishes competitive solicitation and expedited Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) processes for dispatchable generation, energy storage, and nuclear energy; sets specific rate schedule requirements for large load customers; restricts utility cost recovery for certain expenses; excludes waste-to-energy and refuse-derived fuel from Tier 1 of the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS); and directs Strategic Energy Investment Fund compliance fees to provide electric bill credits to residential customers in fiscal 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residential, commercial, and industrial electric and natural gas customers; investor-owned utilities, municipal electric utilities, and electric cooperatives; clean energy, nuclear, and energy storage developers; and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by $200 million to distribute residential electric customer bill credits funded by a transfer from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. PSC and Office of People's Counsel administrative special fund expenditures increase by at least $2.9 million annually beginning in FY 2026, matched by assessment revenues on utilities. Department of Natural Resources expenditures increase by $0.8 million in FY 2026 and at least $1.2 million annually thereafter. Local finances are impacted, including an estimated $12.2 million annual revenue loss for Montgomery County starting in FY 2027 due to the removal of waste-to-energy from the RPS.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency under the bill. It is responsible for overseeing utility rates, reviewing gas infrastructure replacement plans, regulating large load tariffs, conducting procurements for energy storage and nuclear generation, administering expedited Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) reviews, and overseeing the distribution of $200 million in ratepayer relief credits.

MEA is tasked with pursuing interstate cost-sharing and federal siting agreements for nuclear energy in coordination with PSC and DNR, reporting on those efforts, and managing the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is significantly impacted by the transfer of up to $200 million for ratepayer refunds.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is assigned key statutory duties to review, evaluate, and recommend proposals for dispatchable energy and large capacity energy resources, evaluate CPCN application completeness under expedited timelines, and coordinate on regional nuclear agreements.

OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC. The numerous new complex regulatory proceedings, multi-year rate cases, and procurement dockets established by the bill require OPC to expand staff and consultant capacity, and OPC is granted fast-track procurement authority.

DHCD is authorized to issue loans in addition to grants for multifamily residential building greenhouse gas reduction projects and can count expanded funding sources toward its EmPOWER Maryland energy reduction targets, significantly altering its program financing and ratepayer funding needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is specifically required by the bill, in consultation with the Office of the Attorney General, to assist potential applicants and minority investors in nuclear energy projects and establish clear plans for setting MBE participation goals and procedures.
DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer (CPO), who is required under new fast-track procurement provisions to review and approve specified consultant procurement contracts within five business days.

MD Labor's Commissioner of Labor and Industry is tasked with determining prevailing wage rates and enforcing prevailing wage and labor standards required for underground infrastructure contracts, energy storage construction, and community benefit agreements under the bill.

DHS is mandated to submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, detailing legislative and regulatory changes needed to consolidate all State energy assistance programs into a single program.

The Comptroller administers Maryland's income tax and will be responsible for implementing the new income tax subtraction modification for legislative energy relief refunds received by residential utility customers.

The OAG is required to consult with GOSBA to provide assistance to potential applicants and minority investors and to establish minority business enterprise plans and procedures for approved nuclear generation projects.

As the State's MBE certification agency, MDOT is identified in the fiscal note as needing to conduct a disparity study to evaluate MBE participation in nuclear energy facilities to support GOSBA's goal-setting requirements.

MDE is granted fast-track consultant procurement authority for climate and greenhouse gas matters, provides greenhouse gas emissions data used to set baseline reduction targets, and handles air and water quality permitting for new generation and storage facilities.

The Governor is specifically authorized to transfer up to $200 million by budget amendment from SEIF to PSC for electric bill refunds and receives multiple mandated reports from state agencies under the bill.
BPW maintains overarching constitutional and statutory oversight of State procurements, including reviewing contracts exceeding $200,000 that may arise under the fast-track procurement provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Renewable Energy Certainty Act establishes a standardized framework for the siting, review, and approval of solar energy generating stations and front-of-the-meter energy storage devices. It creates a Distributed Generation Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (DGCPCN) for community solar systems between 2 and 5 megawatts, restricts local governments from banning these facilities or denying conforming site plans, and requires expedited local reviews. Additionally, it establishes consumer protections and a special contractor license for residential rooftop solar installations, updates state solar mapping tools, and directs the Public Service Commission to conduct studies on energy procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Solar and energy storage developers, electric companies and suppliers, residential rooftop solar customers and contractors, community solar subscribers (including low- to moderate-income households), and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State expenditures increase by approximately $2.41 million across agencies: $403,385 in special funds for the Public Service Commission (PSC), $1,816,564 in general/special funds for the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Power Plant Research Program, and $187,270 in general funds for the Maryland Department of Labor. PSC special fund revenues increase correspondingly by $403,385 in FY 2026 and by at least $0.7 million annually beginning in FY 2027 from utility assessments and DGCPCN application fees. MD Labor general fund revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 from licensing fees. Local government operations and finances may be significantly impacted through altered zoning authority, administrative permitting workloads, and changes in local tax and permit revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulator and implementing agency under the bill, responsible for establishing and issuing Distributed Generation Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (DGCPCNs), approving front-of-the-meter energy storage devices, adopting associated regulations, jointly setting application fees, and conducting two major studies on generation procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.

The department's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is tasked with developing proposed standard siting and design requirements and licensing conditions for DGCPCNs, reviewing DGCPCN applications, jointly setting application fees, updating the SmartDG+ tool, and assessing State-owned land for solar suitability, requiring significant additional staff and budget.

The Maryland Department of Labor is required to establish and administer a new special solar contractor license for individuals installing and maintaining residential rooftop solar energy generating systems, establish minimum qualifications, and handle licensing enforcement.

The Maryland Energy Administration is statutorily required to consult with the Department of Natural Resources to update the SmartDG+ screening tool with State-owned land and complete an analysis identifying State land suitable for solar energy development.

The Department of Planning is required to consult with the Department of Natural Resources on updating the SmartDG+ tool and analyzing State-owned land for solar development, and is involved in land use coordination concerning Priority Preservation Areas.
The Department of Transportation must consult with the Department of Natural Resources to update the SmartDG+ tool and evaluate State-owned land suitable for solar energy development.

The Department of the Environment must be notified of power plant construction CPCN applications, is required to expedite regulatory processes under electricity procurement models, and oversees environmental and stormwater standards referenced in the bill.

The bill mandates that herbicide use on solar and energy storage sites comply with the Department of Agriculture's weed control program and references agricultural activities recognized by the department for agrivoltaics.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility customer interests in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding CPCN/DGCPCN approvals, utility rate impacts, and the mandated generation procurement and community solar studies.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and enforcement support for state agencies, with the fiscal note budgeting for legal staffing to assist the Department of Labor with developing and enforcing the new solar contractor licensing program.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates statutory references to federal law across several health insurance consumer protection standards and the State Family Planning Program to reflect federal regulations in effect on December 31, 2024. It expands the definitions of 'legally protected health care' and 'sensitive health services' to include gender-affirming care under medical record confidentiality laws, and establishes concurrent enforcement jurisdiction between the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights regarding nondiscrimination in health insurance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Commission on Civil Rights, and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals receiving family planning, reproductive health, or gender-affirming services; health insurance carriers; health insurance policyholders; and health care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates numerous insurance consumer protection provisions under Title 15 of the Insurance Article, grants the Insurance Commissioner concurrent jurisdiction to enforce anti-discrimination laws in health insurance, and authorizes the Commissioner to adopt corresponding regulations.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Family Planning Program and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program administered by MDH, and alters statutory definitions of 'legally protected health care' and 'sensitive health services' regarding medical records and health care protection under the Secretary of Health.

The bill establishes concurrent jurisdiction between the Commission on Civil Rights and the Insurance Commissioner to enforce statutory prohibitions against discrimination by health insurance carriers.

The bill updates federal reference dates governing the Exchange's statutory requirement to adopt regulations establishing processes for hardship and affordability exemptions, and requires the Insurance Commissioner to consult with the Exchange regarding summary of benefits and coverage standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits motor vehicle mechanical repair contracts from including provisions that preclude coverage solely for vehicle issues identified in a technical service bulletin, and prohibits guarantors or providers from denying claims solely because the diagnosed issue was identified in such a bulletin.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners who purchase mechanical repair contracts or extended warranties, as well as vehicle dealers, contract obligors, guarantors, and providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Service Contracts and Consumer Products Guaranty Act under Title 14 of the Commercial Law Article, which the bill amends to prohibit excluding coverage or denying claims based on technical service bulletins.
