The Motor Vehicle Administration licenses and regulates motor vehicle dealers who sell mechanical repair contracts governed by § 15-311.2 of the Transportation Article referenced in the bill.
As the parent agency overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and transportation-related commerce, MDOT provided analysis on vehicle repair contract regulations.
Obligors who issue mechanical repair contracts are required to register annually with and submit required documentation to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Judicial and Public Safety for Service Members Act establishes uniform statutory definitions for military and uniformed services terms across several articles of the Maryland Code. It broadens various existing rights, exemptions, protections, and benefits—including those relating to court records, jury service, firearms licensing, militia service, residential leases, and civil relief—to encompass all uniformed services, including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service (PHS) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), rather than solely the armed forces.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty service members, reserve component members, and veterans of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, PHS, and NOAA), as well as their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2026 only to update the Department of State Police licensing portal to accommodate uniformed services identification. Other agencies and the Judiciary can absorb any operational or minimal programming costs within existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters firearm licensing exemptions and acceptable identification to include uniformed services, requiring a $50,000 update to the Maryland State Police licensing portal in FY 2026. It also governs the reappointment of police employees who resign to enter uniformed service.

The bill amends the Department's governing statute (State Government § 9-901) to establish standard definitions for veterans and military families, and tasks the Department with presenting State flags to the families of deceased service members.

The bill amends provisions governing the organized militia, appointment and commissioning standards in the Maryland Defense Force, and the Adjutant General's authority to organize uniformed honor guards for deceased veterans.

The bill updates definitions, enlistment, and Maryland Code of Military Justice provisions impacting Guard members, and references information to be posted on the Maryland National Guard website under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act.

The bill impacts judicial operations by expanding fee exemptions for court records to all service members of the uniformed services, updating the juror qualification form, and altering provisions on CINA court jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Correctional Services § 2-109, requiring the Secretary to adopt regulations exempting honorably discharged reserve component members of the uniformed services from the minimum age requirement for correctional officers.
The bill updates eligibility terminology regarding uniformed services duty for out-of-home placement programs administered for former CINAs under the Family Law Article.
The bill amends the statutory definition of 'emergency management' in Public Safety § 14-101 to exclude functions for which the uniformed services are primarily responsible.
The bill amends Public Safety § 1-202 regarding the Secretary of State's duty to issue State flags to the families of uniformed service members killed in the line of duty.

The bill expands contract termination rights and consumer protections under the State's Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which falls within the enforcement jurisdiction of the Consumer Protection Division.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that project site visits and educational field tours do not constitute open meetings subject to live video or audio streaming requirements for the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, provided that no organizational business is conducted.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Planning Board and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and staff of the Montgomery County Planning Board, Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC), and members of the public seeking access to their meetings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Montgomery County Planning Board or the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General provides legal interpretation and advice regarding the Open Meetings Act and statutory compliance across Maryland public bodies, and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Prince George’s County Board of Appeals by requiring the County Council to appoint at least three members rather than exactly three, and establishes that a simple majority of members must concur in any resolution rather than a fixed minimum of two.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County residents, members of the Prince George's County Board of Appeals, and individuals or entities appealing local zoning and administrative decisions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal year 2026 if additional members are appointed to the Board of Appeals (compensation, fringe benefits, and operating expenses). Prince George's County revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to establish a workgroup dedicated to improving health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use. The workgroup must evaluate the availability and outcomes of substance use disorder treatment, criminal justice involvement and its associated costs, and regulations governing patient discharge from treatment programs, and recommend policy changes to mitigate harms related to criminalization.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with substance use disorders, justice-involved individuals, patients in treatment programs, and substance use disorder treatment providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health increase by $38,000 in FY 2026 and $39,600 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time contractual health policy analyst to staff the workgroup until the commission's scheduled termination on June 30, 2027. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) provides administrative and staffing support to the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access. The bill requires the new workgroup to review MDH's regulations concerning patient discharge standards from substance use treatment programs, and MDH incurs general fund expenditures to hire contractual staff to support the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily establishes a new workgroup under the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access focused on the improvement of health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use, requiring regular meetings, evaluation, and annual reporting.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from selling, delivering, or issuing health insurance policies, life insurance policies, annuity contracts, or HMO contracts that contain discretionary clauses reserving sole discretion to the carrier to interpret policy terms or establish review standards inconsistent with Maryland law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Insurance carriers (including insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations) and consumers/policyholders holding health insurance, life insurance, annuities, or HMO contracts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee as carriers update forms. The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for reviewing and approving insurance policies, contracts, and form filings, as well as enforcing compliance with state insurance laws prohibiting discretionary clauses in life, health, annuity, and HMO contracts.

The bill amends the Health - General Article (§ 19-706) to apply the discretionary clause prohibition to health maintenance organizations (HMOs), which fall under statutory provisions codified within the Department of Health's governing article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the State and participating local employers pay separate administrative fees to the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), instead funding administrative and operational expenses directly through the accumulation fund in fiscal year 2026 and incorporating those expenses into the actuarially certified employer normal contribution rates beginning in fiscal year 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and the State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, participating local governmental employers (such as local school boards, community colleges, and participating governmental units), and the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State Retirement Agency (SRA) special fund revenues decrease by an estimated $21.8 million due to the cancellation of local employer administrative fee payments, resulting in an identical $21.8 million expenditure reduction for local participating employers. State general fund expenditures decrease by $5.7 million ($5,691,206) in FY 2026 due to a planned budget reversion, accompanied by an equal reduction in reimbursable fund revenues for SRA. Beginning in FY 2027, the inclusion of administrative and operating expenses in the employer normal contribution rate fully offsets the repeal of administrative fees, resulting in no material net effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) and its Board of Trustees are the primary entities governed by the bill, which restructures the funding mechanism for SRA's administrative and operational expenses by repealing per-participant administrative fees and incorporating those costs directly into actuarially certified employer contribution rates.

The Board of Trustees is required to annually certify the employer contribution rates to the Secretary of Budget and Management. DBM also oversees state personnel retirement benefit budgeting, which is fiscally impacted in fiscal 2026 through general fund expenditure decreases and budget reversions.
The bill requires the Board of Trustees to annually certify the recommended employer contribution rates directly to the Governor for the formulation of the annual state budget.

The bill repeals Section 21-316 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, which previously required the Comptroller to exercise the right of setoff against delinquent local employers for unpaid administrative fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1076 requires residential landlords to provide tenants with at least 24 hours of written advance notice before entering a leased premises, limits entry to between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday (except during emergencies or by mutual agreement), specifies permitted reasons and delivery methods for entry notices, and authorizes courts to grant injunctive relief and assess damages for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Maryland Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords, and property managers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The small business effect is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory civil cause of action allowing residential tenants to seek injunctive relief and damages against landlords in court for unlawful entry or improper demands for entry, which directly impacts the court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, oversees statewide consumer protection and landlord-tenant rights, and was consulted regarding the legal and operational impact of this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $200 million in the annual operating or capital budget bill for site redevelopment and transportation infrastructure improvements related to the relocation of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) headquarters to Prince George's County, contingent upon the U.S. General Services Administration applying for a relocation permit from Prince George's County or the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, commuters, and businesses in Prince George's County (specifically the Greenbelt area), as well as the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the U.S. General Services Administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is estimated to be zero assuming $200 million in previously authorized General Obligation (GO) bond funding satisfies the bill's mandate over fiscal years 2026 through 2028. If interpreted as requiring an additional $200 million, Pay-As-You-Go Transportation Trust Fund expenditures and/or GO bond expenditures would increase by up to $200 million in fiscal 2027. Local effect is zero.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a statutory requirement mandating the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $200,000,000 in the annual operating or capital budget bill for the FBI headquarters relocation project if the specified condition is met.

As the principal agency responsible for developing and administering the state operating and capital budgets on behalf of the Governor, DBM is directly impacted by the mandated appropriation requirement and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

The mandated appropriation is dedicated to transportation infrastructure improvements and site redevelopment, which are programmed in MDOT's Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP) and could impact Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) or General Obligation bond funding allocations.

The funding supports highway infrastructure improvements, specifically the construction of an interchange along I-95/I-495 at the Greenbelt Metro Station under the jurisdiction and operational scope of MDOT SHA.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1080 authorizes county and municipal governmental units in Maryland to provide paid disaster service leave (up to 30 days in a 12-month period) to employees who are certified disaster service volunteers or members of specified volunteer emergency response organizations. It also authorizes local governments to grant paid leave for jury service, approved employee organization events, uniformed services training or active reserve duty, subpoenaed court or administrative appearances, certain administrative removals, and any other purpose deemed necessary by the local government head.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governmental units of Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: County and municipal government employees—especially volunteer emergency responders, disaster service volunteers, and military reservists—and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for overtime, substitute coverage, and payroll costs if local governmental units choose to provide additional paid leave to their employees. Because the provisions are discretionary and require approval from the local government, specific dollar estimates are indeterminate. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes paid disaster service leave for local government employees who volunteer with disaster relief organizations, including Maryland VOAD, CERT, and volunteer fire and rescue entities, which directly support emergency response and disaster resilience efforts coordinated statewide by MDEM.

The bill authorizes local government units to provide up to 30 days of leave with pay for employees participating in uniformed services training or active duty in the organized militia, which is overseen and commanded by the Adjutant General.

The Maryland National Guard constitutes the organized militia referenced in the bill; local government personnel who are Guard members may be granted up to 30 days of paid leave for training or active duty deployments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program within the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to provide subsidies to individuals purchasing health coverage in the individual market in calendar years 2026 and 2027, mitigating the potential loss or reduction of federal advance premium tax credits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents purchasing health benefit plans through the individual health insurance market, particularly those facing reduced federal premium tax credits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: If federal advance premium tax credits are not extended for calendar years 2026 and 2027, special fund expenditures from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund increase by a significant but indeterminate amount (estimated up to $75.0 million in FY 2026, $150.0 million in FY 2027, and $75.0 million in FY 2028) to provide state subsidies. Administrative costs can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. If federal credits are extended, the bill terminates and no state expenditures are incurred. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) to establish, administer, and adopt regulations for the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program, as well as administer and expend from the MHBE Fund.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must be consulted by MHBE in establishing the program and setting its eligibility and payment parameters, and is tasked alongside MHBE with notifying the Department of Legislative Services if federal tax credits change.
The Comptroller accounts for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, the purposes and allowed uses of which are modified under this legislation.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the moneys of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, which is expanded to accommodate funding and disbursements for the new subsidy program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, through its workgroup on youth behavioral health, individuals with developmental disabilities, and individuals with complex behavioral health needs, to develop recommendations for implementing federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services best practices for Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) requirements for children. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Advisory Council, and Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid-eligible children and youth, particularly those with behavioral health conditions, complex needs, or developmental disabilities, along with their families, caregivers, and pediatric behavioral health providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The advisory council and commission can provide recommendations and the Maryland Department of Health can submit the required report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers Maryland's Medicaid program and Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) services, supports behavioral health policy, and is statutorily mandated to submit the final report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access (through its youth behavioral health workgroup) to convene stakeholders and formulate recommendations implementing CMS best practices for EPSDT requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill standardizes the tax treatment of real property owned by nonprofit entities established by public housing authorities across Maryland by expanding a property tax exemption statewide. Previously limited to Baltimore City, Howard County, and Montgomery County, qualifying property used for housing persons of eligible income is exempt from State and local property taxes, and the housing authority entities may make payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) to local jurisdictions pursuant to mutual agreements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Public Housing Authorities
qa_results.stakeholders: Public housing authorities, nonprofit housing entities, local governments, and individuals and families of eligible income seeking affordable housing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State and local property tax revenues may experience a potential minimal decrease to the extent that public housing authorities establish qualifying nonprofit entities. State and local expenditures are not significantly affected. Any revenue loss may also be partially offset by negotiated payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1085 amends the Housing and Community Development Article to extend property tax exemptions to nonprofit entities established by public housing authorities statewide, facilitating affordable housing financing mechanisms such as Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC). The Department of Housing and Community Development was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
As the State's chief tax collection and financial agency, the Comptroller is impacted by changes affecting State property tax revenues and was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), managed care organizations, and private health insurers from imposing time limits on coverage for anesthesia delivery when ordered by a licensed medical professional. Insurers and Medicaid must cover anesthesia for the full duration of the procedure as well as related care provided immediately before and after.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients undergoing procedures requiring anesthesia, healthcare providers and anesthesiologists, health insurance carriers, and Medicaid managed care organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but minimal amount starting in FY 2026 (funded 50% general funds and 50% federal funds), matched by an equivalent increase in federal fund revenues. No impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration, the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), requiring MDH to cover anesthesia without time limitations and resulting in an indeterminate but minimal fiscal impact on Medicaid expenditures.

The bill adds § 15–861 to the Insurance Article, establishing coverage requirements and prohibiting time limitations on anesthesia for private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs regulated by the Administration.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while evaluated for potential fiscal and coverage impacts relating to health plan mandates, the bill does not impact the State plan.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing step therapy or fail-first protocols on FDA-approved prescription drugs prescribed to treat symptoms or side effects of stage four advanced metastatic cancer, provided the treatment follows best practices, is supported by peer-reviewed literature, and is covered under the policy.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients diagnosed with stage four advanced metastatic cancer, treating physicians, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and pharmacy benefits managers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees, with reviews handled using existing resources. No anticipated impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, and minimal assumed impact on local governments with fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing the Insurance Article, reviewing carrier form and rate filings for compliance with the prohibition on step therapy protocols, and collecting associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and benefit design regarding prescription drug protocols.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees broad state health policies and programs and provided information on clinical standards and impacts related to cancer treatment protocols.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for a beauty salon alcoholic beverages license in Montgomery County to include licensed barbershops, renames it the beauty salon and barbershop beer, wine, and liquor license, allows licensees to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor, and increases the maximum amount of beer that may be provided to a customer for on-premises consumption from 5 to 12 ounces.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Beauty salon and barbershop owners, employees, and customers in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect. Montgomery County revenues are not affected, and any additional enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that eligibility for the license requires holding a barbershop or beauty salon permit issued under Titles 4 and 5 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which are licensed and regulated by boards under the Maryland Department of Labor.

The Comptroller serves as the state's principal alcohol regulator and tax collector; while licensing is administered locally by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners, the bill alters allowable alcoholic beverage service parameters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) to calculate and report risk-based capital levels, maintain total adjusted capital at or above company action level requirements beginning December 31, 2026, and adhere to prior approval ratemaking standards during specified periods. Additionally, directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to establish a workgroup to study private passenger automobile insurance affordability and excess insurer profits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), private passenger automobile insurance companies, insurance producers, and Maryland motor vehicle policyholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources with no impact on State general revenues. MAIF nonbudgeted revenues may be impacted if meeting risk-based capital thresholds requires reducing higher-yield equity investments in favor of lower-risk assets, which could affect investment income and potentially influence future industry assessments. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), requiring it to calculate and report risk-based capital (RBC) levels, maintain a specified total adjusted capital level, submit an RBC plan under certain conditions, and comply with prior approval rate-making provisions. Its Executive Director also serves on the study workgroup.

The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is tasked with reviewing and determining the adequacy of MAIF's RBC plans, overseeing prior approval rate filings, establishing and staffing a workgroup to study automobile insurance affordability, and having the Insurance Commissioner chair the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a specialized temporary workgroup tasked with studying the affordability of private passenger automobile insurance in Maryland and reporting findings and recommendations.
The workgroup established under the bill is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations regarding automobile insurance affordability to the Governor on or before January 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the Commission on Health Equity, to develop and maintain an easy-to-understand graphic data dashboard tracking age-adjusted health disparity data disaggregated by race, ethnicity, and gender across various health indicators, updated quarterly on its website.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents, public health researchers, healthcare policymakers, and demographic communities affected by health disparities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Department of Health can develop and update the dashboard using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to develop, maintain, quarterly update, and host a comprehensive health equity data dashboard on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop the graphic health equity data dashboard in collaboration with the Commission on Health Equity.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Population Health Improvement Fund jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission to invest in population health improvements and support health equity targets under the federal AHEAD Model. The bill permits the use of electronic health care transaction data for state participation in the model, authorizes a temporary hospital rate assessment through 2027 to finance the fund, and requires annual progress reporting.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, health care providers, electronic health networks, Medicaid beneficiaries, and Maryland residents receiving care under population health initiatives.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $25.0 million in FY 2026 from an HSCRC hospital rate assessment credited to the Population Health Improvement Fund, with indeterminate increases in FY 2027 and FY 2028 if assessments continue. State Medicaid expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2026 ($2.0 million in general funds and $3.0 million in federal matching funds) due to higher hospital rates. Minimal general fund revenue increase from interest earnings through FY 2028. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary executive department responsible for jointly administering the newly established Population Health Improvement Fund with the HSCRC, managing expenditures aligned with the Statewide Health Equity Plan, and submitting required annual reports to the General Assembly.

HSCRC is given direct authority to assess uniform amounts in hospital rates to fund the Population Health Improvement Fund, jointly administer the Fund with MDH, and provide monthly updates to designated General Assembly members.

The bill impacts MHCC's regulatory oversight and standards regarding electronic health networks and the State-designated health information exchange (CRISP), specifying that its regulations may not restrict State use of financial claims information for AHEAD Model purposes.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund separately and manage the investment of the Fund's balances.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established special, nonlapsing Population Health Improvement Fund.
The bill explicitly provides that the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum employment age from 16 to 18 years for alcoholic beverage license holders in Allegany County that do not derive more than half of their revenue from food sales, while maintaining the minimum age of 16 for establishments where food sales exceed 50% of revenue.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees in Allegany County and individuals aged 16 to 17 seeking employment at these establishments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Allegany County operations or finances. Any impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the legal minimum age of employment for certain alcoholic beverage license holders in Allegany County, touching on youth employment and labor standards enforced by the Department of Labor.
The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry, although day-to-day retail alcoholic beverage licensing and local enforcement in Allegany County are handled primarily at the local level.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility under Maryland's Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program to include solar energy generating systems located on or over industrial water retention ponds or quarries. It also authorizes Baltimore City and county or municipal governments to grant an optional property tax credit for nonresidential solar energy generating systems built on brownfields, industrial water retention ponds, or quarries.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresidential solar energy system developers and owners, owners of industrial brownfields, quarries, and water retention ponds, local governments, and electric utility customers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Public Service Commission, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that local governments elect to grant the optional property tax credit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission administers the Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program and is directly responsible for certifying eligible solar energy generating systems, which the bill expands to include systems located on or over certain water retention ponds or quarries.

The department regulates brownfields, industrial sites, and nontidal wetlands and waterways; its Water and Science Administration reviews and handles environmental approval processes for floating solar installations on water retention ponds and quarries.
MEA oversees the state's clean energy policies, solar incentive programs, and land assessment studies regarding solar siting on brownfields and industrial sites.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Youth Transitioning from Foster Placement to Successful Adulthood Program within the Child Care Scholarship Program, administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. The bill eliminates certain application barriers—such as work/training requirements, information on the other parent, and foster parent income documentation—and waives copayments to improve child care subsidy access for parenting foster youth ages 16 through 21.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Parenting foster youth (ages 16 to 21) in out-of-home care or who exited care at age 18, their children, and child care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $91,000 in FY 2026 for MSDE system reprogramming. Expenditures further increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 to provide child care scholarships without copays for newly eligible foster youth families (illustratively estimated at $355,680 annually if 30 families participate). No impact on state revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary administering agency responsible for operating the Child Care Scholarship Program, implementing the new Youth Transitioning From Foster Placement to Successful Adulthood Program, updating IT application portals, and awarding copay-free scholarships to eligible parenting foster youth.
DHS oversees the state's foster care and child welfare system and is statutorily mandated by the bill to make referrals of eligible parenting foster youth to MSDE for the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum number of members on the Office of Child Care Advisory Council from 30 to 31 and adds a representative from the Maryland Association of Public Library Administrators to the council.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Office of Child Care Advisory Council, the Maryland Association of Public Library Administrators, child care providers, and early childhood education advocates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Child Care Advisory Council advises the Early Childhood Development Division of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), and the State Superintendent is responsible for appointments to the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory membership and size of the Office of Child Care Advisory Council, an executive advisory board.

The Maryland State Library Agency oversees and coordinates the state's public library systems, which are directly represented by the addition of a representative of the Maryland Association of Public Library Administrators to the Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the medical and geriatric parole processes in Maryland. It requires the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) to consider an incarcerated individual's age and its effect on recidivism, alters criteria and evaluation procedures for medical parole, and repeals the Governor's authority to disapprove medical parole for individuals serving life sentences. It also establishes a standardized geriatric parole review process for incarcerated individuals who are at least 65 years old, have served at least 20 years, are not sex offenders, have parole-eligible sentences, and have no serious recent infractions. Additionally, it directs any incarceration savings to parole-related assessments and reentry services, and authorizes the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board to recommend distributing funds to MPC to hire psychologists for risk assessments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Parole-eligible incarcerated individuals (specifically individuals aged 65 and older and individuals with chronic debilitating or terminal medical conditions), victims and their representatives, and correctional system staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,494 in FY 2026 (reflecting the October 1, 2025 effective date) and rise to $654,500 by FY 2030, covering salaries and operating expenses for three psychologists and one administrative officer to conduct risk assessments and comply with reporting requirements. This estimate does not reflect potential savings in incarceration costs, which are indeterminate. To the extent funding is distributed to MPC from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund via GOCPP/JROB, the need for general funds would decrease. Local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the department and its Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) by altering the evaluation process and requirements for medical and geriatric parole, mandating ongoing identification and submission of eligible incarcerated individuals, requiring risk assessments and parole hearings, and regulating the use of departmental savings resulting from the Act.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP houses and supports the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB) and administers the Performance Incentive Grant Fund. The bill requires MPC to report annual geriatric parole outcomes to JROB and authorizes JROB to recommend distributing Justice Reinvestment Act savings to MPC for hiring psychologists.
The bill repeals the statutory authority of the Governor to disapprove a decision by the Maryland Parole Commission to grant medical parole to an incarcerated individual serving a life sentence.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB), an executive body, receives mandated annual outcome reporting on geriatric parole determinations and is authorized to recommend funding allocations from reinvestment savings to the Maryland Parole Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment, upon request from the Dorchester County government and its delegated approval authority, to establish a temporary privatization program for performing activities related to well and on-site sewage disposal (septic) system oversight, permitting, and inspections.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County property owners and residents, licensed environmental health specialists, private well and septic contractors, and the Dorchester County Health Department.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $96,043 in FY 2026, $84,500 in FY 2027, and $88,200 in FY 2028 for one contractual sanitarian to develop, audit, and oversee the program until its termination on June 30, 2028. State revenues are unaffected. Local expenditures and fee revenues for the Dorchester County Health Department may be affected depending on program specifics and workload shifts, but the exact fiscal effect cannot be determined in advance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to establish, oversee, regulate, and audit a privatization program for well and septic system activities in Dorchester County, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact on the agency.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees local health departments, and the Dorchester County Health Department serves as the delegated approval authority whose workflow, permitting review responsibilities, and fee collections are directly affected by the privatization program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the duties of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring to study and make recommendations on policies, practices, and responses regarding violations of home detention monitoring conditions. The bill also requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to annually collect and report detailed demographic and violation data regarding individuals on home detention monitoring to the workgroup by September 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals placed on home detention monitoring, private and public home detention monitoring agencies, law enforcement agencies, and the judiciary.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the data collection and reporting requirements using existing resources, with no effect on State revenues. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency; it provides staff support to the Workgroup, holds a membership seat (Secretary or designee), has its responses to violations studied, and is mandated to collect and report detailed annual home detention monitoring data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory study topics, data receipt responsibilities, and reporting mandates of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender of Maryland or their designee serves as a designated statutory member of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland appoints a representative of the Judiciary to the Workgroup, and data collected includes violations reported to judges.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several stakeholder representatives to the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Child Support Arrearage to Work Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Labor to connect individuals who are unemployed and behind on child support payments with employment opportunities, including jobs within State government.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (specifically the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning, in consultation with the Department of Human Services and the Department of Budget and Management)
qa_results.stakeholders: Unemployed individuals who are in arrears on child support obligations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor may increase by up to approximately $156,600 in FY 2026 only to hire two contractual staff members, depending on the scale of the pilot program. Existing budgeted resources will handle coordination among other agencies, and no material impact is expected on local government finances, small businesses, or the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Child Support Arrearage to Work Pilot Program directly within the Department of Labor, requiring it to lead implementation, establish data-sharing protocols, and submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill statutorily requires the Department of Labor to consult with the Department of Human Services, which oversees the Child Support Administration, to implement the pilot program and share child support data securely.

The Department of Budget and Management must be consulted on the program's implementation, particularly regarding the goal of connecting participants with State government employment opportunities given DBM's role as the state's central personnel agency.
The Department of Labor is required to submit a report on findings and recommendations concerning the pilot program to the Governor by July 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Buprenorphine Training Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to help counties offset the cost of training paramedics to administer buprenorphine, funded by a mandated annual appropriation of at least $50,000 from the Opioid Restitution Fund. The bill also directs the Maryland Office of Overdose Response to convene a stakeholder workgroup to study buprenorphine access and provider capacity across the State and report findings by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Office of Overdose Response
qa_results.stakeholders: County governments, local health departments, local behavioral health agencies, paramedics, emergency medical services personnel, and individuals with opioid use disorders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) increase by at least $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2031 due to the mandated appropriation for the grant program, with no net effect on total ORF spending because funds are redirected from other authorized uses. General fund expenditures increase by $56,066 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Office of Overdose Response to hire contractual staff for the workgroup and study. Local revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2027 as counties apply for and receive paramedic training grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Buprenorphine Training Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health, expands authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund administered by MDH, and requires MDH's Behavioral Health Administration and the Maryland Office of Overdose Response to participate in and staff the newly created workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves training paramedics to administer buprenorphine and mandates that MIEMSS be represented on the workgroup studying buprenorphine access and service delivery statewide.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary workgroup tasked with studying buprenorphine access, provider capacity, geographic service gaps, and funding feasibility across Maryland.

The bill requires the Governor to include an annual mandated appropriation of at least $50,000 from the Opioid Restitution Fund in the State budget bill, and requires the workgroup's final report to be submitted to the Governor.
DBM oversees the development of the annual State budget and is responsible for incorporating the bill's mandated annual appropriation from the Opioid Restitution Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to approve a change of location for a certain alcoholic beverages license if the license was originally issued within the same election district and has been at the same location for at least 10 years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and commercial businesses in Baltimore County seeking to change their operating locations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state effect, and the bill does not materially affect Baltimore County finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While the bill specifically alters rules administered at the local level by the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing within the broader statutory framework overseen by the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group within the Maryland Department of Health to evaluate the sufficiency of Medicaid payment rates and address challenges to accessing home- and community-based services, direct care workforce conditions, and related issues.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid beneficiaries receiving home- and community-based services, direct care workers, direct care provider associations, residential service agencies, and consumer advocacy organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact because the legislation generally codifies an advisory group required by federal rule (the 2024 Access Final Rule). Revenues are unaffected, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group within the Department of Health. The Deputy Secretary of Health Care Financing serves as chair, appoints members, and MDH is tasked with providing staff, technical, logistical, and data support, as well as managing the advisory group's website page and reports.
The Secretary of Labor (or the Secretary's designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory advisory body, the Maryland Interested Parties Advisory Group, to consult, study, and provide ongoing policy recommendations regarding Medicaid payment rate sufficiency and direct care workforce access.
The Advisory Group is required to submit an annual report detailing its activities and recommendations regarding Medicaid payment rates and workforce issues to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Collaborative to Improve Children's Oral Health Through School-Based Programs to study and make recommendations on enhancing children's oral health and access to dental services in school settings. The collaborative is required to submit an interim report by December 1, 2025, and a final report by October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland school children (especially underserved children and Medicaid recipients), school-based health centers, public schools, dental hygienists, dentists, and school nurses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $38,000 in FY 2026 and $16,700 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time contractual health policy analyst to staff the collaborative and produce the required reports. Collaborative member travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. State revenues and local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency; it is required to staff the Collaborative, its Secretary designates the chair and appoints several members, and it incurs general fund operational expenses to support the initiative.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes a new temporary advisory body, the Maryland Collaborative to Improve Children's Oral Health Through School-Based Programs, to study and issue interim and final recommendations.

The State Superintendent/Secretary of Education (or designee) serves as a member of the Collaborative, and the Collaborative's scope focuses on school health guidelines, school nurses, and dental health delivery in public school settings.
The newly established Collaborative is required to submit both an interim report and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the prohibition of individuals alleged to have assaulted or caused bodily injury to a public transit operator or passenger from using State public transit services or entering transit stations, subject to guidelines and an appeals process. It also requires the Maryland Transit Administration to convene a workgroup to establish a rider code of conduct and implement an internal safety program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: State public transit operators, transit passengers, and individuals accused of assault or bodily injury on public transit facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $18,800 in FY 2025 and by $131,200 in FY 2026 for consultant services to support the workgroup and develop the safety program and code of conduct; future staffing will use existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MTA is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing guidelines and appeals for excluding individuals who commit assault or bodily injury, convening a workgroup to develop a rider code of conduct, implementing an internal safety program, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.

MDOT is the parent agency of the MTA and administers the Transportation Trust Fund, which will incur expenditures of $18,800 in FY 2025 and $131,200 in FY 2026 to support consultant staffing and development of the safety program and code of conduct.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a specialized statutory workgroup convened by MTA to create a rider code of conduct, recommend safety policies and consequence structures, and submit a report to legislative committees.

The bill explicitly requires MTA to consult with the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA), an interstate compact entity, when convening the safety workgroup, and defines operators under transportation compacts as public transit operators.

USM institutions (such as the University of Maryland operating Shuttle-UM) provide public shuttle services that could fall under the bill's definition of State public transit service operated by another State agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes waiting periods in Baltimore County following the denial of an alcoholic beverages license application, prohibiting a new application for the same location for one year after a denial, and prohibiting the issuance of a license for that location for two years after a second denial.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants, business and commercial property owners in Baltimore County, and the local licensing board.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal effect and does not materially affect Baltimore County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary state entity charged with regulatory oversight of Maryland's alcohol industry. However, HB 1145 pertains specifically to retail licensing waiting periods administered locally by the Baltimore County Board of Liquor License Commissioners, having no direct operational or fiscal impact on the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill integrates the 9-8-8 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline into the Maryland Behavioral Health Crisis Response System, requiring each jurisdiction or region to maintain a State 9-8-8 Lifeline coordinating with the national network to provide crisis counseling, intervention, and referral services. It also expands requirements for evaluating service outcomes, requiring annual public reporting of crisis call metrics, mobile crisis team responses, crisis stabilization center usage, and law enforcement involvement beginning December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Behavioral Health Administration)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals experiencing mental health or behavioral health crises and their families, 9-8-8 lifeline operators, mobile crisis response teams, crisis stabilization centers, and local behavioral health authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $63,100 in FY 2026, and between $55,200 and $62,900 annually in FY 2027 through FY 2030, for the Maryland Department of Health to hire one part-time epidemiologist to oversee data systems, collection, and analysis for the annual report. State revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not expected to be affected, provided the reporting requirements align with existing local health department and behavioral health authority data collection practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (through the Behavioral Health Administration) oversees the Behavioral Health Crisis Response System and the 9-8-8 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. The bill directly alters system requirements, integration standards, and data collection and annual outcome reporting mandates, resulting in ongoing operational and general fund expenditure impacts for the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits insurers from refusing to issue a residential condominium unit insurance policy based solely on a prior lapse in coverage, provided the lapse occurred because the prior insurer withdrew from the market, lasted no more than 90 days, and the applicant satisfies documentation requirements, including an affidavit of no incurred losses during the lapse.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential condominium unit owners who experienced coverage lapses due to an insurer leaving the market, and insurers issuing residential condominium unit policies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Any impact on small business insurers is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance market and enforces provisions of the Insurance Article, including underwriting standards and prohibitions on unfair trade practices such as denying residential condominium unit insurance based on lapses in coverage.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Pet Policy Transparency Act requires landlords of residential rental property who own or operate five or more individual dwelling units in Maryland to disclose the property's pet policy. Landlords must provide a link to the pet policy on the property's website, if applicable, and provide a written copy or summary within any rental application form, outlining breed and weight limits, required fees and deposits, pet quantity limits, vaccination and insurance requirements, and any additional rules.
qa_results.responsible_party: Residential rental property landlords (with enforcement oversight under the Office of the Attorney General)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential rental property landlords owning or operating five or more dwelling units, prospective tenants, and pet-owning renters in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government finances or operations. The effect on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees and enforces statutory consumer protection and tenant disclosure requirements in residential leases and rental applications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a formal statutory definition of 'ecological restoration' within the Maryland Environment Article, defining it as an activity aimed at recovering, re-establishing, or enhancing a degraded, damaged, or destroyed ecosystem through physical, chemical, or biological improvements, restoring natural or historical functions, or improving resiliency.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Entities, organizations, and developers undertaking or permitting environmental and ecological restoration projects, conservationists, and regulatory agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to directly affect State or local finances or operations, with minimal or no effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a statutory definition of 'ecological restoration' to the Environment Article, implementing a key recommendation from the Maryland Department of the Environment's Ecological Restoration Permitting Study Report.

The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency managing state waterways, forests, and wildlife habitats, and collaborates closely with MDE on ecological restoration projects and permitting frameworks.

Maryland Environmental Service plans and implements environmental restoration, dredging, and habitat creation projects across the state, which are directly guided by statutory definitions and regulatory standards governing ecological restoration.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly selling or offering to sell heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, or refrigeration (HVACR) equipment unless the purchaser holds a specified license issued by the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, employs a licensed individual, operates a business reselling equipment to licensed individuals, or qualifies for an exemption. It also requires sellers to provide written notice regarding licensing requirements to purchasers and establishes civil penalties for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors
qa_results.stakeholders: HVACR contractors and technicians, HVACR equipment retailers and wholesalers, and consumers or businesses purchasing HVACR equipment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors can implement the requirements with existing resources. State General Fund revenues may minimally increase from civil penalties of up to $1,000 for a first violation and up to $5,000 for repeat violations. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor houses and oversees the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, which is tasked with adopting implementing regulations, prescribing required notice content for purchasers, and enforcing the equipment sales restrictions and civil penalties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the authority of municipal corporations and governed special taxing districts in Montgomery County to impose additional or stricter building requirements (such as setbacks, bulk, parking, and lot coverage) beyond county or regional standards. It allows these jurisdictions to regulate buildings with four or fewer dwelling units—including duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottage clusters, and townhouses—and accessory structures without regard to underlying zoning, provided requirements for buildings with two to four units are not more restrictive than those for single-unit houses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Legislative bodies of municipal corporations and governed special taxing districts within Montgomery County
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, residents, and construction/remodeling contractors and developers of small residential properties (up to four units) in Montgomery County municipalities and governed special taxing districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local government finances. It may have a meaningful impact on small businesses involved in the construction, repair, or remodeling of residential buildings with two to four dwelling units if local jurisdictions enact stricter requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Land Use Article regarding local municipal authority to impose building and zoning requirements on residential structures. As the State's principal agency for land use planning policy and technical guidance to local jurisdictions, the Maryland Department of Planning tracks and advises on local planning authorities and served as an information source for this bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill allows a corporation to transfer collateral assets securing a mortgage, pledge, or security interest without stockholder approval under certain circumstances, such as default enforcement by a secured party or an alternative sale reducing secured debt when the asset's value is less than or equal to the debt. It also eliminates requirements to report specific percentages and classes of partnership or membership interests in articles of merger involving limited partnerships, limited liability companies, or general partnerships.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs), limited partnerships, partnerships, corporate directors, stockholders, and secured creditors/lenders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It may potentially have a meaningful impact on small businesses by streamlining asset transfers and corporate merger filings.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1172 requires the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to charge a fee of up to $250 for expedited processing of Class C per diem license applications submitted less than two weeks prior to an event, and authorizes the Board to regulate, deny, revoke, or limit such licenses. The bill also authorizes the issuance of specific Class B and Class C alcoholic beverages licenses at designated locations in the 40th alcoholic beverages district under certain conditions, establishes daily sales hour restrictions for specified areas within the 40th district, and exempts Class M-F (municipal family fun center) licenses from certain hour restrictions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants, event organizers seeking per diem licenses, designated businesses and venues in Baltimore City's 40th legislative district (including restaurants, campus event venues, and barbershops), neighborhood community associations, and local patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues will increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that new alcoholic beverage licenses are issued and expedited application processing fees of up to $250 are collected. Specific dollar totals are unavailable. Baltimore City expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C beer and light wine license for on-campus events in the 2500 block of West North Avenue, which is the campus location of Coppin State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland.

The Comptroller is responsible for regulating Maryland's alcohol industry and collecting state alcoholic beverage taxes, although primary administration and licensing under this bill is carried out locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the placement and operation of speed monitoring systems on highways in Montgomery County identified in Strategic Highway Safety Plans or Vision Zero Plans as high-risk for severe or fatal crashes, while prohibiting their use on controlled access highways, expressways, and interstates. The bill also dedicates net revenues from these systems to safety-related roadway projects and requires system evaluations every five years.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers, pedestrians, Montgomery County government, and municipal governments within Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by approximately $12,208 in FY 2026 for District Court computer programming changes, with minimal potential revenue increases from contested citations. Local government revenues and expenditures in Montgomery County may increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 depending on the number of speed monitoring systems deployed; excess fine revenues after cost recovery must be spent on road safety projects on high-risk roadways.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The District Court of Maryland (supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts) is responsible for prescribing uniform citation forms, processing fine payments, and adjudicating contested citations resulting from newly authorized speed monitoring systems, with an estimated programming cost of $12,208 in FY 2026.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding speed monitoring on highways and safety-related projects, which directly intersects with MDOT's oversight of statewide transportation infrastructure and traffic safety planning.

The MVA houses the Maryland Highway Safety Office (MHSO), which develops and administers the State's Strategic Highway Safety Plan and Vision Zero program—the exact plans the bill uses to qualify high-risk roadways eligible for speed camera placement.

SHA partners closely with MHSO to implement traffic safety plans and policies, maintains state non-toll roadways, establishes traffic control device standards, and may be involved in the design or coordination of safety-related roadway projects funded by fine revenues.
The Comptroller receives and deposits into the General Fund any excess fine revenues remitted by political subdivisions if net speed monitoring revenues exceed 10% of total local revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permits an individual or entity in Montgomery County to hold up to two Class BD-BWL alcoholic beverages licenses, an increase from the previous limit of one. For an establishment operating under a second Class BD-BWL license, average daily receipts from food sales must exceed average daily receipts from alcohol sales, and off-premises sales are restricted to private-label products manufactured exclusively for the license holder.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and prospective Class BD-BWL alcoholic beverages license holders and restaurant and bar owners in Montgomery County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Montgomery County revenues will increase depending on how many licensees obtain a second Class BD-BWL license ($3,500 annual fee, $600 initial application fee, and $100 annual renewal fee). For illustrative purposes, if all 52 existing licensees apply for and maintain a second license, county revenues would increase by $213,200 in fiscal 2026 and by $187,200 annually thereafter. Montgomery County can handle any additional enforcement activities with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and collecting state excise and sales taxes on alcoholic beverages. While this bill specifically addresses local Class BD-BWL retail licensing limits administered by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to alcohol regulation under the Comptroller's broader industry purview.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes statutory factors for courts to consider when determining legal and physical custody in the best interest of a child. It requires courts to articulate their findings of fact on the record or in a written opinion and authorizes courts to modify child custody or visitation orders upon a material change in circumstances.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Parents and children involved in legal and physical child custody and visitation proceedings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs judicial determinations in child custody and visitation proceedings by establishing statutory factors judges must consider and requiring courts to articulate findings of fact on the record or in a written opinion.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Housing Data Transparency Act requires counties with at least 150,000 residents that issue at least 50 residential building permits annually to submit quarterly reports to the Maryland Department of Planning on residential building and development permits.
