qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $44,844 in FY 2026 only for one-time costs incurred by the Judiciary to update juror qualification forms and develop reporting systems. Local expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for local governments that construct or undergo major renovations of circuit courthouses to add compliant lactation rooms. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by altering juror excusal criteria, mandating annual data collection and reporting on jury excusals to the General Assembly, and requiring circuit courthouses to provide lactation rooms. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs one-time general fund expenditures of $44,844 in FY 2026 to update juror qualification forms and develop reporting systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the reporting requirements for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland's annual report on Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs (TRPPs) to require details on the number of TRPPs established in the State, the number of participants, participant outcomes, and recommendations to improve program function.
qa_results.responsible_party: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland (Maryland Judiciary)
qa_results.stakeholders: Juveniles and students participating in Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs, public school systems, and juvenile courts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Judiciary can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, assuming current internal data collection suffices. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the reporting requirements for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland regarding Truancy Reduction Pilot Programs. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and technological support to the Judicial Branch and maintains the case management data necessary to compile and submit the required report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to grant hiring and promotion preferences to eligible veterans, spouses of eligible active-duty service members, spouses of disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of deceased veterans, including the option to adopt local laws awarding credit points on selection tests.
qa_results.responsible_party: County and municipal governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible veterans, spouses of active-duty service members, spouses of veterans with service-connected disabilities, surviving spouses of deceased veterans, and county and municipal governments and job applicants.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact because the bill applies only to local governments. There is no direct local fiscal impact, as the bill is authorizing in nature and discretionary preferences or test credits do not directly affect local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly addresses hiring and promotion preferences and test credits for veterans, active-duty spouses, and surviving spouses, which directly aligns with the department's core mission to advocate for and support veterans and military families in Maryland.
The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article (§ 3-714) to clarify the definition of employer to include counties and municipalities regarding permissible hiring and promotion preferences.

The bill includes a specific safe harbor provision clarifying that granting veteran and military spouse hiring or promotion preferences does not violate State or local equal employment opportunity laws enforced by the Commission.

The legislation references and mirrors the State Personnel Management System's selection test credit provisions (under the State Personnel and Pensions Article) administered by DBM, though the bill's authority applies to local governments.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the Maryland Small Business Innovation Research and Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) Incentive Program by removing statutory limits on award and investment amounts, as well as the maximum caps on the number of Phase I and Phase II awards granted each fiscal year. Businesses remain limited to receiving no more than one award or investment per fiscal year and a maximum of three total awards or investments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland small businesses engaged in research and development that apply for or receive federal SBIR or STTR awards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect overall State revenues or expenditures, as TEDCO can implement the changes with existing budgeted resources. In the fiscal 2026 budget, $1.33 million is included for program awards and investments and $0.5 million for technical assistance. The bill may reallocate funding among eligible small business recipients, and general fund expenditures could increase in future years if funding expectations rise. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1450 directly amends the Maryland Small Business Innovation Research and Technology Transfer Incentive Program, which is established under the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) and administered by the Corporation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Program by restructuring the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board's membership, barring General Assembly members from serving on the board, updating the purpose of the Senator George C. Edwards Fund to focus on job creation and economic development opportunities, and revising the criteria required for projects to qualify for grant and loan funding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board and the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Western Maryland local governments, economic development entities, businesses, and residents in Districts 1 and 2 seeking grant and loan funding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not alter State funding for the program and does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. The mandated annual appropriation of $10,000,000 remains through fiscal year 2026 under existing law, and funding beyond fiscal 2026 remains discretionary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition, voting procedures, and project evaluation and grant-awarding criteria of the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board.

The bill removes the statutory requirement for a representative from the Department of Commerce, appointed by the Secretary of Commerce, to serve on the Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes an optional alternative registration process for owners of fleets of five or more rental vehicles, requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue distinctive 'Fleet Vehicle' registration plates and align fleet registration expiration dates without requiring validation tabs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Rental vehicle fleet owners and rental car businesses with fleets of five or more vehicles
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues increase by $208,000 in FY 2026, $277,300 in FY 2027, and $69,300 in FY 2028 from the one-time $8.50 registration plate fee. TTF expenditures increase by $293,600 in FY 2026, $411,100 in FY 2027, and $107,900 in FY 2028 to produce and mail the new distinctive registration plates. Revenues and expenditures are not materially affected after FY 2028 once the existing eligible fleet is fully registered. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration establish an alternative registration process for rental fleet vehicles, issue distinctive 'Fleet Vehicle' registration plates, eliminate validation tab requirements for these vehicles, and collect a one-time initial registration fee.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will experience fiscal impacts in the form of increased revenues from new registration fees and increased expenditures to produce and mail the new license plates.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) to establish an installment payment plan program for individuals who accumulate at least $300 in unpaid video tolls and associated civil penalties. It authorizes MDTA to refer unpaid accounts to the Central Collection Unit (CCU) if an individual fails to make payments according to their plan, and it expands MDTA's authority to recall delinquent accounts from CCU under specific conditions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners with at least $300 in outstanding unpaid video tolls and civil penalties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local operations or finances. MDTA was already in the process of implementing a similar installment payment plan program and does not plan to alter its delinquent debt recall practices despite the expanded authority under the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDTA is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing and administering the installment payment plan program for unpaid video tolls and civil penalties, adopting implementing regulations, and managing account referrals to and recalls from the Central Collection Unit.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU) is housed within DBM; the bill alters criteria under which MDTA refers unpaid video tolls and penalties to CCU and expands MDTA's authority to recall delinquent accounts from CCU.
MDTA notifies the Administration (MVA) when an individual fails to pay in accordance with an approved installment payment plan, which prompts MVA to refuse or suspend the vehicle's registration.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and coordinates closely with MDTA on transportation operations and toll enforcement procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a statewide policy promoting the creation of accessory dwelling units (ADUs) on land with a single-family detached dwelling unit as the primary dwelling. The bill mandates that local legislative bodies adopt local laws by October 1, 2026, authorizing ADU development under specified conditions; voids private deed restrictions, covenants, or homeowners association (HOA) rules that unreasonably limit ADU development or rental; and allows HOAs to treat ADUs as separate lots for voting and assessment purposes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local legislative bodies (county and municipal governing bodies)
qa_results.stakeholders: Single-family detached residential property owners, tenants and individuals seeking housing, homeowners associations (HOAs), residential building contractors, and local planning and zoning authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be directly affected. Local government finances may experience indeterminate impacts: expenditures may increase for drafting and adopting local ADU laws, conducting required parking studies, and processing development reviews and approvals, offset by potential increases in local permitting and application fee revenues. The net direct local fiscal impact cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly exempts historic properties listed in or determined eligible by the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is a unit within the Department of Planning. Additionally, the department provides comprehensive land use planning policy guidance and technical assistance to local jurisdictions implementing state land use mandates.

The bill establishes state policy to encourage the creation of accessory dwelling units to meet statewide housing needs and expand rental housing opportunities, which aligns directly with the department's core mission of promoting affordable and accessible housing options.

The bill modifies the Maryland Homeowners Association Act and places restrictions on private covenants and deed restrictions, which falls within the regulatory and consumer protection interest of the Attorney General's Office regarding homeowners associations and real property law enforcement.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies laws governing special taxing districts for erosion prevention and control projects. In Anne Arundel County, it exempts the planning, permitting, cost estimation, and construction of erosion control projects from the requirement of a 75% property owner petition, as well as the requirement for public notice and hearings prior to proceeding. Statewide, it requires interest earned on deposited district funds to be credited to that district and authorizes entities administering shore erosion control districts to use tax funds for the maintenance, repair, or restoration of existing projects after a public hearing, without requiring a property owner petition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Council and county governing bodies serving as district councils for special taxing and assessment districts
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners within shoreline subdivisions and special taxing districts, local county governments (particularly Anne Arundel County), and small businesses contracted for shoreline erosion planning, maintenance, and construction
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Locally, the bill may accelerate and/or increase expenditures and revenues for erosion prevention or control districts in Anne Arundel County by removing petition, notice, and hearing requirements that could otherwise delay or block projects. Additionally, shore erosion control districts statewide may experience increased utilization of district tax funds for maintenance and repair of existing projects. Crediting interest earnings directly to districts is not expected to materially alter local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1467 modifies provisions in the Local Government Article that specifically supplement the Natural Resources Article regarding shore erosion control projects. The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) administers the state's shore erosion control program, reviews and recommends shore erosion control districts, and provides financing/loans for erosion control projects maintained and repaired by these local taxing districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Prince George’s County Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement to record a lien within 90 days of issuing a notice of violation for cutting or clearing trees in the Critical Area on non-commercial parcels under five acres in order to hold a subsequent property owner liable. It also retroactively vacates enforcement actions and requires the county to reimburse a current property owner who purchased a property in good faith for costs and fees related to violations committed by a prior owner on or before November 7, 2018.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement (DPIE)
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County property owners of non-commercial parcels of less than five acres in the Critical Area who purchased property in good faith after a prior owner's tree-clearing violation, as well as Prince George's County local government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Prince George's County expenditures increase by approximately $40,000 in FY 2026 only to reimburse a current property owner for costs and fees associated with past administrative enforcement actions. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 8–1815.1 of the Natural Resources Article governing the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program, which is overseen by the Critical Area Commission housed within the Department of Natural Resources, and involves forest mitigation plans and penalties paid to the Department.

The underlying statute (§ 8–1815.1) authorizes the Critical Area Commission to refer tree-clearing violations to the Office of the Attorney General to initiate enforcement actions and seek statutory remedies in court.
The bill involves the recording and enforcement of property liens and legal remedies for Critical Area violations that may be adjudicated through the circuit courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1473 expands Maryland's equal access requirements for public services to include individuals with disabilities in addition to individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP). It requires designated State departments, agencies, and programs to develop, implement, and update biennial language access plans, translate vital documents, and provide necessary oral, written, and sign language assistance services. The bill also establishes the Maryland Language Advisory Group, co-chaired and staffed by the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs and the Maryland Department of Disabilities, to provide guidance, develop templates, review compliance, and submit annual reports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs and the Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with limited English proficiency, individuals with disabilities requiring language assistance or alternative communication formats, and Maryland State agencies and staff providing public services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs increase by $55,991 in FY 2026 to hire a part-time director to support the Maryland Language Advisory Group. Beginning in FY 2027, State expenditures across affected agencies are expected to increase significantly and exceed $1.5 million annually to implement language access plans and provide translation and interpretation services. The Department of Human Services may see an increase in matching federal fund revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Co-convenes, co-chairs, and shares staffing responsibilities for the newly created Maryland Language Advisory Group, and is required to develop and implement expanded language access plans for individuals with disabilities.

Houses the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs, which co-convenes, co-chairs, and staffs the Maryland Language Advisory Group, receiving an explicit fiscal impact of $56,000 in FY 2026 and ongoing operational funding.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (or designee) is statutorily designated as a member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a member of the Advisory Group; MSDE is specifically required to fully implement language access provisions and anticipates up to $125,000 annually for translation services.

The Secretary of Human Services is a member of the Advisory Group and collaborates with the Attorney General to identify independent agencies subject to the law; DHS projects over $250,000 in system and translation costs.
The Secretary of Health is designated as a member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and MDH is subject to the expanded language access mandates as a principal department.
The Secretary of Labor is designated as a member of the Maryland Language Advisory Group, and the department is subject to the language access plan requirements.
The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the Advisory Group, and DoIT anticipates ongoing expenditures of $50,000 annually for translation services.

Explicitly required to implement language access plans, collaborates with DHS to designate five independent entities subject to the law, and anticipates at least $25,000 annually in translation costs.
Specifically mandated to fully implement the language access requirements by July 1, 2028, and projects needing up to five administrative staff plus significant annual translation and website costs.
Explicitly named in statute as one of the agencies required to fully implement the expanded language access requirements by July 1, 2028.
Specifically named as required to achieve full compliance with language access requirements by July 1, 2028, with potentially significant translation costs.
Specifically listed in statute to fully implement language access plans and reporting requirements by July 1, 2028.
Specifically listed as an agency required to fully implement the bill's language access provisions by July 1, 2028, anticipating contractual and translation specialist costs.
As a principal department and the parent agency of MTA and MVA, MDOT is subject to implementation requirements, with costs supported through the Transportation Trust Fund.

As a primary public-facing administration under MDOT analyzed in the fiscal note, MVA will need to adapt its extensive public testing, vital documents, and language access plans to comply with the bill.

As a principal department, MDoA must comply with language access requirements and notes contractual costs over two years to develop, implement, and update its language access plan and translated vital documents.
Subject to full implementation by July 1, 2028 as a principal department; expects $14,000 annually in translation procurement plus $28,000 in FY 2028 for equipment.
Required to implement expanded language access plans and notes potential needs for additional staff and translation services beyond Spanish.
Subject to the requirements as a principal department, anticipating potential needs for administrative staff and translation services.
Subject to the requirements as a principal department, projecting potential need for additional staff to assist with vital document translations and interpretive services for public meetings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Maryland Language Advisory Group (MLAG) as an interagency advisory body charged with oversight, policy development, and reporting.
As a principal department, DBM is subject to the language access mandate and served as an information source during the bill's fiscal evaluation.
Coordinates executive branch community initiatives and outreach to immigrant and ethnic communities closely tied to the Governor's Office of Immigrant Affairs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a nonrenewable, six-month temporary telehealth license issued by the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists. The license authorizes qualifying out-of-state licensed professional counselors to provide telehealth counseling services in Maryland exclusively to out-of-state students attending and residing at or near a Maryland institution of higher education, provided they have a pre-existing therapeutic relationship of at least six months.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state college students enrolled at Maryland higher education institutions and out-of-state licensed professional counselors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as any additional workload on the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Any revenue impact from temporary telehealth license application fees is assumed to be minimal. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, with creating and administering a new temporary telehealth license, adopting regulations, and establishing application fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to convene a workgroup to analyze the mixed-delivery, publicly funded prekindergarten system established under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. The workgroup must solicit feedback from public, private, and non-participating child care providers and submit an interim report by June 1, 2026, and a final report by December 31, 2027, with recommendations to improve the program's equity and efficacy.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and private prekindergarten providers, child care centers and family child care providers, prekindergarten students (including students with disabilities), and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MSDE can convene and staff the workgroup with existing resources, although resources may temporarily be diverted from other projects. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for convening and staffing the workgroup, leading the comprehensive analysis of the mixed delivery prekindergarten system, and submitting the interim and final reports to the General Assembly and AIB.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary advisory workgroup comprised of legislators, agency representatives, educators, and child care providers to study the mixed delivery prekindergarten model and report its findings and recommendations.
MDH is mandated to designate at least one representative to serve as a member of the workgroup examining the publicly funded prekindergarten mixed delivery system.
The Office of the State Fire Marshal, an agency within the Department of State Police, is required to designate a representative to serve on the prekindergarten mixed delivery workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to study and submit a report by December 31, 2025, on the feasibility of establishing and maintaining an online directory of home health care providers in the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Home health care providers, residential service agencies, health care workers, and Maryland residents seeking home health care services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Department of Aging can conduct the study and complete the report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1478 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to study and submit a report to the General Assembly by December 31, 2025, on the feasibility of establishing and maintaining an online directory of home health care providers.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Maryland Department of Aging in conducting the feasibility study and preparing the report.
The bill requires the feasibility report to include a review of existing home health care consumer resources and service programs currently available through the Maryland Health Care Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Adapted Vehicle Access Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Disabilities to provide adapted motor vehicles to licensed, qualified drivers who require mobility aids and do not qualify for other department vehicle programs, giving priority to those in areas with limited access to public transportation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals who require a mobility aid, are licensed and qualified to drive an adapted vehicle, and do not qualify for other state adapted vehicle programs, especially those residing in areas with limited public transit.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can likely be absorbed within existing budgeted resources through the Assistive Technology Guaranteed Loan Program. If federal grants, corporate donations, or individual contributions are received, federal and special fund revenues and expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount from FY 2026 through FY 2030. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Disabilities is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing, administering, and operating the Adapted Vehicle Access Pilot Program, facilitating donations and grants, conducting an impact study, and submitting the required report.
The Department of Disabilities is statutorily required to submit a comprehensive report on the pilot program to the Governor on or before December 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class MT (movie theater) beer, wine, and liquor license in Howard County, allowing qualifying movie theater owners who hold crowd control training certification to sell alcoholic beverages to ticket-holding patrons for on-premises consumption.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County movie theater owners, movie theater patrons, and Howard County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. Howard County license fee revenues will increase depending on the annual license fee set by the board and the number of licenses issued, which cannot be reliably estimated. Howard County can handle any enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new local Class MT (movie theater) alcoholic beverages license in Howard County administered by the local Board of License Commissioners. While the fiscal note indicates no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland is the principal tax collector and regulatory body for the state's broader alcohol industry and sales tax collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames Baltimore City's AIDS Prevention Sterile Needle and Syringe Exchange Pilot Program to the HIV Prevention Syringe Services Program and updates its operating procedures, data collection, and evaluation requirements. The bill also alters the composition and duties of the program's oversight committee, allows syringe distribution and exchange via mobile sites as needed, and repeals certain limitations on criminal immunity regarding paraphernalia for program staff and participants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Health Department
qa_results.stakeholders: People who inject drugs in Baltimore City, Baltimore City Health Department staff, program participants, addiction treatment providers, and public health advocates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The legislation primarily updates statutory terminology, modernizes requirements, and adjusts program oversight and data collection procedures without requiring additional expenditures or generating new revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates one representative from the Maryland Department of Health to serve on the Baltimore City Syringe Services Program oversight committee and requires the program to send returned needles and syringes to the Rapid Analysis of Drugs Program operated by MDH's Center for Harm Reduction.
The Baltimore City Health Department is required to submit an annual report to the Governor by December 31 detailing the number of hypodermic needles and syringes exchanged under the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the statutory requirement that the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services nominate the law enforcement representative to the program's oversight committee.
The bill removes the Department of Juvenile Services from the pool of state agencies eligible to fill designated state seats on the program's oversight committee.
The bill removes the Maryland State Department of Education from the list of agencies eligible to be represented on the program's oversight committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes paid family and medical leave (PFML) benefits for all Executive Branch state employees, including temporary workers, allowing them to take up to 12 weeks (and up to 24 weeks under specific circumstances) of fully paid leave. It permits the State to self-insure rather than participate in the public Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) system, repeals the State's existing paid parental leave program, and requires the Department of Budget and Management and public higher education institutions to adopt regulations to administer the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management and governing bodies of public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch state employees (including temporary workers), state agencies, and public institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (all funds) decrease significantly in FY 2026 due to the State not paying FAMLI employer contributions, with annual cost savings potentially exceeding $35 million across all funds (including nearly $12 million in general funds). FAMLI Fund special fund revenues decrease by twice that amount due to foregone employer and employee contributions. Beginning in FY 2027, FAMLI contribution savings continue, but State expenditures increase to provide fully paid leave and administer the program (including contracting a third-party administrator and hiring additional staff); the net expenditure impact is indeterminate. FAMLI special fund expenditures also decrease beginning in FY 2027 from not paying FAMLI benefits to State employees. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the sponsor and primary administering agency of this departmental bill. The Secretary of Budget and Management is required to adopt regulations establishing conditions and procedures for Executive Branch employees to request and receive paid family and medical leave benefits.

The Maryland Department of Labor administers the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. Under the bill, quarterly wage and hour reports must be submitted to MD Labor, appeals of leave denials follow procedures established by the Secretary of Labor, and the FAMLI special fund experiences significant revenue reductions due to the State self-insuring.
The bill explicitly mandates that the governing body of a public institution of higher education adopt regulations governing paid family and medical leave benefits for its employees.

As an independent public institution of higher education in the Executive Branch governed by its own Board of Regents, Morgan State University is specifically required to adopt regulations governing paid family and medical leave benefits for its personnel.

As an independent public honors college governed by its own board, St. Mary's College of Maryland is required by the bill to adopt regulations governing paid family and medical leave benefits for its employees.
MDOT operates an independent personnel system within the Executive Branch covered by the bill's provisions and provided information for the fiscal analysis regarding operational and staffing impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes health care providers to send notice of the destruction of medical records or laboratory and X-ray reports by either first-class mail or email, rather than requiring both methods. If email notice is sent and no response or delivery receipt is received, the provider must send notice by first-class mail at least 10 days prior to the destruction date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, health care facilities, and patients (or their parents and guardians) whose medical records are scheduled to be destroyed.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the change is procedural and does not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures. Small business health care practices may experience minimal administrative impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1510 amends the Health - General Article regarding the statutory requirements health care providers must follow when providing notice before destroying medical records, laboratory reports, or X-ray reports. The Maryland Department of Health regulates health care professionals and facilities, oversees compliance with health standards under this article, and served as the informational source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain trusts—specifically passive trusts that acquire or are assigned mortgage loans and trusts established by federal corporate instrumentalities—from State mortgage lender licensing requirements. It also creates the Maryland Licensing Workgroup to review financial services licensing requirements and make recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Passive trusts, mortgage lenders, secondary mortgage market participants, financial service providers, and Maryland mortgage borrowers and consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) will experience an indeterminate impact due to foregone licensing fees and regulatory costs that would have otherwise occurred to license and examine passive trusts under a 2024 appellate court decision. OFR can staff the workgroup and absorb minimal member travel reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies licensing requirements under the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law administered by the Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation (OFR). Additionally, the Commissioner of Financial Regulation chairs the newly established Maryland Licensing Workgroup, and OFR is tasked with providing staff support for the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Maryland Licensing Workgroup, a temporary statutory advisory body established to study financial services licensing statutes and submit findings and recommendations by December 31, 2025, terminating in June 2026.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the Maryland Licensing Workgroup and will receive the workgroup's final report on findings and recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and appointing members to state task forces and workgroups, which includes the two gubernatorial appointments to the Maryland Licensing Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Amends prior authorizations of Maryland State debt across several previous capital budgets by altering grant purposes, changing grantee names, extending deadlines to expend or encumber funds, and eliminating certain matching fund requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Capital grant recipients, non-profit organizations, healthcare systems, educational institutions, local governments, and communities receiving state capital grant funding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the bill modifies the terms, allocations, and deadlines of previously authorized State debt rather than creating new debt authorizations. There is no local fiscal impact unless the grantee receiving or altering grant funds is a local government.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends and extends multiple prior state debt authorizations for capital projects at the University of Maryland, College Park, specifically for the Health and Human Sciences Building in Cole Field House.

DGS serves as the state's primary operational support agency overseeing state capital projects and administering legislative bond initiatives and miscellaneous capital grants authorized through state debt.
The bill amends specific capital grant authorizations and reallocations under the Department of Housing and Community Development's Division of Neighborhood Revitalization.
The bill creates a direct capital grant to the Department of Veterans and Military Families for improvements to the Historic White House at Charlotte Hall Veterans Home.
The Board of Public Works oversees and certifies matching fund requirements, approves state grant agreements, and monitors the expenditure and encumbrance of state debt authorizations.
The bill modifies a project authorization administered under the Department of Natural Resources Capital Grants and Loans Administration.
DBM assists in supervising capital budget execution, state debt tracking, and fiscal planning for state-funded capital grant programs.
The State Treasurer manages the issuance and servicing of state general obligation debt and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees these capital grant authorizations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the election structure of the Wicomico County Board of Education beginning in the 2026 general election by electing all seven voting members from seven councilmanic districts rather than five districts and two at-large. It also adds at least one nonvoting student member to the board, authorizes the board to award student scholarships and reimburse expenses, and allows the Wicomico County Council to set salaries for elected members higher than existing statutory minimums.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Wicomico County public school students, Wicomico County Board of Education members, and Wicomico County voters and residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Locally, Wicomico County Board of Education expenditures may increase if the Wicomico County Council chooses to set elected board member salaries above the statutory minimums ($4,000 for the chair and $3,700 for other members) or if the board awards scholarships to student members. Member expense reimbursements and election adjustments by the local board of elections are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the composition, election structure, student membership, and compensation for the Wicomico County Board of Education, one of the 24 local school systems overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill alters the election structure of the Wicomico County Board of Education starting with the 2026 election, shifting from five district members and two at-large members to seven district members, which impacts ballot configuration and election administration overseen by the State Board of Elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain competitively awarded Class B sports wagering facility licensees originally licensed on or before September 30, 2023, to submit a written request to relocate their sports wagering facility to a new location within the same county, subject to statutory location restrictions and approval by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B sports wagering facility licensees seeking relocation, commercial gaming operators, and sports wagering patrons in affected counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State revenues. The State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission can process and approve any relocation requests using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (part of the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency) with receiving, reviewing, and granting written requests from certain Class B sports wagering facility licensees to relocate their facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires that any proposed new location for a Class B sports wagering facility must be approved by the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), a statutory independent commission tasked with evaluating sports wagering licenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires applicants for barber, cosmetologist, and related limited licenses to complete at least one hour of approved domestic violence awareness training in person or virtually as a qualification for licensure. Current license holders must also complete the one-hour training once as a condition for their next license renewal, and the Maryland Department of Labor is tasked with approving qualifying training programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (State Board of Barbers and State Board of Cosmetologists)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed barbers, cosmetologists, estheticians, hairstylists, nail technicians, applicants for these licenses, and their clients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the State Barbers and Cosmetologists Boards' Fund increase by approximately $10,000 in FY 2026 for computer system reprogramming. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses both the State Board of Barbers and the State Board of Cosmetologists. The bill requires the Department to approve domestic violence awareness training programs and implement the one-hour training requirement for initial licensure and license renewals, resulting in an estimated $10,000 IT reprogramming expenditure.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires private nonprofit institutions of higher education to submit semi-annual letters of intent to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) outlining intended graduate-level programs, aligning their process with public four-year institutions. It repeals a provision that granted five public institutions exclusive 90-day authority to propose emerging workforce need programs, placing all institutions on equal footing. It also clarifies that letters of intent do not grant a right of first refusal, eliminates the mandate that MHEC circulate all letters across all institutions, and permits MHEC to notify only institutions proposing similar programs to facilitate collaboration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public senior institutions of higher education, private nonprofit colleges and universities in Maryland, and prospective graduate students.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the changes and handle the additional letters of intent using existing resources. Higher education revenues and expenditures for public four-year institutions are not expected to be materially impacted because the repealed exclusive authority provisions were never implemented; any potential broader financial impact cannot be reliably estimated. The bill has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and implementing body for the bill, tasked with administering the academic program approval process, receiving and reviewing semi-annual letters of intent for graduate programs from both public and private institutions, providing feedback to avoid duplication, and updating the State Plan for Higher Education.

Duplicate listing for MHEC, which serves as the primary agency responsible for reviewing letters of intent, coordinating academic program approvals, and maintaining the State Plan for Higher Education.

USM and its constituent member institutions (including Bowie State University, Coppin State University, UMCP, and UMES) are directly affected by the repeal of the 90-day exclusive authority to propose emerging workforce need programs, and are subject to the revised letter of intent and academic program approval procedures.

Morgan State University is directly impacted as one of the specified institutions whose 90-day exclusive authority to propose emerging workforce need programs is repealed, and it must comply with MHEC's graduate academic program approval and semi-annual letter of intent requirements.

As an independent public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is subject to MHEC's academic program approval requirements and semi-annual letter of intent submissions for intended graduate programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes expedited proceedings in tenant holding over actions for active duty U.S. military service members or their spouses who relocate to Maryland and intend to occupy the property. Under the bill, the District Court must order the tenant to appear within 45 days of the complaint, and authorizes service of summons by a private process server if a county sheriff or constable fails to serve it within 10 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Active duty U.S. military service members and their spouses who own residential rental property in Maryland, holdover tenants residing in those properties, county sheriffs and constables, and private process servers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations and scheduling of the District Court by requiring an expedited hearing within 45 days of a tenant holding over complaint when filed by an active duty service member, and modifies summons procedures.

The bill establishes legal protections and expedited real property repossession procedures specifically for active duty military service members and their families relocating to Maryland, which aligns with the department's mission to support active-duty service members and their families.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters procedures governing wrongful detainer actions by requiring the District Court to hold a show-cause hearing within 10 business days after a complaint is filed. It also modifies service of process requirements when an occupant cannot be found after two good faith efforts on separate days, requiring an affidavit of efforts, service by both certified and first-class mail, and conspicuous posting on the property within four business days of filing.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners claiming possession of real property, individuals occupying real property without legal right (wrongful detainers), process servers, and county sheriffs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Any impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 46 establishes strict statutory timelines and procedural requirements for wrongful detainer actions in the District Court and Circuit Court. It mandates that hearings occur within 10 business days after a complaint is filed, sets requirements for service of process affidavits and default judgments, and expedites the timeline for appeals. As the central administrative agency for the Maryland Judiciary, AOC is responsible for implementing the necessary court scheduling, case management, and operational adjustments to comply with these statutory court deadlines.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of General Services to place a veteran status notation on identification security cards for individuals who provide acceptable proof of veteran status, and allows applicants to consent to having their contact information shared with executive agencies regarding eligibility for veterans' benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Military veterans who are state employees, contractors, regulated lobbyists, media personnel, local government officials, or volunteers receiving identification cards from the Department of General Services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Department of General Services can implement the veteran status notation and manage information transmission using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local effect: No material effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency responsible for authorizing and issuing the veteran status notation on state identification cards, updating application forms to capture veteran status and contact consent, transmitting consented information to executive agencies, and potentially adopting regulations.

DVMF is explicitly named as an entity providing certifications of veteran status required for the ID card notation, and serves as a primary executive agency that can receive contact information of consented veterans to connect them with state and federal benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, and reduction facilities to notify and transfer unclaimed cremated, hydrolyzed, or soil remains of veterans or eligible dependents to the Department of Veterans and Military Families if a veterans service organization does not take possession of them within 10 days of notification, ensuring appropriate disposition and burial in a State veterans' cemetery.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Deceased veterans and their eligible dependents with unclaimed remains, licensed funeral establishments, crematory operators, natural organic reduction facilities, and veterans service organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (general and federal funds) for the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) may increase by an indeterminate but minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 for additional burials in State veterans' cemeteries. Costs for veterans are fully reimbursed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs through a $978 plot allowance, generating matching federal fund revenue. Costs for burying veterans' dependents are not reimbursed and must be covered by general funds (estimated illustratively at $5,000 annually for five dependents). Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 57 directly impacts the department by requiring licensed funeral establishments, crematories, and reduction facilities to notify and transfer unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, or eligible soil remains of veterans and their dependents to the department for final disposition and burial in State veterans' cemeteries, which also carries an operational and fiscal impact.

The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which regulates crematories and reduction facilities under the Business Regulation Article, the primary section of state law amended by this bill.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which licenses funeral establishments and crematories regulated under Title 7 of the Health Occupations Article amended by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes health occupations boards under the Maryland Department of Health to establish a process allowing applicants and licensees to include a notation indicating veteran status on their license, certificate, registration, or public profile, and to share relevant information with Executive Branch agencies to assist in determining eligibility for state and federal veterans benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Health Occupations Boards within the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Military veterans applying for or holding health occupation credentials in Maryland and Maryland health occupations boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate, likely minimal amount to the extent that health occupations boards opt to create the process (primarily for one-time licensing software and IT system updates, which are largely absorbable within existing resources). Revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the 20 health occupations boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health to establish processes for noting veteran status on licenses, certificates, registrations, and public profiles, and to transmit relevant applicant data to executive branch agencies.

The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status obtained from the Department of Veterans and Military Families and allows applicant information to be shared with executive branch agencies to determine eligibility for and connect veterans to state and federal benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Chesapeake Conservation Corps Program to be the Thomas V. Mike Miller, Jr., Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Chesapeake Bay Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteers and young adults participating in the corps, grant-recipient organizations, and communities served by environmental and climate projects.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Chesapeake Bay Trust is the primary entity that administers the Chesapeake Conservation Corps Program, which is renamed by this bill to the Thomas V. Mike Miller, Jr., Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department administers the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway under State Government Article § 21-206, which is specifically amended to reflect the renamed Corps Program when using pathway funds to expand service opportunities.

DNR oversees natural resources provisions and the Environmental Trust Fund in the Natural Resources Article, which transfers funds to the Chesapeake Bay Trust for the renamed Corps Program, and DNR provided information on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a distinct criminal misdemeanor offense for animal abuse or neglect that results in the death of a domestic animal or livestock, or the need to euthanize it based on the validated recommendation of two licensed veterinarians. The bill sets penalties of up to one year imprisonment and/or a fine up to $5,000, and allows courts to impose conditions of sentencing such as psychological counseling, restitution for care and euthanasia costs, and prohibitions on owning, possessing, or residing with animals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals accused or convicted of animal abuse or neglect, domestic animal and livestock owners, veterinarians, animal welfare organizations, and state and local law enforcement and correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $34,600 in FY 2025 for one-time programming costs for the Judiciary. General fund incarceration expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may also increase, while state general fund revenues will be minimally affected. Local revenues may increase from higher fines imposed in circuit courts, while local expenditures may rise due to longer incarceration terms in local detention centers and potential costs to compensate veterinarians for validating euthanasia decisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense and associated sentencing conditions for animal abuse resulting in death or euthanasia. The fiscal note identifies a direct fiscal impact of $34,558 in FY 2025 for one-time computer system programming costs for the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to one year of imprisonment, which the fiscal note notes may increase state incarceration expenditures for convictions arising in Baltimore City served at state-operated correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new criminal misdemeanor penalty punishable by up to one year in prison, impacting caseloads and representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants charged under the statute.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees animal health and livestock welfare in the state. The bill specifically establishes criminal penalties regarding abuse or neglect resulting in the death or euthanasia of livestock.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating and enforcing violations of state criminal law, including criminal animal cruelty and abuse statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment, in collaboration with its licensing boards, to establish a process allowing applicants for professional licenses or certificates to submit proof of veteran status, consent to a veteran notation on their credential, and consent to being contacted by Executive Branch agencies regarding eligibility for state and federal veterans' benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterans seeking or holding professional licenses and certificates from boards under the Maryland Department of the Environment (such as marine contractors, well drillers, and waterworks operators).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the necessary updates to forms and databases using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Department of the Environment and its licensing boards to establish a process to include a veteran status notation on professional licenses and certificates, collect documentation and consent, transmit information to executive branch agencies, and adopt related regulations.

The bill explicitly references veteran status certification obtained from the Department of Veterans and Military Families, and involves sharing veteran applicant information to assist with determining eligibility for state and federal veterans benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local boards of elections to include a written notice regarding requests for a State-approved absentee ballot application with mailed specimen ballots and any other mailings to voters or eligible voters to raise awareness of mail-in voting options, excluding voters who have permanent absentee ballot status, voters who have already received the notice for that election, or vote-by-mail elections.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local boards of elections and the Maryland State Board of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, eligible voters, and local election boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances, as the notice is sent alongside existing mailings such as specimen ballots.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Election Law Article regarding absentee ballot request notices sent by local election boards to eligible voters. The Maryland State Board of Elections oversees and administers election laws statewide, supervises local boards of elections, and approves the absentee ballot applications referenced in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that property damage resulting from a vessel accident on Maryland waters includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers, requiring the vessel operator or owner to report such accidents to the Department of Natural Resources within 10 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Vessel operators and owners on Maryland waters, boaters, and maritime navigation authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and it does not directly affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency under the State Boat Act. Operators or owners of vessels involved in boating accidents on State waters that result in specified property damage are required to file accident reports directly with the department.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted regarding potential judicial impacts of reporting mandates and violations under the Natural Resources Article, though boating accident reports themselves are not admissible as evidence in court proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local school board, including the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, to certify annually to the State Ethics Commission by October 1 that it complies with the Maryland Public Ethics Law regarding conflict of interest and financial disclosure provisions for board members and, if applicable, school system officials and employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school board members, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, and local school system officials and employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The State Ethics Commission and local school boards can handle the annual certification requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Ethics Commission by requiring each local school board to annually submit a compliance certification regarding ethics and financial disclosure provisions to the Commission by October 1.

The Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and 24 local school systems whose governing school boards are subjected to the annual ethics compliance certification requirement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes units within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process allowing applicants for occupational and professional licenses to request a veteran status notation on their license upon submitting proof of service, and to consent to having their contact information shared with Executive Branch agencies to determine eligibility for State and federal veterans' benefits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Military veterans applying for or renewing occupational and professional licenses in Maryland, and relevant State Executive Branch agencies such as the Department of Veterans and Military Families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally on a one-time basis by up to $12,000 as early as FY 2026 if units of MD Labor opt to establish the process and modify licensing systems. State revenues and local finances are not affected. Small business veteran licensees could experience minimal expenses if receiving a new license number necessitates updating vehicle markings and promotional materials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes licensing units within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process to include veteran status notations on professional and occupational licenses and transmit applicant contact information to appropriate executive branch agencies.

The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status issued by the Department of Veterans and Military Families and allows the department to receive contact information of consenting applicants to assist with determining eligibility for state and federal veterans' benefits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty resulting in bodily injury or death to immediately stop the vessel as close as possible to the scene to render assistance and provide identifying information, and establishes misdemeanor and felony penalties for failure to stop or render aid.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Vessel operators, boaters, and individuals involved in boating collisions or accidents on Maryland waters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, although criminal fines and periods of incarceration are established for violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article under the State Boat Act, governing vessel accident response, reporting requirements to the Department of Natural Resources, and enforcement overseen by the Natural Resources Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new misdemeanor and felony penalties carrying maximum prison sentences of up to 10 years, which could impact state correctional facilities and probation supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses with substantial terms of imprisonment, requiring legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants charged under these provisions.
The bill establishes new criminal offenses and penalties that will be tried and adjudicated within the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires that appointments made by the Governor to the State Board of Stationary Engineers be subject to the advice and consent of the Senate.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor, Maryland Senate, and Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Appointees and members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers, stationary engineers, and the boiler manufacturing and design industry.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The change is procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Stationary Engineers is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Secretary of Labor advises on board appointments.
The bill alters the Governor's appointment procedure for the State Board of Stationary Engineers by requiring the advice and consent of the Senate.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, processing, and submitting board appointments to the Senate for confirmation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory appointment and confirmation process for members of this state regulatory board.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends through fiscal year 2028 the requirements for the Comptroller to distribute $14 million annually from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund, and for the Governor to appropriate $14 million from the fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. It also transfers the staffing and appointment responsibilities for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development and authorizes compensation for certain tenant members of the task force.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development and Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction proceedings, legal aid organizations, landlords, and members of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million in FY 2028, offset by an identical $14.0 million increase in special fund revenues to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Special fund expenditures from the fund increase by $14.0 million in FY 2028 to provide funding to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. The Department of Housing and Community Development can absorb task force administrative and compensation costs using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the responsibility for staffing, designating the chair, and appointing members of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development, and authorizes the department to provide stipends or compensation to certain low-income tenant members.

The bill relieves the Office of the Attorney General of its statutory responsibilities to appoint members to and provide staff support for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force, transferring those functions to the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill extends the requirement that the Comptroller distribute $14,000,000 annually from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal 2028, and the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition, appointing authority, staffing, compensation provisions, and reporting requirements of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force.

The bill extends the statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $14,000,000 from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the State budget through fiscal 2028.

As the agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing state revenues and expenditures, DBM is impacted by the continuation of the $14,000,000 mandated annual appropriation and the corresponding reduction in general fund revenues through fiscal 2028.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The Judiciary has designated seats on the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force and was consulted regarding the operational impacts of eviction legal representation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the Maryland Department of Agriculture's statutory authority over the regulation, identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland cantaloupe growers, wholesalers, retailers, and consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances or operations. The Maryland Department of Agriculture does not currently inspect or regulate cantaloupes, as regulation and oversight are conducted at the federal level by the USDA and FDA.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly repeals Title 10, Subtitle 9 of the Agriculture Article, removing the Maryland Department of Agriculture's statutory authority over the identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces remaining statutory references to 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health' within the Health - General Article, renames the Mental Hygiene Community-Based Services Fund, and directs the Maryland Department of Health to update departmental regulations and public-facing electronic materials accordingly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, behavioral health service providers, and individuals seeking or receiving mental health services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures and regulatory updates can be absorbed within existing departmental resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions of the Health - General Article administered by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and explicitly mandates that MDH review its regulations, adopt conforming regulatory amendments replacing 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health' by July 1, 2027, and update all public-facing electronic materials.

The bill amends Section 24-1105(b) of the Health - General Article, which directs the Comptroller to transfer proceeds and investment earnings into the newly renamed Mental Health Community-Based Services Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the membership of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust from 11 to 12 members to include the Secretary of Disabilities, or the Secretary's designee, as an ex officio member.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Veterans Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland veterans, their families, and members of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Altering the composition of the Board of Trustees does not materially affect State or local government finances. The Secretary of Disabilities or their designee can serve on the Board with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust to add the Secretary of Disabilities (or their designee) as an ex officio member.
